question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Drive more slowly.,b:Drive more quickly.,c:Drive through deeper water.,d:Turn off traction control.
note: Hydroplaning is more likely at higher speeds on wet roads; slowing down helps tires channel water and maintain contact with the road.

question: How far ahead should you look while driving to maintain safe awareness?
options: a:About 10 to 15 seconds ahead.,b:Only 100 to 150 yards ahead.,c:One to two blocks only.,d:Directly in front of the hood at all times.
note: Scanning 10–15 seconds down the road helps you anticipate hazards and avoid last-second maneuvers.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, how should you steer?
options: a:Turn the wheel in the direction you want the vehicle to go.,b:Turn the wheel to keep the front wheels straight.,c:Turn the wheel opposite the direction of the skid.
note: If you skid, steer toward where you want the vehicle to go. When the car begins to straighten, correct steering to keep control.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out, what should you do with the steering and brakes?
options: a:Apply the brake and hold it.,b:Hold the steering wheel tightly and use the brakes lightly.,c:Pull over quickly.
note: Hold the steering wheel firmly to keep the vehicle straight, slow gradually by easing off the gas, and apply brakes lightly once the vehicle is under control.

question: Your vehicle's blind spot is the area:
options: a:You cannot see without turning your head.,b:Directly behind your vehicle only.,c:Visible in your rearview mirror.,d:Inside the car behind the passenger seat.
note: Blind spots are areas not visible in mirrors; check them by turning your head to look over your shoulder before changing lanes.

question: If you stop along the road at night, what lighting should you use?
options: a:Keep your low-beam headlights on and turn on emergency flashers.,b:Turn off all lights to conserve battery.,c:Use parking lights only.
note: If you stop at night, turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low-beam headlights on so other road users can see your vehicle.

question: What helps you avoid needing to make emergency stops in traffic?
options: a:Drive only in the right lane.,b:Look ahead and maintain a safe following distance.,c:Honk to make others aware of you.
note: Maintaining a safe following distance and scanning ahead allows you to react and avoid sudden emergency stops.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing from the right lane into the left on a multi-lane highway, what checks should you make?
options: a:Look over your left shoulder for traffic in your blind spot and check mirrors, then signal.,b:Look only in your side mirror and then change lanes.,c:Signal and look in your rearview mirror only.
note: Check mirrors and look over your left shoulder for vehicles in the blind spot; always signal before changing lanes.

question: Anything that requires you to which of the following could cause a crash?
options: a:Take your attention away from the task of driving.,b:Take your hands off the wheel only briefly.,c:Use your mirrors occasionally.
note: Any activity that diverts attention from driving, takes your eyes off the road, or your hands off the wheel is a dangerous distraction that can cause a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing on the left, when is it safe to return to the right lane?
options: a:When you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:After roughly three seconds.,c:When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
note: You may return to the right lane when the passed vehicle's front is visible in your rearview mirror; always signal before changing lanes.

question: Which type of roadway area tends to freeze first in cold weather?
options: a:Areas shaded by trees or buildings.,b:Flat open areas.,c:Roads in direct sunlight.
note: Shaded sections freeze sooner and stay icy longer because they get less sun and dry more slowly than exposed areas.

question: Faced with an oncoming car on your left and a bicyclist on your right, what should you do?
options: a:Pull onto the shoulder.,b:Split the difference.,c:Let the car pass and then pass the bike.
note: When multiple hazards exist, handle one at a time: allow the oncoming vehicle to pass before safely passing the bicyclist.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to turn left but oncoming traffic is heavy and the light is green, what is the appropriate action?
options: a:Use the next intersection.,b:Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.,c:Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
note: If the light is green and it is safe, you may enter the intersection to wait for a gap in oncoming traffic to complete your left turn; do not block the crosswalk.

question: When it starts to rain while you are driving, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down.,b:Drive at the posted maximum speed.,c:Drive faster than surrounding traffic to get through the rain quickly.
note: Reduce speed when rain begins, turn on headlights for visibility, and pull over if visibility becomes too poor to continue safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a multilane, one-way street onto another one-way or multilane roadway, from which lane should you begin the turn?
options: a:The left lane.,b:The middle of the intersection.,c:The right lane.
note: When turning left from multilane or one-way streets, begin the turn from the leftmost lane designated for left turns.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it ever legal to block an intersection?
options: a:If you entered the intersection on the green light.,b:During rush hour traffic.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: You may not enter an intersection unless you can fully clear it; blocking an intersection is unlawful even if the light is green when you enter.

question: If your wheels go off the pavement, what should you do?
options: a:Maintain speed and gently brake while driving with wheels off pavement, then steer back when safe.,b:Grip the wheel and sharply jerk back onto the pavement.,c:Brake hard immediately and stop.
note: If your vehicle leaves the pavement, reduce speed gently while staying straight; when safe, steer back onto the road. Do not make sudden, sharp turns to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.

question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline mean?
options: a:Slow down.,b:Pass with caution.,c:Do not pass.
note: A solid yellow line next to your lane means passing from your direction is prohibited; wait for a legal passing zone.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering the roadway from a driveway, what must you do?
options: a:Must stop and proceed only when there are no pedestrians or vehicles approaching.,b:Must drive slowly so approaching vehicles can get out of your way.,c:Must honk your horn to alert pedestrians and drivers.
note: Stop before entering the roadway from a driveway, yield to approaching vehicles and pedestrians, and proceed only when safe.

question: Why should you be cautious when passing a bicycle?
options: a:Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass the bike.,b:The bicycle always has the right-of-way.,c:You are moving slower than the bicycle.
note: Bicyclists may swerve to avoid hazards and oncoming traffic may not see you moving into its lane; give bicycles extra room.

question: On long highway trips, what helps prevent drowsiness?
options: a:Stopping at regular intervals to rest.,b:Turning up the radio.,c:Slowing down.
note: Schedule regular stops to rest and stretch to reduce drowsiness while driving long distances.

question: How must a driver respond to a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:Stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when safe.,b:Slow down and proceed without stopping.,c:Merge to the right and continue.
note: A flashing red light requires a full stop; yield to other road users and go only when it is safe.

question: If stopped at a railroad crossing with more than one track, when is it safe to proceed?
options: a:When you have a clear view of all tracks and there are no trains approaching.,b:As soon as one train passes on one track.,c:When the crossing lights stop flashing even if you cannot see down all tracks.
note: Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks before proceeding; another train may be approaching on a different track.

question: What does a single dashed yellow line between opposing lanes mean?
options: a:Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.,b:Both lanes travel in the same direction.,c:Drivers may not pass.
note: A single dashed yellow centerline indicates passing is allowed for vehicles in both directions when it is safe.

question: How does alcohol affect driving skills and judgment?
options: a:It harms both driving skills and judgment.,b:It helps driving skills but harms judgment.,c:It has no effect on either.
note: Alcohol impairs reaction time, vision, coordination, and judgment, making driving dangerous at any level of consumption.

question: What is 'highway hypnosis' most likely caused by?
options: a:Staring at the roadway for long periods of time.,b:Frequent rest stops.,c:Too much sleep the night before your trip.
note: Highway hypnosis occurs when you stare ahead for long periods and stop actively scanning; take breaks and stay mentally alert to avoid zoning out.

question: Two solid white lines across a lane mark what?
options: a:The boundaries of a crosswalk where pedestrians should be given the right-of-way.,b:That motor vehicles have priority over pedestrians.,c:That no one has the right-of-way.
note: Two solid white lines across a lane typically mark a crosswalk; drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks.

question: What is the effect of driving while distracted by activities such as phone use?
options: a:It usually causes the driver to react more slowly to hazards.,b:It typically improves driver awareness.,c:It causes drivers to drive faster intentionally.
note: Distracted driving slows reaction time and reduces the ability to perceive and respond to road hazards, increasing crash risk.

question: A vehicle is hydroplaning when what occurs?
options: a:Its tires lose contact with the road surface and the vehicle rides on water.,b:The windshield wipers cannot keep the windshield clear.,c:Spray from a large truck reduces visibility.
note: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on a layer of water, causing loss of steering and braking control.

question: On slippery roads, how should you adjust your following distance?
options: a:Increase your following distance (stay farther back).,b:Keep the same distance as normal.,c:Follow closer to the car ahead.
note: Slippery surfaces require longer stopping distances; maintain extra space between you and the vehicle ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your view to the side at an intersection is blocked, what is the correct procedure?
options: a:Stop, then inch forward until you can see clearly in both directions.,b:Slow down and look both ways without stopping.,c:Maintain speed and look both ways.
note: When sight lines are obstructed, stop and inch forward until you have a clear view before entering the intersection.

question: Which factor commonly contributes to traffic crashes?
options: a:Exceeding the posted speed limit and driving too fast for conditions.,b:Getting adequate rest and staying alert.,c:Careful scanning of the environment.
note: Driving too fast for posted speeds or conditions is a frequent cause of crashes; maintain appropriate speed for conditions.

question: When driving on major highways, what should you remember?
options: a:Stay alert and ready to react to hazards.,b:Keep your eyes fixed straight ahead to maintain concentration.,c:Avoid checking mirrors to reduce distraction.
note: Highway driving requires alertness and scanning to avoid highway hypnosis and to respond to unexpected hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended downward, what does that signal mean?
options: a:Turn left.,b:Stop.,c:Turn right.
note: A downward left-arm signal indicates the driver intends to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you begin to slow down for a highway exit?
options: a:After you have moved into the exit lane.,b:On the main road just before the exit lane.,c:Only when you see a toll booth.
note: Get into the exit lane well in advance and begin to slow down after you are fully in the exit lane, following any posted advisory speeds.

question: Which behavior describes a good defensive driver?
options: a:Drives slowly at all times.,b:Looks out for the actions of other drivers.,c:Travels at a constant speed.
note: A defensive driver anticipates other drivers' actions, scans the road for hazards, and plans safe reactions rather than relying solely on their own speed.

question: When must you yield to a pedestrian?
options: a:At all times when necessary to prevent hitting them, even if they ignore traffic laws.,b:Only in a marked crosswalk.,c:Only when traffic signals favor the pedestrian.,d:Only when a police officer is present.
note: Always do everything possible to avoid striking a pedestrian, regardless of whether they are obeying traffic laws.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach an intersection blocked by traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through completely.,b:Get as close as possible to the vehicle ahead so you can go next.,c:Enter the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.,d:Honk to move traffic along.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it without blocking cross traffic; wait until traffic ahead moves.

question: Which statement accurately describes alcohol's effect on driving?
options: a:Alcohol impairs judgment, which is essential for safe driving.,b:If you can walk in a straight line after drinking, it is safe to drive.,c:Being under the legal BAC limit guarantees unimpaired driving.
note: Alcohol reduces judgment, which is needed to perceive and react to road hazards. Even small amounts can affect driving ability.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on an interstate expressway, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and make a U-turn.,b:Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.,c:Roll down your window and ask the driver next to you for help.
note: Do not back up or make a U-turn on the highway. Continue to the next exit and safely return to the missed exit.

question: If a transit vehicle is signaling to reenter the main roadway after a stop, you must:
options: a:Hon k to let them reenter.,b:Move to the left lane immediately.,c:Yield and allow it to merge safely.
note: Yield to transit vehicles re-entering traffic after a stop by changing lanes or slowing as necessary to let them merge safely.

question: What does it mean when lanes are separated by double solid yellow lines?
options: a:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,b:Passing is allowed from either direction when safe.,c:You may pass from the left only.,d:You may cross the lines to make a U-turn anywhere.
note: Double solid yellow lines mark opposing traffic lanes; passing is prohibited for traffic in both directions.

question: When you see an approaching emergency vehicle using flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Maintain your speed and stay in your lane until the vehicle has passed.,b:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until the vehicle has passed.,c:Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until the vehicle has passed.
note: Pull over to the right edge of the road, stop, and remain stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed; on one-way streets move to the nearest edge.

question: When stopped on an uphill slope, why should you allow a larger space cushion in front of you?
options: a:At an intersection.,b:On an incline, to allow for a vehicle ahead that may roll back.,c:At a stop sign.
note: Allow more space when stopped on an uphill grade because the vehicle ahead may roll backward when traffic starts moving.

question: What do two solid yellow lines in the center of the road mean?
options: a:Passing is not allowed for traffic in either direction.,b:Passing is allowed for drivers in both directions.,c:Passing is allowed only when going downhill.
note: Two solid yellow centerlines indicate opposite-direction traffic and prohibit passing from either side.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the maximum speed limit in a school zone where children or crossing guards are present?
options: a:10 mph,b:15 mph,c:20 mph
note: Unless signs indicate otherwise, the maximum speed limit in a school zone with children or crossing guards present is 15 mph.

question: What is the only effective method to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Drink coffee.,b:Exercise.,c:Allow your body time to get rid of the alcohol.
note: Only time allows your body to metabolize alcohol; coffee, exercise, and other remedies do not reduce BAC.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to change lanes, what should you check?
options: a:Rearview mirror and side mirror, then glance quickly over your shoulder for blind spots.,b:Only the side view mirror.,c:Only the inside mirror.,d:Nothing; trust other drivers to avoid you.
note: Check mirrors for approaching traffic, then look over your shoulder just before changing lanes to ensure it is clear.

question: While driving in fog or other low-visibility conditions, what should you do about headlights?
options: a:Slow down and use your low beam headlights.,b:Turn on your high beams to see further.,c:Increase speed to clear the area quickly.
note: Use low beams in fog; high beams will reflect off moisture and reduce visibility. If visibility is too poor, pull off the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles enter an intersection from different highways at the same time, which vehicle must yield?
options: a:The vehicle on the left.,b:Either one.,c:The vehicle on the right.
note: When two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and remain in your vehicle if possible.,b:Get out of the vehicle and stand near the rear to warn approaching cars.,c:Flag down the first vehicle that passes for assistance.
note: If you can, move off the traveled portion of the roadway, turn on hazards, and stay in the vehicle; walking along the roadway is dangerous.

question: When must you stop for a school bus on a two-lane highway?
options: a:Only if it is stopped in your lane and you are traveling in the same direction.,b:When the bus is parked on the shoulder and has no students.,c:If you and the bus are on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
note: On two-lane highways, traffic from both directions must stop when a school bus is stopped and its red warning lights are flashing or the stop arm is extended.

question: On wet pavement, which should you keep in mind?
options: a:Give extra stopping distance than usual.,b:Wet roads increase the chance of hydroplaning.,c:Road surfaces are most slippery just after rain begins.
note: Wet roads often have a film of oil and dirt that makes traction poor, especially just after rain starts; slow down in heavy rain, standing water, or slush to reduce loss of control.

question: What can happen to bicyclists who disobey traffic laws?
options: a:They can be ticketed.,b:They are exempt from traffic laws.,c:They always get a warning instead of a ticket.
note: Bicyclists have the same duties and responsibilities as motor vehicle drivers and can receive citations for violations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you drive faster than other vehicles on a two-lane road and keep passing, what is likely to happen?
options: a:Get you to your destination much more quickly and safely.,b:Increase your chances of a collision.,c:Help prevent traffic congestion.
note: Passing repeatedly on two-lane roads increases the risk of collision each time you pass; avoid unnecessary passing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering an interstate highway, what should you generally do?
options: a:Stop, check for cars, then enter when safe.,b:Check for cars, increase speed to match traffic, and merge when clear.,c:Check for cars and reduce speed to 25 mph before entering.
note: Use the acceleration lane to reach highway speeds and merge into traffic smoothly when there is a safe gap.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may proceed through an intersection with a yellow light under which circumstance?
options: a:There is an emergency vehicle crossing your lane.,b:You are turning right.,c:There are pedestrians crossing.
note: If you are already completing a lawful turn when the light is yellow, proceed carefully. Otherwise, slow and stop if safe.

question: What color are construction and maintenance temporary signs and markings?
options: a:Orange background with black writing.,b:Red background with green writing.,c:Yellow background with blue writing.,d:Blue background with white writing.
note: Temporary signs in work zones have orange backgrounds with black letters or symbols to warn drivers of construction activity.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop and wait for a green light.,c:Stop and look for other vehicles, then go if there is no traffic.
note: A flashing yellow light tells drivers to slow down and proceed carefully, watching for cross traffic and hazards.

question: If pedestrians cross illegally in the middle of the street, what must you do?
options: a:Yield and stop for them.,b:Do not stop for them.,c:Sound your horn and continue.
note: You must yield to pedestrians at all times, even if they are not in a crosswalk.

question: On a road without sidewalks, where should pedestrians walk?
options: a:Side of the road which has the lightest traffic.,b:Same side of the road on which traffic is moving.,c:Side of the road facing oncoming traffic.
note: Pedestrians should walk on the side of the road facing oncoming traffic so they can see approaching vehicles and react.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on a freeway, you should not:
options: a:Back up on the road or shoulder.,b:Proceed to the next exit, leave the freeway, and return to your proper exit.,c:Continue on the freeway and find an alternate route to your destination.
note: Never back up on the shoulder or travel lane if you miss an exit. Continue to the next exit and re-route from there.

question: Which behavior may indicate an aggressive driver?
options: a:Erratic and improper lane changes.,b:Having many passengers.,c:Driving consistently under the speed limit.,d:Using cruise control.
note: Aggressive drivers often make sudden or improper lane changes; avoid confrontation and get out of their way.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, what is the best initial action?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of the traffic lane.,b:Pump the brakes rapidly.,c:Brake hard and steer immediately to the right edge of the roadway.
note: If a tire blows out, keep a firm grip on the wheel, ease off the accelerator, and slow down gradually before steering to safety. Avoid sudden braking or turning.

question: If your accelerator becomes stuck while driving, what should you do first?
options: a:Shift into neutral and apply steady pressure on the brake.,b:Reach down and attempt to lift the accelerator with your hand.,c:Shift into park immediately.
note: If the accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road, shift to neutral, apply steady braking, pull off the road when safe, and then turn off the engine.

question: What does a diamond-shaped traffic sign indicate?
options: a:Alerts drivers to public recreation areas.,b:Alerts drivers to school zones.,c:Warns of existing or possible hazards.
note: Diamond-shaped signs, typically yellow or orange, warn drivers of special conditions or potential hazards ahead.

question: How often should you check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you?
options: a:Every two to four seconds.,b:Every four to six seconds.,c:Every six to eight seconds.
note: You should glance at your rearview mirror roughly every six to eight seconds to monitor traffic behind you.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim headlights, where should you look?
options: a:Look toward the center of the roadway.,b:Look toward the right side of the road.,c:Look straight ahead.
note: Look toward the right edge of the road to avoid being blinded and to maintain enough visibility to steer safely.

question: Is it legal to drink alcoholic beverages in a vehicle on a public highway?
options: a:No; possessing or consuming alcohol on public roads is prohibited.,b:Yes, as long as you are not driving.,c:Yes, if you are in the back of a pickup.,d:Yes, if you are over 21.
note: It is illegal to possess or consume an alcoholic beverage on public roads; open container laws prohibit having open alcohol where driver or passengers sit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you approach an intersection and the light turns from green to yellow, what is the best action?
options: a:Be prepared to stop; stop if you can do so safely.,b:Speed up to beat the red.,c:Come to a stop in the center of the intersection.
note: A steady yellow warns of an upcoming red; slow and stop if safe, otherwise proceed through cautiously.

question: In which situations should you reduce your speed?
options: a:On narrow or winding roads.,b:At intersections or railroad crossings.,c:When the road is wet or slippery.,d:All of the above
note: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, near intersections and railroad crossings, and whenever the road is wet, slippery, or visibility is reduced.

question: A blood alcohol concentration increase of 0.02 percent results in what change to crash risk?
options: a:It nearly doubles a driver's chance of being in a fatal crash.,b:It has no measurable effect.,c:It halves the crash risk.,d:It makes driving safer.
note: Even small increases in BAC significantly increase the risk of a fatal crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it permissible to cross solid yellow centerlines?
options: a:Only when you are making a turn.,b:Any time you want to pass.,c:During daylight hours only.
note: Solid yellow lines should not be crossed except when making lawful turns where allowed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parallel parking between two vehicles, what should you do first?
options: a:Pull up even with the car in front of the parking space, then begin backing in.,b:Turn your wheels to the left immediately.,c:Turn your wheels to the right immediately.
note: After finding a space and signaling, stop parallel to the vehicle ahead of the spot before beginning the backing maneuver.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who moves first?
options: a:All drivers who got there before you.,b:The driver on your right, regardless of who got there first.,c:The driver on your left, regardless of who got there first.
note: At a four-way stop, the vehicle that arrives first goes first; if two arrive together, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the default maximum speed limit in outlying parts of cities and villages when no speed is posted?
options: a:35 mph.,b:25 mph.,c:45 mph.
note: Unless posted otherwise, the default speed limit in outlying parts of cities and villages is 35 mph.

question: If poor weather reduces visibility, what should you do about following distance?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Speed up to get off the road sooner.,c:Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
note: When visibility is reduced by weather or darkness, increase following distance to give yourself more time to react.

question: When must drivers yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk?
options: a:Only if the pedestrians first wave to the driver.,b:Only if the pedestrians are not texting while walking.,c:At all times.
note: You must stop for and yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk. Proceed only when the crosswalk is clear and it is safe.

question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?
options: a:Avoid sudden stops by releasing the gas early and braking smoothly.,b:Brake abruptly to get attention.,c:Check mirrors only after stopping.
note: To reduce the chance of being hit from behind, release the accelerator to slow and then apply steady braking so your brake lights warn drivers behind you.

question: A solid white edge line that slants toward the left indicates what about the road ahead?
options: a:The road becomes narrower ahead.,b:There is an intersection just ahead.,c:You will be required to turn left ahead.
note: An edge line angling toward the center of the road indicates the roadway narrows ahead; reduce speed and be prepared for the change.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to change lanes, which actions are important?
options: a:Signal in advance, check your blind spot, and verify the lane is clear.,b:Only signal at the last second.,c:Change lanes quickly without checking mirrors.
note: Always signal, check mirrors and blind spots, and ensure the target lane is clear before changing lanes.

question: When are streets and highways most slippery?
options: a:When it has been raining hard for several hours.,b:Just after it starts to rain.,c:When they are clean and dry.
note: Roads are often most slippery just after rain begins because water mixes with oil and other residues on the surface that have not yet been washed away.

question: When driving at night, what is a key safety action?
options: a:Always use your high beams.,b:Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: Night driving reduces visibility and depth perception; increase your following distance and use appropriate headlights (low beam when others are present).

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while you're driving, what should you do?
options: a:Keep driving normally.,b:Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow to a stop.,c:Slam on your brakes.
note: If a tire blows out, grip the wheel, steer to keep your lane, release the accelerator to slow, then brake lightly once you are moving slowly and pull off the road to a safe area.

question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?
options: a:Railroad crossings.,b:School zones.,c:No passing zones.
note: A crossbuck indicates a railroad crossing; drivers must yield to trains and never try to beat a train across the tracks.

question: What usually causes hydroplaning?
options: a:Driving too fast on a wet road so tires cannot clear water.,b:Excessive stops.,c:Sudden stops.
note: Hydroplaning occurs when tires cannot channel water away at higher speeds, causing loss of traction and control.

question: When following another vehicle, you should allow extra space behind which type of vehicle?
options: a:Passenger vehicle.,b:Station wagon.,c:Motorcycle.
note: Give extra following distance for motorcycles; they can stop more quickly and are harder to see, especially at night.

question: When preparing to exit an interstate, when is the proper time to begin slowing down?
options: a:About halfway through the deceleration lane.,b:Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.,c:As you approach the deceleration lane.
note: Keep highway speed until you enter the deceleration lane, then slow to the advisory speed posted for the exit ramp.

question: What does a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line mean for drivers?
options: a:Drivers next to the broken line may pass; drivers next to the solid line may not.,b:Driving in both directions may pass.,c:Drivers next to the solid line may pass.
note: When your lane is next to the broken yellow line, you may pass; if your lane is beside the solid line, you may not pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you and a driver on your left reach a four-way stop at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle to your right has the right-of-way (you go before the driver on your left).,b:The driver on your left has the right-of-way.,c:Whoever is signaling to make a turn has the right-of-way.
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously at a stop, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

question: If you are about to be hit from the rear, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Releasing your seat belt.,b:Bracing yourself and pressing your head against the head restraint.,c:Keeping a firm grip on the steering wheel.
note: Do not release your seat belt; brace back against the seat and head restraint to reduce injury risk.

question: Which category of drug best describes alcohol?
options: a:A depressant.,b:An antihistamine.,c:A stimulant.
note: Alcohol is a depressant which slows central nervous system functions and impairs driving skills and judgment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about driving speed is correct?
options: a:As your speed increases, the chance of a fatality increases, and you should increase following distance.,b:As your speed increases, so should your following distance only.,c:Your speed does not affect stopping distance.
note: Higher speeds increase stopping distance and the likelihood that a crash will be fatal; increase following distance as speed increases.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what condition may you legally pass another vehicle on the right?
options: a:If the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available lane to pass on the right.,b:Even if it means driving off the pavement.,c:On a narrow bridge.
note: You may pass on the right when a vehicle is turning left and a safe passing lane is available, but never by leaving the paved road.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing that has no flashing lights or gates, what should you be prepared to do?
options: a:Cross immediately and quickly.,b:Always stop before crossing.,c:Yield to a train and only proceed when the entire vehicle can clear the tracks.
note: At crossings without active signals, be prepared to yield to trains and never enter unless you have room to clear the tracks; avoid shifting gears while crossing.

question: What best ensures safety when you intend to back up a vehicle?
options: a:Check your rearview mirrors to see what is behind you.,b:Check behind the vehicle before you get into the driver's seat.,c:Honk your horn right before shifting into reverse.
note: Before getting into the car to reverse, walk behind it and check for children, pets, or obstacles that may be out of view.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a roadway from a private road or driveway, what should you do?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians and traffic already on the roadway.,b:Blow your horn to warn oncoming traffic.,c:Pull partially onto the roadway to check for traffic.,d:Enter quickly to merge smoothly.
note: You must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway when entering from a private road or driveway.

question: What does a single broken white line between lanes indicate?
options: a:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction; you may change lanes or pass when it is safe to do so.

question: What is the safest way to prevent hydroplaning in wet weather?
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Put on cruise control.,c:Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts to rain.
note: Lowering speed reduces the risk of hydroplaning; avoid cruise control on wet roads.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it appropriate to drive at the posted maximum speed limit?
options: a:Only under ideal driving conditions.,b:During the day.,c:Only at night.
note: The posted maximum speed is the legal maximum under ideal conditions. Adjust your speed lower when conditions are not perfect.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic is passing you on both sides while you are in the center lane of an expressway, what is the appropriate action?
options: a:Move to the lane on your right.,b:Stay in the center lane.,c:Move to the lane on your left.
note: On multi-lane roads, drive in the right lanes unless passing or preparing for a left turn. If traffic is passing on both sides, move right when safe.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your vision.,b:When exiting an expressway.,c:When following a motorcycle closely in good conditions.
note: Increase following distance when visibility is reduced (e.g., behind large vehicles), in bad weather, or when behind motorcycles or bicycles.

question: Collisions are more likely to occur under which condition?
options: a:All vehicles are traveling at about the same speed.,b:One lane of traffic is traveling faster than the other lanes.,c:One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.
note: A vehicle moving significantly faster or slower than surrounding traffic increases the chance of collisions; match the flow of traffic when safe.

question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights of an emergency vehicle, you must:
options: a:Drive to the right side of the road and stop.,b:Slow down but remain in your lane.,c:Signal the emergency vehicle to pass.,d:Speed up and clear the area.
note: Yield immediately to emergency vehicles using lights or sirens by pulling to the right and stopping until they pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle, what is the proper response?
options: a:Drive as far to the right as safely possible and stop.,b:Stop immediately in the lane you are in.,c:Proceed slowly and allow it to pass without pulling over.
note: On a two-lane road, immediately move as near as possible to the right side and stop to allow the emergency vehicle to pass, avoiding stopping in an intersection.

question: What is a “No zone” around large vehicles?
options: a:A one-way traffic area.,b:A designated no-passing zone.,c:The blind spot of a large vehicle.
note: No zones are the large blind spots around trucks and other large vehicles. Avoid lingering in these areas where the driver cannot see you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a red light, when may you turn right?
options: a:When the cross traffic has cleared.,b:After you stop.,c:Both of the above.
note: Unless a sign forbids it, you may turn right on red after coming to a complete stop and yielding to traffic, pedestrians, and bicyclists.

question: There is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane ahead. What must you do?
options: a:Make eye contact with and then pass the pedestrian.,b:Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.,c:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing the street.
note: Even when there is no marked crosswalk you must yield to pedestrians crossing your lane and allow them to finish crossing safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach an intersection at the posted speed and the signal turns yellow, what should you do?
options: a:Stop before entering if you can do so safely; otherwise proceed through carefully.,b:Speed up to cross before red.,c:Cross the intersection without caution.
note: A steady yellow warns of an upcoming red; stop if it's safe, otherwise clear the intersection with caution.

question: When checking the blind spot to change lanes left, you should glance:
options: a:Over your left shoulder.,b:Only at your side mirror.,c:Over your right shoulder.
note: To check the blind spot for a left lane change, briefly look over your left shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

question: If an oncoming car's headlights are very bright at night, what should you do?
options: a:Glance toward the right edge of your lane.,b:Stop until the car passes.,c:Look directly below their headlights.
note: To avoid being blinded, don't stare at oncoming headlights; glance toward the right edge of the road until the vehicle passes.

question: Does drinking coffee after consuming alcohol lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:No — it has no effect on BAC.,b:Yes — it decreases BAC.,c:Yes — it cancels alcohol's effects.
note: Coffee may make you feel more awake but does not reduce the amount of alcohol in your bloodstream or your impairment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic light turns green, what must you still yield to?
options: a:Other vehicles only.,b:Pedestrians and any traffic already in the intersection.,c:No one; you have the right-of-way.
note: A green light means you may go, but you must yield to pedestrians and any traffic still in the intersection.

question: If you are about to be struck from the rear, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Letting go of the steering wheel.,b:Applying your brakes.,c:Pressing your head firmly against the head restraint.
note: If hit from the rear, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, brace your body against the seatback and head restraint to reduce whiplash, and be prepared to brake.

question: When should you allow extra following distance behind a vehicle?
options: a:Your car is cold.,b:There are no vehicles behind you.,c:You are following a motorcycle.
note: Motorcycles can fall or be less visible; allow extra space when following them so you can react safely if the rider loses control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Whose instructions must drivers obey at a construction site?
options: a:Security guards patrolling parking lots.,b:Other drivers whose vehicles are broken down on the roadway.,c:Flaggers (signal persons) at construction sites.
note: Drivers must obey directions from flaggers and other authorized traffic control personnel at work zones for everyone’s safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach an emergency vehicle stopped with flashing lights on the roadside, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and, if possible, change lanes to avoid driving next to the stopped vehicle.,b:Drive to the right side of the road and stop immediately.,c:Continue at the same speed in your lane.
note: When an emergency, tow, or roadside assistance vehicle is stopped with flashing lights, move over a lane if safe; if you cannot change lanes, slow to a safe speed below the limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes or passing, you should:
options: a:Signal your intention and check mirrors and blind spots (all of the above).,b:Signal only after you begin the lane change.,c:Change lanes without checking mirrors if you can see enough.
note: Always signal, check mirrors, and look over your shoulder to verify the blind spot is clear before changing lanes or passing.

question: How can you ensure your physical condition won't make driving unsafe?
options: a:Know the effects of any medicine on your driving ability and drive within your limitations.,b:Always drive faster to stay alert.,c:Skip regular health checks.,d:Drive only at night.
note: Be aware of medical conditions and medication effects; drive only when physically fit and within your limits.

question: Which of the following will lower blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Drinking caffeine,b:Eating foods high in fat,c:Time
note: Only time allows the body to eliminate alcohol and reduce BAC; other remedies do not speed up this process.

question: What are blind spots?
options: a:Areas you cannot see using a vehicle’s mirrors.,b:Spots in your vision when you become fatigued.,c:Traffic control devices that block your view.
note: Blind spots are areas near the rear corners of your vehicle that are not visible in mirrors; always check over your shoulder before changing lanes.

question: To be able to turn quickly and safely, how should you position your hands on the steering wheel?
options: a:On opposite sides of the wheel (e.g., 9 and 3 o'clock or 8 and 4 o'clock).,b:Next to each other on the top of the wheel.,c:On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.
note: Place both hands on opposite sides of the wheel to maintain control and make quick, safe steering inputs.

question: If a driver behind you wants to pass, how should you respond?
options: a:Slow down to allow room for the passing maneuver.,b:Speed up to prevent the pass.,c:Maintain the same speed.
note: When another driver wants to pass, reduce speed slightly to create space in front of your vehicle so the pass can be completed safely.

question: When approaching a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog, you should:
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop; yield the right-of-way.,b:Proceed normally because the pedestrian will hear you.,c:Take the right-of-way so you don't block traffic.,d:Sound your horn to alert them.
note: Drivers must yield to blind pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog; slow and stop as needed to avoid danger.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parallel parking facing downhill, how should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels away from the curb.,b:Turn your wheels sharply toward the side of the road.,c:Keep your wheels straight.
note: When parked downhill, turn your front wheels toward the curb or edge of the road so the vehicle will roll toward the curb if it moves.

question: Coming to a complete stop and yielding to cross traffic and pedestrians corresponds with which type of signal?
options: a:A solid red light.,b:A flashing yellow light.,c:A flashing red light.
note: A flashing red traffic signal is treated like a stop sign: stop completely, yield, and go when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady green traffic light allow you to do?
options: a:Proceed through the intersection if the way is clear.,b:Stop and check for cross traffic before moving.,c:Always yield to all traffic even if the light is green.
note: A steady green light means you may drive through the intersection when it is safe; you may also turn unless a sign prohibits it, yielding as required.

question: Which statement about using feet to operate pedals is correct?
options: a:Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.,b:Use your left foot to brake.,c:Always brake abruptly to ensure stopping.
note: Use your right foot for both the gas and brake to maintain smooth, controlled pedal application.

question: What is important to know about large trucks?
options: a:They have large blind spots and need more room to maneuver and stop.,b:They can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.,c:They need less room to maneuver than passenger vehicles.
note: Large trucks have substantial blind spots and require more distance to maneuver and stop than smaller vehicles.

question: A pentagon-shaped traffic sign indicates:
options: a:A school zone or school crossing.,b:A stop requirement.,c:A regulatory speed sign.,d:A yield ahead warning.
note: Five-sided signs identify school zones and school crossings; they warn you to be alert for children.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Large trucks tend to slow down under which condition?
options: a:When climbing long or steep hills.,b:When driving through long, gradual curves.,c:When descending long, gradual hills.
note: Because heavy trucks take longer to accelerate, they often lose speed going up long or steep inclines. Allow extra space when following trucks on hills.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When traffic is moving at 50–55 mph, when are you least likely to have an accident?
options: a:If you stay within the same speed range as most other vehicles.,b:If you drive a few miles per hour faster than others.,c:If you drive much slower than other traffic.,d:If you drive in the leftmost lane only.
note: Adjust your speed to flow with other traffic (within legal limits); collisions are less likely when vehicles move at similar speeds.

question: If other drivers around you are acting angrily, what should you do?
options: a:Distance yourself from them and avoid eye contact or gestures.,b:React with similar gestures to defend yourself.,c:Confront them to resolve the issue.
note: Mentally and physically distance yourself from aggressive drivers; do not engage or escalate the situation.

question: What does a diamond-shaped sign indicate?
options: a:Yield.,b:Stop.,c:Warning.
note: Diamond-shaped signs warn of hazards or special conditions ahead and are usually yellow or orange.

question: How can you keep track of traffic behind you?
options: a:Frequently check your rearview mirror.,b:Turn and look out your back window for long periods.,c:Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots at all times.
note: Regularly scanning your rearview mirror helps you stay aware of approaching traffic and changing conditions behind you.

question: As your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) increases, how are you affected?
options: a:You become more intoxicated and impaired.,b:You become more coordinated.,c:You become more sober.
note: Higher BAC causes greater impairment of judgment, coordination, and reaction time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a two-lane road with traffic in opposite directions, when should you return to your lane?
options: a:Return to the driving lane when there's enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.,b:Remain in the left lane if you intend to turn left.,c:Return to the right side of the roadway immediately.
note: After passing, return to your lane only when you can see the passed vehicle’s front bumper in your rearview mirror and there is adequate space.

question: If you are under 18, which is required to get a probationary license?
options: a:Hold an instruction permit for at least six months.,b:Be free of moving violations for the prior six months.,c:Complete an approved driver education course.
note: To qualify for a probationary license an under-18 applicant must complete approved driver education, hold an instruction permit at least six months, complete 30 hours of supervised driving (10 at night), have no moving convictions in the prior six months, pass a driving test, and pay fees.

question: What does a 'No passing zone' sign tell drivers?
options: a:To speed up slightly.,b:That it is not safe to pass.,c:To maintain a steady speed.
note: A 'No passing zone' sign indicates that passing is illegal and unsafe in the area where the sign is posted due to limited visibility or other hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you face a green light but pedestrians are in the intersection, what must you do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.,b:Proceed because you have the right-of-way.,c:Sound your horn to make pedestrians move.
note: Even on a green light, yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection; yield when turning on a steady green signal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is a U-turn prohibited?
options: a:On or near any curve or hill where you cannot be seen by oncoming traffic.,b:In a parking lot.,c:On a straight roadway with clear view for 500 feet both directions.
note: Do not make U-turns on or near curves or hills where visibility of oncoming traffic is limited—this can cause collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady yellow traffic light indicate?
options: a:Slow down and prepare to stop because the light will soon turn red.,b:Go immediately.,c:Yield to other cars only.
note: A steady yellow warns that the light is changing to red; slow and prepare to stop unless you are already too close to stop safely.

question: At dawn, dusk, or in precipitation, what should you do to be more visible to others?
options: a:Turn on your headlights (low beams).,b:Use parking lights.,c:Turn up the instrument panel lights.
note: Use your headlights (low beams) when visibility is reduced or when windshield wipers are needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you respond to a flashing yellow traffic signal at an intersection?
options: a:Slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution.,b:Stop before crossing the intersection.,c:Wait for a green light before going.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down, be alert, and proceed with caution while watching for pedestrians and cross traffic.

question: When is it legal to drive around or under a lowered railroad crossing gate?
options: a:Never.,b:When you can clearly see both directions.,c:When the warning lights are not flashing.
note: Do not go around or under any lowered railroad crossing gate under any circumstance; wait until gates are fully raised and it is safe to proceed.

question: On roadways, bicycles are legally considered what?
options: a:Vehicles subject to the same rules as motor vehicles.,b:Hazards that must yield to cars.,c:Objects that are not covered by traffic laws.
note: Bicycles on roadways are treated as vehicles; bicyclists and motorists must follow the same traffic laws.

question: Guide signs that provide directions and mileage are normally what color?
options: a:Green.,b:Yellow.,c:Red.
note: Guide or destination signs are green with white lettering and give directional and distance information.

question: What is the only medically proven method of removing alcohol or drug effects from your system?
options: a:Breathe in some fresh air.,b:Give your body time.,c:Drink coffee.
note: The only proven way to reduce alcohol or many drug effects in your body is to allow time for metabolism and elimination.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Within an intersection where there are no oncoming vehicles,b:Wherever signs and/or pavement markings permit passing,c:Within a curve where there are no oncoming vehicles
note: You may pass only where pavement markings and signs allow and where you have a clear view of the road ahead; never pass at intersections or on curves with limited visibility.

question: Approximately how far might it take a fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling 55 mph to stop?
options: a:Up to 400 feet.,b:About 50 feet.,c:About 125 feet.
note: Large trucks require much longer stopping distances; a loaded tractor-trailer at 55 mph can take nearly 400 feet to stop.

question: A single broken yellow centerline on a two-lane road indicates what?
options: a:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.,b:Lanes move in the same direction and passing is not allowed.,c:Drivers are not permitted to pass in either direction.
note: Broken yellow lines separate opposing traffic and mean passing is permitted for drivers next to the broken line when safe.

question: What action must you take when you approach an octagonal traffic sign?
options: a:Stop.,b:Slow down but keep moving.,c:Turn immediately.
note: An octagonal sign always means Stop. Come to a complete stop, yield to others as required, and proceed when safe.

question: How can you prevent becoming an aggressive driver?
options: a:Relax, focus on driving, and be realistic about travel time.,b:Tailgate slower drivers to pressure them.,c:Drive above the posted speed limit to get ahead.
note: Manage frustration, plan adequate time, obey speed limits, and concentrate on safe driving to avoid aggression.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim high beams, where should you look to avoid glare?
options: a:Toward the right edge of your lane.,b:Directly at the headlights.,c:Toward the left edge of your lane.
note: When an oncoming vehicle has high beams, avert your eyes toward the right edge of your lane and use peripheral vision to maintain lane position.

question: Which behavior describes defensive driving?
options: a:Keep your eyes moving to look for possible hazards.,b:Look only at the car directly in front of you.,c:Put one car length between you and the car ahead.
note: Defensive driving requires constantly scanning and looking well ahead to spot hazards early.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to return to the right lane?
options: a:When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:About three seconds after passing.,c:When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.,d:Whenever you feel comfortable.
note: Only move back into your lane when you can clearly see the passed vehicle's front in your rearview mirror and after checking blind spots.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Straight ahead,b:Right, toward the side of the road,c:Left, toward the center of the road
note: When parked downhill with or without a curb, turn wheels toward the edge of the road so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if the brakes fail.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with no warning signals, you should:
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,b:Always come to a complete stop whether a train is visible or not.,c:Assume a crossing will have signals.
note: At an unsignaled crossing, reduce speed, look and listen for trains, and stop if any are approaching.

question: How does the type of alcoholic beverage affect impairment?
options: a:The type of alcohol (beer vs. wine) does not change impairment; the amount consumed does.,b:Beer impairs less than wine.,c:Hard ciders and mixed drinks always cause the most impairment.
note: Impairment depends on the amount of alcohol in the bloodstream, not the specific beverage type. All alcoholic drinks can impair reflexes and judgment.

question: If pedestrians are in a crosswalk ahead, what must you do?
options: a:Stop and wait for them to finish crossing.,b:Proceed; drivers have the right-of-way.,c:Drive around them on the right if safe.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and wait until it is safe to proceed.

question: What best describes distracted driving?
options: a:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.,b:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,c:Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.
note: Distracted driving includes any activity that takes your eyes, hands, or mind away from driving and is a leading cause of collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a pedestrian is in the middle of the street when your light turns green, what should you do?
options: a:Wait until the pedestrian has finished crossing before proceeding.,b:Proceed if you have the right-of-way.,c:Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.,d:Honk to hurry the pedestrian along.
note: Even with a green light, you must yield to pedestrians already in the crosswalk and allow them to finish crossing safely.

question: On a vertically arranged traffic light, what is the top-to-bottom order of the lights?
options: a:Red, yellow, green.,b:Red, green, yellow.,c:Green, red, yellow.
note: On vertical signals the top light is red, the middle yellow, and the bottom green. On horizontal signals, red is on the left and green on the right.

question: Before switching on the ignition, what safety checks should you make?
options: a:Buckle your safety belt.,b:Be sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.,c:Both of the above.
note: Develop a routine: before starting the engine, buckle your seat belt and ensure all passengers are belted as well.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an emergency vehicle using flashing lights approaches while you are on a one-way street, you must:
options: a:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.,b:Drive with your flashers turned on.,c:Speed up to reach the nearest exit.
note: On a one-way street, move toward the nearest side of the road and stop to allow emergency vehicles to pass.

question: When you take any medication, what should you do regarding driving?
options: a:Consult your doctor or pharmacist about effects before driving.,b:Drive the same as always because medications usually have no effect.,c:Keep your window open and drive more slowly.
note: Both prescription and over-the-counter medicines can impair driving. Ask a healthcare professional whether the medicine affects driving ability.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing warning sign, what should you be ready to do?
options: a:Look for a way around any lowered gates.,b:Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.,c:Drive faster than the train to clear the crossing.
note: Railroad crossing warning signs indicate a possible train ahead; be prepared to stop and obey all crossing signals and barriers.

question: If the rear of your car begins skidding to the left, what is the correct steering action?
options: a:Steer to the right.,b:Steer to the left.,c:Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral.
note: If the rear skids left, steer left (in the direction you want to go) to realign the vehicle; avoid braking abruptly.

question: A steady yellow traffic signal warns that which light will soon appear?
options: a:Steady red.,b:Flashing yellow.,c:Steady green.
note: A steady yellow means the signal is about to change to steady red; slow down and prepare to stop unless you are too close to stop safely.

question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:
options: a:Follow the flagger's directions.,b:Copy what surrounding traffic is doing despite the flagger's instructions.,c:Assume the flagger is not supposed to be directing traffic.
note: Flaggers control traffic in work zones for safety; obey their signals and directions.

question: Why should drivers give extra space to children on bicycles?
options: a:They have less developed reflexes and are smaller and harder to see.,b:They always follow traffic laws.,c:They can stop more quickly than adults.,d:They always use bike lanes.
note: Children are less predictable and harder to see; watch carefully near schools, parks, and playgrounds and be prepared for sudden movements.

question: Which statement about large trucks is true?
options: a:They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.,b:They all have air brakes that allow them to stop quickly.,c:They are more maneuverable than passenger vehicles.
note: Large trucks require much greater stopping distances than smaller passenger vehicles, especially when fully loaded.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should drivers on a freeway make space for vehicles entering from an on-ramp?
options: a:Maintain speed and position.,b:Merge into an adjacent lane when possible or adjust speed to create a gap.,c:Slow to a stop on the freeway.
note: When possible, move into another lane to create a gap; if not, adjust your speed to allow entering vehicles to merge safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do speed limit signs indicate?
options: a:The maximum or minimum speed that is legally allowed.,b:Potential driving speeds for the area.,c:The speed drivers should drive in heavy traffic.
note: Speed limit signs indicate the legal maximum (and sometimes minimum) speeds under ideal conditions; adjust speed lower when conditions are unsafe.

question: What is the 'No zone' in relation to large trucks and buses?
options: a:The blind spots around a truck or bus where smaller vehicles cannot be seen.,b:A special reduced speed zone near large vehicles.,c:A road area where loud music is restricted.
note: Large trucks and buses have blind spots on each side, in front, and behind; stay out of these 'no zones' to remain visible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you plan to turn left at a corner, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:All approaching vehicles.,b:Oncoming vehicles turning left with you.,c:Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting for a “Walk” signal.
note: When making a left turn, yield to pedestrians and bicyclists using the crosswalk and to oncoming traffic with the right-of-way.

question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?
options: a:Passing is not permitted.,b:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,c:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
note: A broken yellow line means you may pass to the left when it is safe and there is no oncoming traffic; do not cross solid yellow lines to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change with vehicle speed?
options: a:They increase as speed increases.,b:They decrease as speed increases.,c:Speed has no effect.
note: Higher speeds lengthen stopping distances and increase collision severity, so increase following distance as speed rises.

question: Which action helps prevent crashes by communicating with other road users?
options: a:Signal when slowing, stopping, or changing direction.,b:Ignore other drivers.,c:Drive only on side streets.
note: Use signals, horn, or emergency flashers as appropriate to inform others of your intentions and reduce surprises.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at the same time to a four-way intersection controlled by stop signs, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.,b:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,c:One driver may continue driving without stopping.
note: At a four-way stop where vehicles arrive simultaneously, yield to the driver on your right.

question: What can happen when you drink alcohol and take drugs together?
options: a:The effects of both can be increased, greatly impairing driving.,b:They will cancel each other out.,c:They will help cure your illness.
note: Combining alcohol and drugs often magnifies impairment, making driving far more dangerous than either substance alone.

question: What do downward-facing triangular traffic signs typically indicate?
options: a:Indicate construction zones.,b:Tell drivers to yield.,c:Indicate school zones.
note: A downward-pointing triangle is a yield sign; slow and give the right-of-way to oncoming traffic and pedestrians when required.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left, what should drivers do?
options: a:Signal, slow gradually while checking mirrors, move into the left lane if necessary, and watch for oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Move into the left lane at the last second.,c:Speed up and complete the turn quickly to avoid delays.
note: Signal a few seconds in advance, slow gradually while checking mirrors, position in the left lane, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and complete the turn when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you encounter a flashing red traffic light, what must you do?
options: a:Treat the intersection as if controlled by a stop sign (come to a full stop).,b:Continue through if no other vehicles are present.,c:Wait until it changes to green before proceeding.
note: A flashing red light requires a complete stop. Proceed only when it is safe, yielding to other traffic and pedestrians.

question: An octagonal eight-sided traffic sign always indicates:
options: a:A stop sign.,b:A speed limit sign.,c:A hospital sign.
note: An eight-sided (octagonal) sign always means STOP. Come to a complete stop at the sign before proceeding.

question: If you have a probationary license or instructional permit, when may you use your cell phone while driving?
options: a:If you are just answering a call.,b:As long as you don't text.,c:When you are reporting an emergency.
note: Drivers with probationary licenses or instructional permits are prohibited from using a cell phone while driving except to report an emergency.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, you should:
options: a:Slow down and carefully steer back onto the pavement once it is safe.,b:Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.,c:Stop immediately on the shoulder and wait.
note: Reduce speed without braking hard and carefully steer back onto the pavement when traffic allows; sudden steering or hard braking can cause loss of control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is true about emergency vehicles using sirens and flashing lights?
options: a:They have the right-of-way and you must yield.,b:They always must pull over to the right before you do.,c:You should follow them closely so traffic clears.
note: Yield to police, fire, or ambulance vehicles using a siren or flashing lights. Follow any directions from the emergency vehicle’s loudspeaker and proceed only when clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady green traffic light allow you to do?
options: a:Proceed through the intersection at a safe speed if it is clear.,b:Increase your speed to beat other cars.,c:Adjust your mirrors.
note: A steady green lets you go when the intersection is clear; always yield to those already in the intersection.

question: When driving on slippery surfaces such as ice or snow, what should you do before going down steep hills?
options: a:Shift to a low gear.,b:Follow other vehicles closely.,c:Pump your brakes continuously to keep them from freezing.
note: Shift to a lower gear before descending steep hills to help maintain control. Also increase following distance and avoid sudden stops.

question: When you see a steady yellow arrow at a traffic signal, what should you do?
options: a:May turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic.,b:Should slow to a stop if it is safe to do so.,c:Merge into a lane in the arrow's direction without stopping.
note: A steady yellow arrow warns that a red arrow is coming; you should stop unless you are already in the intersection and can clear it safely.

question: Why is night driving more hazardous?
options: a:Distance and speed of other vehicles are harder to judge in the dark.,b:Speed limits are higher at night.,c:There are always fewer vehicles at night.
note: Reduced visibility at night makes it difficult to judge distances and speeds; you can only see as far as your headlights allow.

question: At a light rail intersection you should always:
options: a:Pay attention to signals and signs and look both ways before crossing tracks.,b:Share the road only with pedestrians and bicycles.,c:Ignore traffic signals if no train is visible.
note: Obey all traffic controls at rail crossings and always look both ways before crossing train tracks; never drive around lowered gates.

question: Before turning on the ignition, what safety check should you do?
options: a:Buckle your own seat belt and make sure all passengers are buckled.,b:Buckle only child passengers.,c:Buckle only adult passengers.
note: Get into the habit of buckling your lap and shoulder belt and ensuring all occupants are properly restrained before starting the vehicle.

question: What is true about drivers who travel much slower than the speed limit?
options: a:Driving excessively slowly can be hazardous and you may be required to pull off to let traffic pass.,b:They always have the right-of-way.,c:They are always very safe drivers.
note: Driving so slowly that traffic backs up can be dangerous; you must allow others to pass if obstructing traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Left-turning drivers must yield to which traffic?
options: a:Oncoming traffic that is going straight or turning right.,b:Only vehicles that are overtaking them.,c:No one—they have the right-of-way.
note: Drivers making left turns must yield to oncoming vehicles traveling straight or turning right until it is safe to turn.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning on wet pavement?
options: a:Slow down.,b:Put your cruise control on to maintain a constant speed.,c:Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts to rain.
note: Hydroplaning is caused by driving too fast on wet roads. Reduce speed in wet conditions to maintain tire contact with the pavement.

question: What is the purpose of regulatory signs?
options: a:To tell drivers what they must or must not do.,b:To mark danger areas only.,c:To always be diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
note: Regulatory signs (often rectangular, white with black markings) indicate legal requirements such as speed limits, turn prohibitions, and other traffic rules.

question: If an oncoming driver uses high beams, where should you look?
options: a:Toward the right side of the road.,b:Toward the center of the road.,c:Toward either side of the road.
note: If another vehicle fails to dim high beams, glance toward the right edge of the road to avoid being blinded while maintaining your lane position.

question: If you begin to feel tired while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and rest or switch drivers.,b:Open a window to stay awake.,c:Drink caffeinated beverages and continue driving.
note: Stop for a rest or change drivers; caffeine and windows are not reliable substitutes for sleep.

question: What steps should you take when changing lanes?
options: a:Check mirrors and glance over your shoulder for blind spots before changing lanes.,b:Begin signaling as you move into the next lane.,c:Signal at least 500 feet before your lane change when driving in residential areas.
note: Before changing lanes, check mirrors, signal, and glance over your shoulder to clear your blind spot; signal in advance (about 100 feet in residential areas).

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about blind spots is true?
options: a:They are eliminated by having one outside mirror on each side.,b:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,c:Blind spots can be checked only with rearview mirrors.
note: Large trucks have much larger blind spots than passenger vehicles; mirrors do not eliminate all blind spots.

question: A flashing red traffic light has the same meaning as which sign?
options: a:Yield sign.,b:Stop sign.,c:Solid red light.
note: A flashing red signal is treated like a stop sign: stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: What is the shape of a stop sign?
options: a:Octagon.,b:Rectangle.,c:Square.
note: Stop signs are uniquely octagonal (eight-sided), indicating drivers must come to a complete stop.

question: Combining a prescription drug with alcohol can cause what effect?
options: a:It can make you unfit to drive and increase impairment.,b:It will make you more alert.,c:There will likely be no effect.
note: Many medications interact with alcohol, increasing drowsiness or impairment and making driving unsafe.

question: If you are under 21, what blood alcohol level can result in license suspension?
options: a:0.15 percent or more.,b:0.08 percent or more.,c:Any detectable amount.
note: Wisconsin has zero-tolerance for drivers under 21 — any detectable alcohol can lead to license suspension and penalties.

question: When changing lanes, which action should you never take?
options: a:Change lanes abruptly or spontaneously.,b:Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.,c:Check for vehicles moving into the same lane.
note: Never change lanes suddenly. Always check mirrors and blind spots and signal in advance to allow others time to react.

question: Which road surface tends to freeze first?
options: a:An intersection,b:A bridge,c:A tunnel
note: Bridges and overpasses often freeze before the surrounding pavement because air circulates both above and below their surfaces.

question: Approaching a heavy truck from behind on a hill, what should you expect?
options: a:The truck may be traveling slower than the posted speed limit.,b:You may not be able to legally pass the truck.,c:You will always be able to safely pass the truck.
note: Large trucks often travel below the posted limit on inclines; exercise caution and only pass where legal and safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?
options: a:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:When you have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.,c:When you are 50 feet in front of the passed vehicle.
note: Only move back into your lane when you can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror, ensuring you have enough space.

question: What attitude should a driver adopt about other drivers' compliance with right-of-way rules?
options: a:Assume most drivers obey the right-of-way rules.,b:Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way.,c:Assume all drivers automatically obey the right-of-way rules.
note: Even though right-of-way rules exist, never assume other drivers will follow them. Be prepared to yield to avoid a collision.

question: Where is the safest place for children age 12 and under to ride in a vehicle equipped with airbags?
options: a:The front seat.,b:The back seat.,c:The bed of a pick-up truck.
note: Airbags are designed for adults and can seriously injure children; anyone age 12 and under should ride in the back seat.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill on a two-way road with no curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Toward the right/side of the road so the vehicle will roll away from the center.,b:Straight ahead,c:Toward the left/center of the road.
note: When parking on an uphill without a curb, turn your wheels toward the right edge so, if the brakes fail, the vehicle will roll away from the roadway's center.

question: If a vehicle equipped with ABS starts to lose traction on a slippery road, what should you do?
options: a:Pump the brakes.,b:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.,c:Press and hold the gas pedal.
note: With ABS, press and hold the brake firmly; the system will automatically modulate braking to help maintain steering control.

question: When encountering a flashing yellow light at an intersection, you should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution.,b:Stop and wait for a green light.,c:Yield to all traffic before crossing the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down, be alert, and proceed carefully through the intersection when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you proceed through an intersection that has a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk?
