options: a:After slowing down to verify that there is no cross traffic,b:After coming to a complete stop and verifying that it is safe to proceed,c:After you have stopped at least 20 feet prior to the intersection
note: If a stop sign controls the intersection and there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection and proceed only when safe.

question: When a school bus is stopped to pick up or drop off passengers, what must drivers do?
options: a:Stop, regardless of your direction of travel.,b:Slow down and pass carefully.,c:Stop only if you are traveling in the same direction.
note: When a school bus displays flashing red lights and/or extends its stop arm to load or unload children, drivers from all directions must stop until the signals are turned off.

question: When should you allow an extra cushion of space behind or around your vehicle?
options: a:When following a small passenger car.,b:When following a driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle.,c:When following a station wagon.
note: Give extra space when following vehicles that cannot see behind them (such as trucks, buses, and vehicles towing trailers) to avoid collisions and to see around them.

question: Because motorcycles and mopeds are harder to see, what should car drivers do?
options: a:Make constant visual checks for motorcycles.,b:Share a lane with a motorcycle to keep it visible.,c:Slow down whenever one is nearby but not check mirrors.
note: Motorcycles are small and can be hidden in blind spots. Drivers should make frequent checks and be especially alert for two-wheeled vehicles.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing, what should you be prepared to do?
options: a:Slow down, look for trains, and be ready to stop.,b:Speed up to cross before a train arrives.,c:Ignore it if no train is visible.
note: Slow, look, and be prepared to stop. If warning lights flash or gates lower, stop 15 to 50 feet from the tracks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Another driver is passing you. How should you respond?
options: a:Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to allow safe passing and reentry.,b:Pull off the road.,c:Signal them when it's safe for them to pass.
note: Maintain your lane and speed or slightly reduce speed if safe to help the passing vehicle complete the maneuver and return to the lane.

question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow signal, what should you do?
options: a:Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.,b:Drive carefully through the intersection.,c:Stop and wait for the light to change.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution; scan traffic both directions and yield to any conflicts.

question: Which centerline marking prohibits passing from either direction?
options: a:Double solid yellow,b:Single broken yellow,c:Combination solid and broken yellow
note: A double solid yellow centerline means no passing by traffic in either direction.

question: When should you increase the distance between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead?
options: a:Are following a small passenger vehicle.,b:Are being tailgated by another driver.,c:Are driving more slowly than the posted speed limit.
note: If you are being tailgated, create extra space ahead of your vehicle by slowing gradually or changing lanes so you can stop safely if needed.

question: A leaking exhaust system can cause what while driving?
options: a:Make you drowsy or cause dangerous fumes.,b:Increase oil consumption.,c:Require an early tune-up.
note: A leaking exhaust can introduce toxic fumes into the vehicle cabin and make you drowsy; exhaust systems remove toxic gases and cool engine gases, so leaks can be deadly.

question: What dangers do worn or bald tires present?
options: a:They increase stopping distances, make turning harder, and raise hydroplaning risk.,b:They always reduce fuel consumption.,c:They improve ride comfort.,d:They decrease stopping distances.
note: Tires lacking adequate tread increase stopping distance, impair handling, and are more likely to hydroplane.

question: Which statement is true about driving and medications?
options: a:Medications are safe to take at any time, if prescribed by a doctor.,b:Over-the-counter medications cannot impair driving ability if taken in the recommended dosages.,c:Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.
note: Both prescription and over-the-counter medicines can impair driving; many cold and allergy medicines cause drowsiness and reduced coordination.

question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes, you should:
options: a:Look over your shoulder toward the direction you plan to move.,b:Look only at your side mirror.,c:Look only at your rearview mirror.
note: A quick over-the-shoulder glance in the direction you plan to move is the proper way to check the blind spot.

question: What does a pentagonal (five-sided) traffic sign warn you about?
options: a:Speed limits.,b:School zones.,c:No passing zones.
note: A pentagonal sign indicates a school zone or school crossing area; be alert for children and reduce speed as required.

question: When stopped in line on a railroad crossing with no gates, what must you ensure?
options: a:That there is room ahead so your vehicle can clear the tracks without stopping.,b:You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.,c:You may pass slower drivers while on the tracks.
note: Before crossing tracks without signals or gates, be certain there is enough space on the far side so you will not have to stop on the tracks.

question: A broken yellow centerline between two lanes means what?
options: a:Traffic flows in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.,b:Both lanes go in the same direction.,c:Passing is not permitted.
note: Broken yellow lines separate opposing traffic and indicate passing is permitted when the way ahead is clear.

question: Where is it best to keep a space cushion while driving?
options: a:On all sides of your vehicle.,b:Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.,c:Only in front of the vehicle.
note: Maintain space on all sides of your vehicle to give yourself time and room to react to hazards.

question: If your vehicle is blocking traffic after a minor accident, what should you do if possible?
options: a:Move your vehicle off the traveled portion of the roadway.,b:Leave your vehicle where it is until police arrive.,c:Drive away immediately and report the crash later.
note: After a minor collision, move vehicles out of traffic if possible, identify yourself, and render assistance as needed; do not leave the scene.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Left-turning drivers must yield to which vehicles?
options: a:Oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right.,b:Passing cars only.,c:No one at all.
note: When turning left, yield to all oncoming traffic and pedestrians until it is safe to turn.

question: What instruction is given by a red octagon-shaped sign?
options: a:Stop.,b:Do not enter.,c:Yield.,d:No parking.
note: An eight-sided red sign always means STOP; you must come to a complete stop at this sign.

question: What does a steady red arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:Traffic in the indicated lane must stop and may not proceed in that direction.,b:Drivers may turn after a complete stop.,c:Drivers may proceed in any direction.
note: A steady red arrow prohibits movement in the arrow's direction until a green signal permits it.

question: At about what speed can tires begin to hydroplane on water?
options: a:Around 35 miles per hour.,b:Around 45 miles per hour.,c:Around 55 miles per hour.,d:At any speed below 20 mph.
note: Tires may start to lose contact with the road and hydroplane as speed increases past about 35 mph on standing water.

question: When must you report a crash to law enforcement in Wisconsin?
options: a:When someone is hurt or damage exceeds $1,000 (or $200 to government property).,b:Only when someone is killed.,c:Only if your vehicle is severely damaged.
note: Report crashes that cause injury, death, or $1,000+ property damage (or $200+ damage to government property) to law enforcement.

question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what is the correct steering action?
options: a:Steer in the direction of the skid (into it).,b:Overcorrect in the opposite direction.,c:Turn the wheel into oncoming traffic.
note: If the vehicle skids, remain calm and steer in the direction of the skid until control is regained.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement edge, what is the correct way to return to the roadway?
options: a:Wait until it is safe, then gradually steer back onto the roadway.,b:Turn sharply back onto the pavement immediately.,c:Stop where you are and remain off the pavement.
note: Do not jerk the wheel; slow down, check traffic, then carefully re-enter the roadway when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If driving in the left lane and planning to move right, what checks should you perform before changing lanes?
options: a:Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder for vehicles.,b:Check mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder for vehicles.,c:Check mirrors, signal, and look over both shoulders.
note: When moving to the right, check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder to check the blind spot for other vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Excessive speed most commonly does what?
options: a:Often leads to high-risk decision-making and increases crash severity.,b:Decreases your ability to react to hazards but reduces crash severity.,c:Has no effect on crash risk.
note: Excessive speed increases the likelihood of crashes and the severity of injuries when crashes occur and often results in risky driving choices.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What determines how much space you need to cross traffic?
options: a:Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.,b:Presence of a stop sign.,c:Use of your turn signals.
note: The space required to cross traffic depends on road and weather conditions and the speed and distance of oncoming vehicles.

question: When driving near a large commercial vehicle, you should:
options: a:Follow the large vehicle closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.,b:Avoid driving beside it for long stretches of time.,c:Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.
note: Large commercial vehicles have significant blind spots; avoid driving beside them for extended periods so the driver can see you.

question: In which situation should your wheels not be pointed straight ahead?
options: a:When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.,b:When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.,c:When parked on the side of a level roadway where there is no curb.
note: When parked facing uphill or downhill with a curb, turn the wheels so the vehicle will roll into the curb rather than into traffic if the brakes fail.

question: What may happen if alcohol is combined with another drug?
options: a:The effects of both the alcohol and the drug may be increased.,b:Nothing will happen.,c:The effects of both will always be reduced.
note: Combining alcohol with other drugs can amplify impairment and unpredictably affect driving ability.

question: A regulatory sign with a red circle and a slash through it means:
options: a:That drivers should come to a complete stop.,b:That an action is forbidden.,c:That some drivers should yield to other drivers.
note: A red circle with a slash over a symbol indicates that the specified action is prohibited by law.

question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic accidents?
options: a:Inattentive driving,b:Excessive speed under the driving conditions,c:Following other vehicles too closely,d:All of the above
note: Inattentiveness, driving too fast for conditions, and following too closely are common causes of crashes; avoid these behaviors.

question: When merging onto a freeway, how should your speed compare to freeway traffic?
options: a:Be at or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.,b:Be 5–10 mph slower than freeway traffic.,c:Always drive at the posted freeway speed limit even if traffic is slower.
note: When merging, match the speed of freeway traffic so you can safely blend into the traffic flow.

question: Alcohol in any concentration is classified as what?
options: a:A depressant (it slows nerve impulses and bodily functions).,b:A stimulant.,c:Neither.
note: Alcohol is a central nervous system depressant that impairs judgment, reaction time, and coordination.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle on a two-lane road, when is it safe to return to your lane?
options: a:Have passed the other vehicle’s front bumper.,b:See the vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.,c:Cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.
note: Return to your lane when you can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror, indicating a safe gap.

question: During the first nine months with a probationary license under age 18, what restrictions apply?
options: a:Limits on the type and number of passengers and restrictions on late-night driving.,b:You cannot drive at all between midnight and 5:00 a.m.,c:No restrictions apply.
note: New drivers under 18 face passenger limits and night-time driving restrictions during the first nine months of their probationary license.

question: After consuming alcohol, when is reaction time slower?
options: a:After drinking alcohol.,b:After sleeping.,c:After working hard.
note: Alcohol slows reflexes and reaction time, impairing judgment and driving ability.

question: Which is a likely consequence of tailgating other drivers?
options: a:Can frustrate other drivers and make them angry.,b:Reduces collisions by preventing being 'cut off.'.,c:Cannot result in a traffic citation.
note: Tailgating increases road rage risks, reduces reaction time, and can lead to citations and rear-end collisions; avoid following too closely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:
options: a:Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.,b:Ignore the guard and follow surrounding traffic.,c:Assume the guard is not authorized to direct traffic.,d:Speed up to clear the area quickly.
note: Obey crossing guards' instructions and use extra caution in school zones for children's safety.

question: What is the best response when another driver is tailgating you?
options: a:Speed up to increase the distance between you and the tailgater.,b:Slam on your brakes to get the other driver to back off.,c:Change lanes or gradually slow down to encourage them to pass.
note: If a driver is following too closely, slow down gradually or change lanes to let them pass; avoid braking suddenly or escalating the situation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about changing lanes is true?
options: a:Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and over your left shoulder for a left lane change.,b:You only need to use your mirrors.,c:Vehicles with two outside mirrors have no blind spots.
note: Always check mirrors and look over the appropriate shoulder to verify the blind spot is clear before moving laterally.

question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are divided by which color lines?
options: a:Yellow,b:White,c:Red
note: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction; yellow lines separate opposing traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering an intersection, in what order should you scan?
options: a:Left, right, then left again.,b:Right only.,c:Left only.
note: Look left, then right, then left again before entering an intersection because traffic from the left may be closer.

question: Where are truck blind spots typically located?
options: a:Directly behind the truck and along the immediate left side of the cab.,b:Only on the right side of the truck.,c:Only directly in front of the truck.
note: Trucks have large blind spots: directly behind and along the immediate left and right sides; if you cannot see the driver in the truck's mirror, the driver likely cannot see you.

question: When approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light, what is the required action?
options: a:Come to a complete stop at the intersection.,b:Maintain your normal speed.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow signal means be alert and proceed with caution; slow down and watch for conflicts.

question: If your wheels run off the pavement edge, what should you do first?
options: a:Hold the wheel firmly, ease off the gas, and gently apply the brakes.,b:Turn sharply back onto the pavement immediately.,c:Stop in the lane and put on hazard lights.
note: If you leave the pavement, stay calm, slow down gradually, check traffic, and re-enter the roadway when safe.

question: Driving considerably slower than surrounding traffic is:
options: a:Appropriate if you don’t know the speed limit.,b:Often a hazard because others may attempt risky passes.,c:A good idea if the weather is bad.
note: Traveling much slower than traffic can be dangerous because drivers behind may make unsafe passing maneuvers.

question: To reduce glare from oncoming headlights, you should:
options: a:Glance briefly toward the right side of the road.,b:Keep your eyes on the centerline.,c:Flash your high beams.
note: Avoid staring at bright oncoming lights; look briefly to the right edge of your lane and then resume scanning ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When allowed to turn right on red, which requirement must you follow?
options: a:Stop completely and make the turn from the lane nearest the right curb after yielding to traffic and pedestrians.,b:Slow down and turn without stopping.,c:Always use your hazard lights before turning.
note: When turning right on red where permitted, come to a full stop, yield to pedestrians and traffic, signal, and turn from the right-most lane.

question: If you are turning and a pedestrian without a traffic signal is crossing your path, who must yield?
options: a:The driver must yield to the pedestrian.,b:The pedestrian must yield to the turning driver.,c:Whoever started moving last must yield.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at intersections even when no traffic light controls the crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To check for objects in your blind spot before changing lanes, you should:
options: a:Look over your left or right shoulder (as appropriate).,b:Only use the left outside mirror.,c:Only use the inside rearview mirror.
note: To see what mirrors can't, glance briefly over the shoulder in the direction of the lane change.

question: What is the best method to avoid hydroplaning?
options: a:Slow down when roads are wet and keep tires properly maintained.,b:Use cruise control to maintain a steady speed.,c:Drive faster to get through puddles quickly.
note: Reduce speed on wet roads, maintain tires, and avoid standing water to minimize hydroplaning risk.

question: When approaching railroad tracks, what precautions should you take?
options: a:Look and listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop.,b:Speed up to cross before a gate lowers.,c:Drive around any lowered gate.
note: Approach tracks with caution: look and listen for trains, slow down, and be prepared to stop if necessary.

question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?
options: a:Before you start driving.,b:Only after you begin moving.,c:Whenever a passenger asks you to.,d:Only when reversing.
note: Adjust mirrors, seat, and secure items before moving so you have the best view and control from the start.

question: What does a red-and-white triangular sign at an intersection indicate?
options: a:Decrease speed and yield the right-of-way when necessary.,b:Always come to a full stop at the intersection.,c:Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching.
note: A red-and-white triangular sign is a yield sign: slow as you approach, yield to vehicles and pedestrians, and be prepared to stop if required.

question: If a vehicle has a two-part (lap and shoulder) seat belt system, you should:
options: a:Use both the lap and the shoulder belts.,b:Use only the lap belt.,c:Use only the shoulder belt.,d:Not use either belt if the airbag is present.
note: Wearing both the lap and shoulder belt together provides the best protection; using one alone reduces effectiveness.

question: Alcohol consumption causes which impairments?
options: a:Slower judgment, poor coordination, and reduced concentration.,b:Improved coordination.,c:Increased concentration.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol impair vision, judgment, concentration, and coordination.

question: What can happen if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicines?
options: a:The combination can multiply the impairing effects of the alcohol or medicine.,b:The medicine will cancel alcohol's effects.,c:Alcohol will help the medicine work better.
note: Combining alcohol with medications can greatly increase impairment and unpredictably affect your ability to drive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes you should check your mirrors and what else?
options: a:Glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot.,b:Always slow down in your current lane.,c:Never look over your right shoulder.
note: Always check mirrors and quickly glance over the appropriate shoulder to confirm the lane is clear before changing lanes.

question: When a school bus ahead on your side has red lights flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Change lanes and pass cautiously.,b:Stop until the lights stop flashing.,c:Slow to 10 mph and pass slowly.
note: If a school bus is stopped with flashing red lights to load or unload children, you must stop and remain stopped until the lights are turned off and the stop arm is withdrawn.

question: When driving to an unfamiliar area, what should you do?
options: a:Only have to know generally where your destination is.,b:Plan your trip in advance.,c:Should depend on road signs to find your way.
note: Plan your route before you go so you are not distracted while driving and can focus on safe operation of the vehicle.

question: Which statement about blind spots is correct?
options: a:Blind spots are eliminated if you have one outside mirror.,b:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,c:Blind spots can be checked solely with the rearview mirror.
note: Even with properly adjusted mirrors, vehicles have blind spots. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than passenger vehicles.

question: What does a green arrow on a traffic signal indicate?
options: a:Traffic in the lane must turn in the arrow direction; it has the same authority as a circular green.,b:The arrow is used only on one-way streets.,c:You may proceed only if accompanied by a circular green light.
note: A green arrow authorizes movement in the arrow's direction and has the same force as a green light for that movement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road should:
options: a:Yield to drivers already on the public road.,b:Assume they have the right-of-way.,c:Force their way into traffic.
note: When entering from a driveway or private road, yield to vehicles on the public road and merge safely when it is clear.

question: When is it appropriate to sound a sharp blast of your horn?
options: a:When another vehicle is in immediate danger of hitting you.,b:When the driver ahead is driving under the speed limit.,c:To greet a friend.,d:To urge someone to drive faster.
note: Use a sharp horn blast only to warn of imminent danger; avoid using it to express frustration or impatience.

question: How do sudden wind gusts affect highway driving?
options: a:They can cause problems for all vehicles, not just large ones.,b:They only affect large vehicles.,c:They only cause visibility issues.
note: Strong, sudden winds can destabilize all types of vehicles and reduce visibility by blowing dust or debris into the roadway.

question: A solid red arrow in a traffic signal means:
options: a:The same as a circular red light; you must stop and may not turn in that direction.,b:The arrow is only advisory.,c:You may turn after slowing and checking for traffic.
note: A red arrow requires drivers in the indicated lane to stop and prohibits turning in the arrow's direction until green.

question: If your car becomes disabled on the highway, where should you park if possible?
options: a:Stop in the right lane.,b:Park with all four wheels off the traveled highway.,c:Stop where you are.
note: If your vehicle fails, move it completely off the main-traveled portion of the highway when it is safe to do so.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is behind you on a city street, what must you do?
options: a:Drive to the right edge of the road and stop until it passes.,b:Stay in your lane and slow down.,c:Keep driving to the right edge and slow down but do not stop.
note: Yield to emergency vehicles by pulling to the right edge and stopping; if in an intersection, clear it first then stop.

question: If you see a pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane, what must you do?
options: a:The pedestrian must yield the right-of-way.,b:You must yield the right-of-way.,c:Honk your horn to let them know you are there.
note: Blind or partially blind pedestrians using a cane or guide dog must be yielded to; slow and stop as necessary to let them cross safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-lane road where traffic moves in the same direction in two lanes and vehicles are passing you on the right, what should you do if the driver behind wants to go faster?
options: a:Move into the right lane when it is safe.,b:Stay in your lane to avoid impeding traffic.,c:Drive onto the left shoulder to let others pass.
note: If traffic is faster behind you and it is safe, move into the right lane to allow faster drivers to pass.

question: Many crashes are caused by which of the following?
options: a:Drivers traveling too fast for conditions.,b:Drivers checking mirrors and blind spots frequently.,c:Drivers yielding right-of-way properly.,d:Drivers keeping to the speed limit.
note: Driving faster than conditions safely allow causes many crashes; always adjust speed for weather, traffic, and road conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at an open (uncontrolled) intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:One driver may continue driving without stopping.,b:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,c:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
note: If you and another vehicle arrive at the same time, yield to the vehicle on your right; proceed when it is safe.

question: What should you allow a motorcycle to do when sharing the road?
options: a:Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.,b:Allow the motorcycle to use only half of a lane.,c:Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.
note: A motorcycle is entitled to a full lane; do not crowd it or occupy part of its lane.

question: To reduce glare from oncoming headlights at night, where should you look?
options: a:Toward the right side of the road ahead.,b:Directly at the oncoming headlights.,c:Over your shoulder.
note: If oncoming drivers don't dim high beams, keep your gaze toward the right edge of the road to avoid temporary blindness.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A curb painted red indicates:
options: a:No parking, standing, or stopping.,b:A loading zone.,c:An area reserved for picking up and dropping off passengers only.
note: Red curbs indicate no stopping, standing, or parking at any time unless otherwise posted.

question: If you want to pass a pedestrian walking along the roadway and an oncoming vehicle is approaching, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.,b:Keep driving at a steady speed; the oncoming vehicle must stop for you.,c:Honk your horn to get the pedestrian to move over.
note: Deal with one hazard at a time: let the oncoming vehicle pass, then pass the pedestrian if it is safe and you can give them adequate space.

question: Broken yellow lines on streets and highways are used to:
options: a:Indicate no passing zones.,b:Separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.,c:Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.
note: Yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions; broken yellow lines mean passing to the left is permitted when safe.

question: What is the best way to avoid hydroplaning when it is raining?
options: a:Slow down and reduce your speed.,b:Apply brakes as soon as the car starts to skid.,c:Drive at the same speed as in ideal conditions.
note: Reduce speed in wet conditions to avoid losing tire contact with the road, which causes hydroplaning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When following a large truck on the freeway, how far should you stay behind?
options: a:Farther behind than you would follow a passenger vehicle.,b:No more than one car length behind the truck.,c:As close as possible so the trucker can see you.,d:Directly beside the truck in the truck's blind spot.
note: Maintain extra following distance behind large trucks to give yourself time to react and to stay out of their blind spots.

question: When should you allow a larger following distance behind a motorcycle?
options: a:When you are behind a motorcycle, allow a larger following distance.,b:When driving more slowly.,c:When you may need to use your horn.
note: Motorcycles can stop quickly and are more likely to fall; maintain a three- to four-second following distance.

question: As a pedestrian, what is the safest practice when vehicles are approaching?
options: a:Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.,b:Always insist on the right-of-way when using a crosswalk.,c:Enter a crosswalk at any time because drivers must stop.
note: Pedestrians should not step into traffic when vehicles are approaching; even with right-of-way, a nearby vehicle may be unable to stop in time.

question: If an approaching driver fails to dim high beams, where should you focus your vision?
options: a:Toward the right side of the road.,b:At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.,c:Toward the left side of the road.
note: When faced with oncoming high beams, glance toward the right side of the roadway and use peripheral vision to keep your vehicle on course.

question: How should drivers equipped with ABS brake on snow or ice?
options: a:Pump the brakes.,b:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.,c:Stay off the brakes and wait for the car to drift to a stop.
note: On vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems, press and hold the brake firmly; the system will modulate the brakes to help maintain control.

question: If you borrow an unfamiliar vehicle, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Take a few minutes to locate and test essential controls such as lights, wipers, brakes, and turn signals.,b:Ignore minor defects to avoid embarrassing the owner.,c:Assume all vehicles operate the same and drive normally.
note: Familiarize yourself with the vehicle's controls and check for defects before driving; correct any safety issues prior to use.

question: If your vehicle has a mechanical problem while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Turn on your hazard lights and pull off the road to a safe location.,b:Stop in your driving lane and leave hazard lights off.,c:Signal and pull into the slow lane and continue driving.
note: When your vehicle breaks down, get off the roadway if possible, activate emergency flashers, and make your vehicle visible to other drivers.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:You must stop when instructed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal.,b:You have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing and do not need to stop.,c:Use cruise control when approaching railroad crossings to maintain speed.
note: You must stop at railroad crossings when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or flashing/activated warning signals.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, which action should you never do?
options: a:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.,b:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.,c:Cross the centerline in an intersection.
note: Never attempt to change lanes by crossing a centerline while inside an intersection. Before changing lanes, check mirrors, glance over your shoulder to clear your blind spot, and be aware of others entering the same lane.

question: What do your brake lights communicate to drivers behind you?
options: a:That you are slowing down or stopping.,b:That you are changing lanes.,c:That your emergency brake is on.,d:That you are turning right.
note: Brake lights indicate deceleration or stopping to following drivers; keep them in working order.

question: When you see a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog crossing, what should you do?
options: a:Stop until the person is safely out of your path.,b:Sound your horn and slowly pass.,c:Carefully drive around them without stopping.,d:Speed past to avoid delay.
note: Blind pedestrians have the right-of-way; stop and wait until they are well clear of your path.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning onto a multi-lane street, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:The lane closest to the one you came from.,b:The middle lane.,c:The lane marked with an arrow only.
note: Turn into the lane nearest your original lane and avoid changing lanes immediately after the turn.

question: Where is parking prohibited?
options: a:On a hill.,b:In a parking lot.,c:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
note: Parking is prohibited in crosswalks and marked bicycle lanes; follow posted rules and park within 12 inches of the curb when on the street.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to other drivers?
options: a:When entering a street from a garage, driveway, or alley.,b:Only when they are on a road to your left at an unmarked intersection.,c:Only when your traffic signal is a green arrow.
note: You must yield when entering a street from an alley, driveway, or garage and to pedestrians on sidewalks; exercise caution when entering roadways.

question: What is the purpose of highway pavement markings?
options: a:They are usually not important.,b:They provide information and guidance for drivers.,c:They are only for construction zones.
note: Pavement markings guide vehicle positioning, show passing zones, and warn about upcoming conditions.

question: How should you drive in work zones?
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop; obey posted limits.,b:Maintain your usual speed through the zone.,c:Speed up to get through quickly.
note: When approaching and driving through work zones, reduce speed, obey posted signs, and be prepared for sudden stops and workers near the roadway.

question: If your tires feel like they have lost contact with the road surface, what should you do?
options: a:Ease your foot off the gas pedal and avoid braking.,b:Shift into a lower gear to slow down.,c:Pump the brakes quickly and firmly.
note: If your tires lose contact with the road (possible hydroplaning), ease off the accelerator and avoid braking or turning until the tires regain traction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is passing prohibited?
options: a:On hills, on curves, at intersections, and at railroad crossings.,b:Only at intersections.,c:Only at railroad crossings.
note: Passing is unsafe and illegal on hills, curves, intersections, and railroad crossings where visibility or conditions make it hazardous.

question: In the rain you should use which headlights?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.,d:Interior lights for visibility.
note: Low beam headlights improve visibility in rain without reflecting back into your eyes as high beams do.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:The protected turning time is ending; prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.,b:Speed up to complete your turn before the light changes.,c:You may turn without signaling.,d:The turn is protected until the next signal change.
note: A steady yellow arrow warns that the green arrow protection is ending; yield to oncoming traffic and stop if you cannot turn safely.

question: What should you adjust first when you get into a car to drive?
options: a:Your seat position.,b:Your rearview mirror.,c:Your steering wheel tilt.
note: Adjust your seat first so you can reach the controls comfortably and see the road clearly; then adjust mirrors and steering wheel.

question: If you are being tailgated, what should you do if there is an open lane to the right?
options: a:Move over to the right, if there is an open lane to your right.,b:If there is not an open lane to your right, wait until the way is clear ahead and reduce your speed slowly to encourage the tailgater to drive around you.,c:Never slow down abruptly.
note: If a rear driver is following too closely, move into an open right lane when safe; if no lane is available, slow gradually to encourage them to pass.

question: When driving in fog, what should you do regarding lights and speed?
options: a:Slow down and use low beam headlights.,b:Slow down and use high beam headlights.,c:Turn your lights on and off to warn others.
note: In fog, reduce speed and use low beam headlights; high beams reflect back and reduce visibility. If visibility is unacceptably poor, pull off the road safely.

question: Fatigue while driving increases the risk of:
options: a:Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.,b:Being early for appointments.,c:Improved concentration over long trips.
note: Fatigue slows decision-making, degrades judgement, and can cause you to fall asleep at the wheel, increasing crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop where two vehicles arrive at exactly the same time, which vehicle proceeds first?
options: a:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.,b:The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.,c:Drivers must make hand motions to communicate with each other.
note: If two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right; proceed when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering interstate traffic from an entrance ramp should:
options: a:Yield to drivers already on the interstate.,b:Expect other drivers to yield to them.,c:Force their way into traffic if necessary.
note: Drivers entering a freeway should yield to traffic already on the interstate and merge safely when a gap is available.

question: A person using a white cane or guide dog is most likely to be:
options: a:A person involved with a traffic study.,b:A blind person.,c:A deaf person.
note: Drivers must always yield the right-of-way to pedestrians who are blind and using a white cane or guide dog.

question: When must you show proof of insurance to law enforcement?
options: a:Whenever stopped by an officer or involved in a collision or citation.,b:Only if you are involved in a crash.,c:Only if you are stopped and cited.
note: You must carry proof of financial responsibility and present it to police when requested after a stop or collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you use your turn signal?
options: a:When changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or entering traffic from an alley or parking area.,b:Only when other traffic is present.,c:Only during the maneuver itself, not beforehand.
note: Signals must be used to inform other road users in advance of lane changes, turns, and when pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.

question: To improve visibility in rain or fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: Low beams reduce glare and make your vehicle more visible to others in fog or heavy rain; avoid high beams.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are waiting in an intersection to complete a left turn, how should your wheels be positioned?
options: a:Keep your wheels straight while waiting.,b:Turn your wheels to the left while waiting.,c:Flash your headlights to request right-of-way.
note: Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left so a rear-end collision won't push you into oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto an interstate highway, what should you do?
options: a:Select a safe gap and merge into the lane of traffic.,b:Merge across two lanes at once.,c:Always stop before entering the highway.
note: On an entrance ramp, accelerate to match traffic speed, find a suitable gap, signal, and merge smoothly into the traffic lane.

question: How can you avoid alcohol-related crashes?
options: a:Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive.,b:Say no if someone offers you a drink while you're driving.,c:Drink coffee to sober up.,d:Consume a small amount so you are safe to drive.
note: Decide not to drive before drinking; alcohol impairs judgment so deciding beforehand helps prevent impaired decisions later.

question: If you are involved in an accident, what should you do first?
options: a:Stop immediately and call for police or medical help if needed.,b:Keep driving to your destination.,c:Move injured people immediately to a safer spot.,d:Ignore the accident if damage is minor.
note: Stop at the scene, move the vehicle out of danger if possible, render aid without moving seriously injured persons, and call authorities if needed.

question: Which substances may impair driving and could lead to a DUII arrest?
options: a:Beer, wine, and other alcoholic beverages.,b:Controlled substances such as illegal drugs or some prescription medicines.,c:Inhalants such as glue or paint.
note: A wide range of substances including alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many legal medications can impair driving. (Any of the listed substances can impair driving.)

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct way to use a freeway exit ramp?
options: a:Begin slowing only after you are on the exit ramp.,b:Slow down to the exit speed before entering the ramp.,c:Keep a constant freeway speed on the ramp.
note: Do not slow abruptly on the freeway; move onto the exit ramp and then reduce speed to the posted ramp speed.

question: The habit of turning your head to check blind spots is:
options: a:A good driving habit.,b:Unnecessary.,c:A bad driving habit.,d:Only required when backing up.
note: Turning your head to check blind spots before lane changes or merging is a safe habit that supplements mirror checks.

question: You must report an accident when property damage to any one person's property is at least how much?
note: You must report a crash to law enforcement if there is an injury, death, or property damage of $1,000 or more to any one person’s property (different thresholds apply for government property).

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes on a highway, which steps should you take?
options: a:Signal, check mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots.,b:Signal only.,c:Increase your speed before changing lanes.
note: Always signal your intentions, check mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to ensure no one is in your blind spot.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal shows a steady green arrow, what should a driver do?
options: a:May turn in the direction of the arrow after yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.,b:Should merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.,c:Should slow to a stop if it is safe to do so.
note: A steady green arrow permits drivers to turn in the arrow's direction. Be in the proper lane and yield to vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you hear a siren behind you while driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Pull over to the right and stop to allow the emergency vehicle to pass.,b:Stop immediately where you are without signaling.,c:Speed up to get out of the way.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights or siren, safely pull to the right and stop so it has a clear path; continue only when it has passed.

question: Which technique helps maintain safe awareness while driving?
options: a:Checking your rearview mirrors frequently.,b:Staring fixedly at the road ahead.,c:Using high beams in poor visibility.
note: To remain aware of hazards, scan the road and check mirrors every few seconds. Avoid staring only at the area directly in front of your vehicle.

question: Which roadway is most likely to be icy in cold weather after snow or rain?
options: a:A hilly, open road,b:A residential road,c:A road in a shaded area
note: Shaded sections of road freeze more quickly and thaw later, making them particularly slippery in cold conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal is steady yellow and you have not entered the intersection, what is the correct action?
options: a:Come to a safe stop.,b:Speed up to beat the red light.,c:Reduce speed and proceed without stopping.
note: A steady yellow means prepare to stop; if you have not entered the intersection, come to a safe stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The largest vehicle.,b:The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.,c:The car on the left has the right-of-way.
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you treat a traffic control signal that is not working?
options: a:Treat the intersection as an all-way stop and come to a full stop before proceeding.,b:If the intersection appears clear, you don't need to stop.,c:Drive quickly through to clear the intersection.
note: If signals are out of service, treat the intersection as an all-way stop: stop, then proceed when it's safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your interstate exit, what should you do?
options: a:Keep driving to the next exit and use it to return safely.,b:Quickly cut across traffic to reach the exit.,c:Make a U-turn on the interstate.
note: Do not attempt last-minute turns or U-turns; proceed to the next exit and safely return to your route.

question: How is having a driver license best described?
options: a:Privilege.,b:Requirement.,c:Right.
note: Driving is a privilege granted by the state and may be suspended or revoked for violations.

question: How should you check blind spots to see vehicles hidden from mirrors?
options: a:Look over your shoulder.,b:Rely solely on the inside rearview mirror.,c:Rely only on outside mirrors.,d:Use turn signals without looking.
note: Blind spots cannot be seen in mirrors; quickly turn your head to check over the shoulder in the lane you intend to enter.

question: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Call your insurance company when you get home.,b:Leave a note with your name and address on the vehicle.,c:Wait at the scene until the owner returns.
note: If you damage a parked vehicle and can’t locate the owner, leave a note with your contact information attached to the vehicle.

question: If there is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, you should:
options: a:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.,b:Cautiously drive around them.,c:Honk and expect them to yield.,d:Speed up to pass before they finish.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway even where no marked crosswalk exists.

question: How is drinking alcohol and driving classified as a traffic problem?
options: a:A minor traffic safety problem.,b:A serious traffic safety problem.,c:Safe if you have only had a few drinks.
note: Driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs is a serious safety problem that endangers you and others on the road.

question: If you see a sign that says 'Reduced speed, 35 mph,' what does it mean?
options: a:The new 35 mph limit begins at that sign.,b:The new 35 mph limit starts at the next speed sign.,c:You have extra time to slow down before the reduced zone.
note: 'Reduced speed' signs indicate you must slow to the posted limit, and if a new limit is shown, it begins at that sign.

question: Is it ever acceptable to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates?
options: a:When the train has passed.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:When the lights have stopped flashing.
note: Do not drive around railroad crossing gates under any circumstances; wait until gates are fully raised and signals stop.

question: When passing a vehicle that has just parked at the side of the road, what should you assume?
options: a:The driver may open a door or step out, so use extra caution.,b:The driver will not open the door.,c:You should speed up to pass quickly.
note: Assume a parked vehicle's occupant may open a door or exit suddenly; give extra space and be prepared to stop.

question: On average, how quickly does the body eliminate alcohol?
options: a:About one standard drink per hour.,b:About two standard drinks per hour.,c:About three standard drinks per hour.
note: An average person's body metabolizes roughly one standard drink per hour, though many factors can affect this rate.

question: Which combination gives the best protection in a collision?
options: a:Both lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.,b:Only an airbag.,c:Only a lap and shoulder belt.,d:No restraint at all.
note: Safety belts significantly increase survival and reduce injury; airbags add protection when used together with belts.

question: Why is using a cell phone while driving considered a distraction?
options: a:It causes the driver to be concerned about the cost of the call.,b:It occupies the driver's hands, eyes, and mind.,c:It is an activity that draws the attention of other drivers.
note: Cell phone use while driving distracts the driver's hands, eyes, and mind, increasing crash risk even if the driver is experienced.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a 'Yield' sign, what is your responsibility?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic close enough to cause conflict.,b:Always proceed without slowing.,c:Yield only to vehicles on your right.
note: At a yield sign you must slow or stop if necessary and give right-of-way to crossing or merging traffic that is close enough to cause conflict.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a crosswalk, who must yield?
options: a:Pedestrians must yield to vehicles.,b:You must yield to pedestrians.,c:Construction workers must yield to you.
note: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crosswalks. If there is no traffic signal, vehicles must stop for pedestrians in marked or unmarked crosswalks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn at an intersection, what must you do?
options: a:You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.,c:You should never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: When turning left you must yield to oncoming vehicles traveling straight and to pedestrians in the crosswalk.

question: How should you adjust your driving on slippery roads?
options: a:Reduce your speed and increase following distance.,b:Always drive at the posted maximum speed.,c:Use cruise control to maintain a steady speed.
note: On slippery roads, slow down, avoid sudden movements, and do not use cruise control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle traveling in the same direction, how should you pass?
options: a:Pass as safely and as quickly as possible.,b:Drive at the same speed as the vehicle being passed.,c:Pass as slowly as possible.
note: Pass promptly and safely, then return to your lane when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a stop is required but there is no stop line or crosswalk, where should you stop?
options: a:At the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic without entering it.,b:You are not required to stop.,c:Only if you can see at least 200 feet in both directions before stopping.
note: Stop at the nearest point to the intersection where you can get a clear view without entering the crosswalk or intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Should you start across an intersection if you know you will block it when the light turns red?
options: a:No — you must not block the intersection under any circumstances.,b:Yes — if you entered on a yellow light it's acceptable.,c:Yes — if traffic is heavy and unavoidable.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it completely; blocking intersections can lead to citations and safety hazards.

question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes mean?
options: a:Drivers may pass or change lanes if it is safe.,b:Drivers may not pass.,c:Lanes move in opposite directions.
note: Dashed white lines separate lanes traveling in the same direction and may be crossed to pass or change lanes when safe.

question: When a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle, what should you expect?
options: a:Beep your horn.,b:Expect the child to be in total control of the bicycle.,c:Expect the unexpected.
note: Children on bicycles can be unpredictable; slow down, stay alert, and be prepared for sudden changes in direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when facing a green arrow signal?
options: a:Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian still in the intersection, then go.,b:Proceed immediately without yielding.,c:Wait four seconds before proceeding.
note: A green arrow gives the right-of-way for the movement indicated, but you must yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians who remain in the intersection.

question: What must you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights is approaching?
options: a:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.,b:Try to outrun it to reach your destination first.,c:Continue driving but stay out of its way.,d:Speed up and move into the emergency lane.
note: You must yield the right-of-way by pulling to the right and stopping when an emergency vehicle with lights or siren approaches.

question: What greatly increases stopping distances and the severity of crashes?
options: a:High speeds,b:Slow speeds,c:Night drives.
note: Higher speeds increase stopping distances and the energy involved in a crash, making collisions more severe.

question: Which action helps reduce road rage incidents?
options: a:Always signal when changing lanes.,b:Use your horn frequently.,c:Talk on your cell phone while driving.
note: Signaling intentions helps other drivers anticipate your moves and reduces misunderstandings that can lead to aggressive driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How long before changing lanes or turning must you signal by law?
options: a:Signal at least 100 feet before moving left or right.,b:Only signal if traffic is present.,c:Signal only during the maneuver.
note: The law requires signaling in advance — generally at least 100 feet — before changing lanes or turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about driving too slowly is true?
options: a:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.,b:Driving too slowly is never unsafe.,c:The speed you drive does not affect safety.
note: Driving substantially below the flow of traffic can cause frustration and unsafe passing maneuvers; drive with the flow of traffic within legal limits.

question: If you have a green light but pedestrians are crossing against the DON'T WALK signal, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and allow the pedestrians to cross safely.,b:Honk to warn them and proceed, c:Speed up to get through before they reach your path.,d:Proceed if there are no cars.
note: You must yield to any pedestrians in the intersection even if you have a green light; wait until they are clear before moving.

question: The driver ahead of you stops at a crosswalk. What is the correct action?
options: a:Cautiously pass the vehicle at 10 mph or slower.,b:Stop, proceeding only when all the pedestrians have crossed.,c:Change lanes, look carefully, and pass the stopped vehicle.
note: Do not pass a vehicle that has stopped at a crosswalk; there may be pedestrians crossing that you cannot see.

question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors while driving?
options: a:Only when you are slowing down.,b:Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.,c:To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.
note: Check your mirrors frequently to monitor traffic behind you and be prepared for lane changes, braking, or other maneuvers.

question: Before driving after a winter snowfall, what parts of your vehicle should you clear of snow and ice?
options: a:Headlights only,b:Turn signals only,c:Windows only,d:All windows, headlights, and signals
note: Clear snow and ice from all windows, headlights, taillights, brake lights, and turn signals so you can see and be seen.

question: If you are worried, nervous, angry, or crying, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Can drive faster because you are more in touch with your senses.,b:Will drive no differently than they would if they were thinking more clearly.,c:Should take the time to focus on driving before starting the engine.
note: Strong emotions distract you from driving. Calm yourself and make sure you are focused before driving to reduce crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may pass another vehicle if the line dividing your lane and the lane you wish to enter is what type of line?
options: a:Broken white,b:Double solid yellow,c:Solid yellow
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to pass when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, what is usually best practice?
options: a:Proceed slowly while waiting for an opening.,b:Accelerate to a speed that matches freeway traffic and blend in.,c:Turn on your hazard lights until safely on the freeway.
note: Use the on-ramp to accelerate to the speed of traffic so you can merge smoothly; traffic on the freeway has the right-of-way.

question: What are the colors of standard warning signs that indicate hazards ahead?
options: a:Black letters or symbols on a yellow background.,b:White letters on a blue background.,c:Black letters on a white background.,d:Red letters on a green background.
note: Warning signs generally have black symbols or letters on yellow backgrounds; work zone warnings use orange.

question: Slowing down just to look at collisions or unusual events on the roadside typically:
options: a:Improves traffic flow by preventing collisions.,b:Prevents rear-end collisions.,c:Causes traffic congestion.
note: 'Rubbernecking' slows traffic and causes congestion; maintain steady driving and avoid unnecessary slowing to look at incidents.

question: If you have had several beers, which action will reduce the effects of alcohol?
options: a:Taking a cold shower.,b:Waiting several hours.,c:Drinking several cups of coffee.
note: Only waiting allows alcohol to be metabolized and its effects to diminish; other measures do not sober you up.

question: Distracted drivers are at greater risk when using which device?
options: a:Cell phones (including hands-free devices).,b:CD players.,c:Radio.
note: Using cell phones—hands-free or handheld—significantly increases crash risk; any device that takes attention from driving is dangerous.

question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle with lights or siren, what must you do?
options: a:Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop, regardless of the direction it is coming from.,b:Only pull over if the emergency vehicle is following you.,c:Only pull over if it is approaching from the opposite direction.
note: You must pull to the right edge of the road and stop for an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or siren, whether it is coming from ahead or behind.

question: How do defensive drivers think and act?
options: a:They consider what other drivers might do and prepare to react.,b:They assume other drivers will always do the right thing.,c:They expect no breaks and give none.
note: Defensive drivers anticipate potential mistakes by others and are prepared to adjust their driving to avoid collisions.

question: How should you respond to a pedestrian who is blind and guided by a dog or carrying a white cane?
options: a:You must always yield the right-of-way.,b:You must tell them where to cross the street.,c:You only have to yield the right-of-way if you are at a corner.
note: Blind or visually impaired pedestrians using a guide dog or white cane have the right-of-way and you must yield to them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection where you want to turn but are not in the proper lane, what should you do?
options: a:Drive to the next intersection and make the turn from the proper lane.,b:Quickly cut across traffic to make the turn.,c:Turn from your current lane after signaling.
note: Never make last-minute turns; go to the next intersection and turn from the correct lane.

question: If a driver is tailgating you on a two-lane road and you cannot safely change lanes, what should you do?
options: a:Apply your brakes suddenly then resume speed.,b:Slow down gradually to encourage the tailgater to pass.,c:Speed up to increase the gap.
note: Slow down gradually to encourage the tailgater to pass when you cannot safely move over; sudden braking is dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How far before a turn should you normally signal?
options: a:About 75 feet before the turn.,b:About 25 feet before the turn.,c:About 50 feet before the turn.
note: You should signal well in advance of a turn—commonly about 100 feet before—so others know your intentions; among the choices, 75 feet is the closest.

question: What problem can result from continuous hard braking on ice or snow?
options: a:Locking the front wheels and losing steering control.,b:Helping you stop faster.,c:Keeping the brakes from freezing.
note: Hard continuous braking on slippery surfaces can lock the front brakes and cause loss of steering; instead brake gently and steer smoothly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an officer is directing traffic at a signalized intersection, whom should you obey?
options: a:Follow the directions indicated by the traffic light.,b:Follow the directions given by the officer.,c:Honk at the officer.
note: Follow the directions of a traffic officer rather than the traffic signal when an officer is controlling traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you required to stop your vehicle?
options: a:At any intersection where a police officer orders you to stop.,b:Where there is a red traffic light.,c:Both of the above.
note: You must obey a police officer's directions and stop at steady or flashing red traffic lights; follow either instruction when applicable.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an intersection with a steady yellow light and you have not entered it, what should you do?
options: a:Stop safely before entering the intersection if you can do so.,b:Speed up to beat the red light.,c:Proceed through the intersection at the same speed.
note: A steady yellow warns the signal is about to turn red; stop if safe, otherwise clear the intersection cautiously.

question: What is the purpose of rumble strips on the road?
options: a:To alert inattentive drivers via sound and vibration that they have left the travel lane.,b:To test a vehicle's shock absorbers.,c:To alert drivers to tire problems.,d:To provide traction for motorcycles.
note: Rumble strips produce noise and vibration to warn drivers they are straying off the lane or approaching a stop.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline mean regarding passing?
options: a:Passing is not allowed from either direction.,b:Passing is allowed from both directions.,c:Passing is allowed only from your direction of travel.
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate opposite-direction traffic and prohibit passing from both directions.

question: To improve visibility during rain or fog, use which lights?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: Use low beams in rain, snow, sleet, or fog; high beams can reflect back and reduce visibility.

question: Which statement is true about drowsy driving?
options: a:Drowsy drivers can perform so poorly they may appear impaired or drunk.,b:Opening a window or turning up the radio is enough to stay alert.,c:Drinking strong black coffee is a reliable way to remain safe to drive.
note: Drowsiness can impair driving to the point that performance resembles intoxication. Small countermeasures like coffee or music are not reliable solutions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you treat a flashing red traffic signal at an intersection?
options: a:Stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when clear.,b:Reduce speed and proceed with caution.,c:Stop and remain stopped while the light flashes red.
note: A flashing red signal is equivalent to a stop sign — come to a complete stop, yield, and go when safe.

question: If a train is approaching and is a danger, what must you do?
options: a:Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Cross quickly if you think you can beat it.,d:Pass other vehicles to get through first.
note: Do not cross tracks if a train is close enough or moving fast enough to be a danger; wait until it has passed entirely.

question: Large vehicles compared with smaller cars generally have:
options: a:Larger blind spots.,b:Smaller blind spots.,c:No blind spots.
note: The bigger the vehicle, the larger the blind spots. Trucks and large SUVs have areas not visible in mirrors where other vehicles cannot be seen.

question: What do pennant-shaped traffic signs signify?
options: a:Speed limits.,b:No passing zones.,c:School zones.
note: Pennant-shaped signs indicate no passing zones; they typically appear on the left side of the road and may include text confirming the restriction.

question: If a lane is separated by a single broken white line on a highway, what are you allowed to do?
options: a:You cannot cross the line to pass.,b:You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.,c:You may only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes going in the same direction and may be crossed for passing or lane changes when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is a good general rule to follow regarding passing?
options: a:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only as needed.,b:Pass on the right whenever possible.,c:Try to get to the front of slow-moving traffic at all costs.
note: Passing increases collision risk; stay with the flow of traffic within speed limits and pass only when necessary and safe.

question: Who must wear seat belts in a moving vehicle under Wisconsin law?
options: a:Everyone in the vehicle.,b:Only the driver.,c:Only children under 16 years old.
note: Wisconsin law requires the driver and all passengers to wear seat belts while the vehicle is moving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement, what is the safest way to return to the road?
options: a:Slow down, steer parallel to the road, then ease back onto the pavement when safe.,b:Accelerate and sharply steer back onto the road.,c:Stop quickly on the shoulder and then pull back on.
note: Do not overreact; reduce speed, stabilize the vehicle, and ease back onto the pavement when it is safe to do so.

question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, what is the safest reaction?
options: a:Call the police immediately.,b:Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.,c:Flash your vehicle's lights to let the aggressive driver know he is wrong.
note: Remain calm and avoid escalating the situation; give the aggressive driver space and, if needed, report the behavior from a safe location.

question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline indicates you should:
options: a:Not pass other vehicles.,b:Reduce your speed immediately.,c:Expect a traffic signal ahead.
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means passing is prohibited for your lane.

question: If you park in an unusual area, what should you ensure?
options: a:Park five feet from the curb.,b:Park with your reverse lights on.,c:Make your vehicle visible to approaching drivers from any direction.
note: When parked in nonstandard locations, make sure your vehicle is visible to other road users so it doesn't create a hazard.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:When passing a bicyclist.,b:When traveling through an intersection.,c:When you see a child who is about to run into the street.
note: Use your horn as a warning when you think another driver or pedestrian is unaware of your presence, for example if a child is about to run into the street.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are in an intersection and an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches, what should you do?
options: a:Continue through the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.,b:Stop immediately in the intersection and remain there.,c:Drive slowly and let it pass without pulling over.
note: If you are in an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches, clear the intersection, then pull to the right and stop to allow it to pass.

question: What does a broken yellow centerline on a roadway indicate?
options: a:Passing is permitted from either direction when safe.,b:A construction zone is ahead.,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: Broken yellow centerlines separate opposing traffic and allow passing for drivers next to the broken line when it's safe.

question: What is the most important rule about speed in curves?
options: a:Slow down before you enter the curve.,b:Drive at the posted speed entering the curve and then slow at the sharpest part.,c:Accelerate gently before entering the curve.
note: Because of inertia, you should reduce speed before entering a curve to maintain control throughout the turn.

question: Which activities can cause distracted driving?
options: a:Eating, drinking, smoking, changing radio stations, or using a cellphone.,b:Only talking on a phone.,c:Only changing a CD.
note: Many common tasks—eating, using a phone, adjusting audio—distract drivers and increase crash risk.

question: Regarding pedestrians, what must a driver do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to all pedestrians, even if the pedestrian is wrong.,b:Yield only when the pedestrian is legally entitled to it.,c:Make sure the pedestrian sees the vehicle before proceeding.
note: Drivers must do everything possible to avoid striking pedestrians and must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians, even when the pedestrian is not where they should be.

question: What happens to tire effectiveness as speed increases on a wet roadway?
options: a:As you drive faster, your tires become less effective.,b:Water does not affect cars with good tires.,c:Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
note: As speed increases on wet roads, tires lose effectiveness and you risk hydroplaning as tires fail to clear water from the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you change lanes?
options: a:Quickly and often.,b:When a car is in your blind spot.,c:Gradually and carefully.
note: Change lanes gradually and carefully, checking mirrors and blind spots before moving; avoid unnecessary lane changes.

question: What do yellow centerlines on the roadway separate?
options: a:Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.,b:Traffic lanes on one-way streets.,c:Carpool lanes from regular lanes.
note: Yellow lines separate opposing traffic on two-way roads; broken yellow allows passing when safe, solid yellow prohibits crossing for passing.

question: Is it legal to drive under the influence of a medication that impairs your driving?
options: a:No — driving under the influence of impairing medication is not permitted.,b:Yes — if a physician prescribed it.,c:Yes — if you do not feel drowsy.
note: Any substance, including prescription or over-the-counter medications, that impairs your driving makes it illegal and unsafe to drive.

question: An arrow painted on the pavement in your lane means:
options: a:Drivers in that lane must make the movement indicated by the arrow.,b:You may choose to ignore it if no other traffic is present.,c:You must stop before making the movement indicated by the arrow.
note: Pavement arrows indicate the required lane movement; follow any traffic signals or signs before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are in a designated left-turn lane and oncoming traffic is present, what should you do before turning?
options: a:Turn your front wheels left to be ready.,b:Signal before you reach the intersection and keep wheels straight until safe to turn.,c:Move to the left of the center lane immediately.
note: Signal about 100 feet before turning and keep wheels straight until you begin the turn to avoid being pushed into oncoming traffic if struck from behind.

question: When following another vehicle at night, which lights should you use?
options: a:Low-beam headlights.,b:High-beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: Use low beams when you are within 500 feet of another vehicle to avoid blinding the driver ahead and to reduce glare.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before returning to your lane after passing another vehicle, what should you make sure of?
options: a:Beep your horn.,b:See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:Flash your headlights.
note: Only return to your lane when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror, indicating you have enough room.

question: What must you do at a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights?
options: a:Stop well behind the gates and wait until they are lifted and the tracks are clear.,b:Drive around the gates if you do not see a train.,c:Slow down and creep around the gates.
note: It is illegal and dangerous to drive around lowered railroad gates; stop behind them and wait until it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a highway marked by double solid yellow lines, you may:
options: a:Cross only to make a left turn into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.,b:Cross to pass slower vehicles when no oncoming traffic is present.,c:Cross these lines under no circumstances.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate opposing traffic and prohibit passing; you may cross them only to make a left turn into or from a driveway or similar location.

question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Four-way flashers.
note: Use low-beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow; high beams can reflect back and reduce visibility.

question: When following a large truck on the freeway, where should you position your vehicle?
options: a:Farther back than you would for a passenger car.,b:Closer behind the truck than usual.,c:To the right side of the truck and wait to pass.
note: Large trucks have larger blind spots and longer stopping distances, so maintain a greater following distance than you would behind a passenger vehicle.

question: What lane width entitlement do motorcycles have?
options: a:The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.,b:Only half the lane width.,c:Only the bicycle lane.,d:They must share the lane with other motorcycles only.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the full lane width just like other motor vehicles and should be given full use of the lane.

question: Under ideal conditions, what is the minimum recommended following distance?
options: a:Four seconds.,b:Two seconds.,c:Six seconds.
note: Under ideal conditions, leave at least four seconds between you and the vehicle ahead to allow enough time to react and stop if necessary.

question: If you hit an unattended parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Leave a written notice with your name, address, and circumstances of the accident.,b:You have done enough if you drive away.,c:Wait until the police arrive and do nothing else.
note: If you strike an unattended vehicle, leave a note with your contact information and details of the incident if you cannot find the owner.

question: Signs that require drivers to obey specific directions are called:
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Information signs.,c:Warning signs.
note: Regulatory signs inform drivers of traffic laws and regulations; failing to comply may result in penalties.

question: Compared to daytime driving, how hazardous is driving at night?
options: a:More dangerous because of reduced visibility and increased chances of impaired or tired drivers.,b:Less dangerous.,c:No more or less dangerous.
note: Night driving is riskier due to limited visibility, glare, and a higher likelihood of tired or impaired drivers.

question: Which is an effective measure to reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Reduce your speed when driving in the rain.,b:Ensure you always drive at the posted speed.,c:Keep your tires dramatically underinflated to increase contact area.
note: Hydroplaning is most likely at higher speeds; reduce speed in wet conditions and ensure tires have good tread and proper inflation.

question: On a dimly lit street at night, how should you drive with respect to what your headlights illuminate?
options: a:Drive slowly enough to be able to stop within the area lit by your headlights.,b:Use high beams to better see the road ahead.,c:Keep instrument panel lights bright for visibility to others.
note: Ensure you can stop within the distance illuminated by your headlights when driving on poorly lit roads.

question: When approaching a school bus with its stop arm extended, how should drivers respond?
options: a:Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.,b:Honk before passing on the left.,c:Continue driving if you believe children are not present.
