note: Drivers must stop for a school bus with stop arm extended and flashing red lights; do not proceed until the bus retracts the arm and lights stop flashing.

question: When a steady green arrow is displayed, when may you proceed in the arrow's direction?
options: a:If you are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear, yielding to pedestrians and vehicles in the intersection.,b:Only after coming to a complete stop.,c:Only after the green arrow turns off.
note: A green arrow allows the movement indicated if you are in the correct lane and have yielded to any pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your turn or exit on a freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Continue to the next exit and turn there safely.,b:Stop and back up on the shoulder.,c:Make a quick U-turn on the freeway.
note: If you miss an exit, do not back up or stop—proceed to the next exit where you can safely turn around.

question: Is it permitted to park on the shoulder of a freeway?
options: a:If no part of your vehicle is on the road.,b:As long as you turn on your four-way flashers.,c:Only in an emergency.
note: Parking on a freeway shoulder is prohibited except in emergency situations.

question: What does a flashing yellow arrow for left turns allow you to do?
options: a:May turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Must come to a complete stop.,c:Should merge into the lane in the arrow's direction without yielding.
note: A flashing yellow arrow permits left turns, but you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the proper sequence for changing lanes?
options: a:Signal, check mirrors, check blind spot, then change lanes.,b:Check mirrors and then change lanes without signaling.,c:Signal and change lanes immediately.,d:Speed up then signal.
note: Signal your intent, check interior and side mirrors, glance over your shoulder to check blind spots, then change lanes when safe.

question: If your vehicle is equipped with airbags, what is true about seat belts?
options: a:Seat belts should still be worn.,b:Seat belts are not necessary.,c:Seat belts should be worn only behind the back.
note: Airbags are supplemental; for full protection you must always wear both lap and shoulder belts.

question: What is the effect of excessive speed on crash severity?
options: a:Saves time so you can get to your destination more quickly.,b:Helps you maneuver around obstacles.,c:Increases the likelihood of serious bodily injury and death.
note: Excessive speed increases both the chance of crashing and the severity of injuries and fatalities in a collision.

question: When is it legal to cross center yellow lines to pass another vehicle?
options: a:When the yellow line next to your side of the road is broken.,b:When the yellow line on the opposite side is broken.,c:When the vehicle ahead moves to the right to let you pass.
note: A broken yellow line next to your lane means you may pass if it is safe. A solid yellow line next to your lane prohibits passing.

question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads, what should you remember about traction?
options: a:Your tires grip the road better than when you are driving on pavement.,b:Your tires do not have as much traction as they do on pavement, so you must slow down.,c:Visibility is better than on pavement.
note: Loose surfaces reduce traction and increase stopping distance; slow down and drive more cautiously on gravel or dirt roads.

question: When a school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing to load or unload children, drivers must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.,b:Slow to 25 mph and then pass cautiously.,c:Proceed once you think the children have cleared the roadway.
note: When a school bus displays flashing red lights and its stop arm is extended, all approaching traffic must stop until the lights stop flashing and the arm is retracted.

question: How must you yield the right-of-way to an emergency vehicle using siren and flashing lights?
options: a:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it has passed.,b:Stop immediately, even if you are within an intersection.,c:Drive as closely to the right edge of the road as possible and stop.
note: Yield to any emergency vehicle using sirens and lights by pulling to the right edge of the road and stopping; do not stop in an intersection. Proceed only after it has passed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer orders you to stop even though the traffic light is green, what should you do?
options: a:Obey the traffic signal.,b:Do what the vehicle in front of you does.,c:Obey the officer.
note: Drivers must follow the directions of a police officer directing traffic even if those directions conflict with traffic signals, signs, or markings.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with no gates or flashing lights but a crossbuck, what should you do?
options: a:Approach all tracks with extreme caution and cross only when you know that there is no train coming.,b:Turn your radio down to hear if there may be an approaching train.,c:Only continue once cleared to do so by a flagger, if applicable.
note: Always approach such crossings cautiously, look both ways, and cross only when you are sure no trains are approaching on any track.

question: What does a broken yellow centerline indicate?
options: a:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,b:Passing is not permitted.,c:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
note: A broken yellow line beside your lane means you may cross the centerline to pass another vehicle if it is safe to do so.

question: Before stopping your vehicle at a traffic signal or sign, you should first:
options: a:Press down hard on the accelerator.,b:Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic.,c:Set the parking brake.
note: Check mirrors to be aware of traffic behind you before you brake for a smooth and safe stop.

question: To avoid losing traction on wet roads, you should:
options: a:Slow down.,b:Make abrupt turns.,c:Brake firmly.
note: Reduce speed in wet conditions and maintain good tire condition; if control loss occurs, ease off the gas, avoid braking, and steer to regain control.

question: A red arrow pointing right on a traffic signal means:
options: a:You may not turn in that direction until the light changes to green.,b:You may turn after slowing and checking for traffic.,c:You may turn after you come to a complete stop.
note: A red arrow indicates a stop for traffic in the direction of the arrow; do not turn until a green signal or green arrow appears.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving in traffic, the safest approach is to:
options: a:Drive with the flow of traffic at a safe speed.,b:Fluctuate your speed to keep alert.,c:Drive faster than most traffic.,d:Always drive slower than the flow to be cautious.
note: Maintaining a speed consistent with the flow of traffic (within limits) reduces collision risk caused by speed differentials.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you required to stop your vehicle?
options: a:When a traffic officer orders you to stop, at stop signs, or at a red signal.,b:Only at stop signs.,c:Only where there is a red light.
note: You must stop when signaled by a traffic officer, at stop signs, or when a red light is displayed.

question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians?
options: a:Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.,b:Even if the pedestrian crosses the street carelessly.,c:Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.
note: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians in the roadway, even if the pedestrian is crossing against a light or acting carelessly; avoid striking them.

question: When should you look over your shoulder to check a blind spot?
options: a:Pulling toward or away from a curb.,b:Turning left or right.,c:Changing lanes.
note: Check over your shoulder whenever you change your vehicle's position, such as when changing lanes; mirrors do not show all blind spots.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, how should your speed compare to traffic on the freeway?
options: a:You should be driving at or near the speed of freeway traffic.,b:You should always be at the posted speed limit regardless of traffic.,c:You should drive much more slowly than freeway traffic.
note: When entering a freeway, match the speed of highway traffic as closely as possible so you can merge safely, unless that speed exceeds the legal limit.

question: The effect that lack of sleep has on driving ability is most comparable to the effect of what?
options: a:The effect that alcohol has.,b:The effect that amphetamines have.,c:The effect that anger has.
note: Fatigue impairs driving in a way similar to alcohol; for example, being awake 18 hours can impair you about as much as a 0.05% BAC.

question: If the roadway is wet or icy, how should you drive?
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Drive at the posted speed.,c:Speed up to maintain momentum.
note: Wet, snowy, or icy roads reduce tire traction; slow down to maintain control and increase stopping distance.

question: If a pedestrian with a guide dog is at a corner ready to cross, what should you do before turning right?
options: a:Turn off your engine until the person crosses the street.,b:Tell the pedestrian when to cross the street.,c:Wait until the person crosses the street.
note: Pedestrians using a guide dog or white cane must be given the right-of-way. Stop and wait for them to cross safely before turning.

question: What color are pavement markings that separate lanes moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Yellow.,b:White.,c:Yellow and white.
note: Yellow pavement markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions. White marks separate lanes moving in the same direction.

question: Orange-colored traffic signs typically indicate:
options: a:Construction and maintenance warning areas.,b:General warning signs.,c:Regulatory instructions.
note: Orange is used for construction and maintenance warning signs to alert drivers to temporary conditions and workers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which sign that you can see in your rearview mirror tells you it is safe to return to the driving lane after passing?
options: a:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:When the driver you passed waves you back.,c:When you are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.
note: Only move back into the driving lane when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, indicating a safe gap.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another driver is passing you in a no-passing zone, what should you do?
options: a:Maintain your speed and position so they can re-enter safely.,b:Pull off the road to let them pass.,c:Speed up to prevent them from passing.
note: Maintain a steady speed and position to allow the passing vehicle to complete the maneuver and merge safely back into the lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is a permitted way to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Pass in a curve or on a hill because the chance of oncoming traffic is small.,b:Pass by using the shoulder of the highway.,c:None of these are permitted.
note: You may not pass on hills or curves where you cannot see oncoming traffic, by driving on the shoulder, or by crossing solid yellow lines. Only pass where it is legal and safe.

question: When are roads most slippery during a rainstorm?
options: a:For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.,b:After it has been raining for several hours.,c:The day after it rains.
note: Pavement can be especially slippery during the first 10–15 minutes of rain because oil and residue on the road surface mix with water.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Interstate driving requires which of the following?
options: a:Both the ability to safely drive at higher speeds and constant alertness.,b:Only the ability to drive fast.,c:Only occasional alertness.
note: Safe interstate driving requires constant alertness and the ability to handle higher speeds and traffic flow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it ever permissible to drive off the roadway onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle?
options: a:No — under no circumstances.,b:Only if the vehicle ahead is turning left.,c:Only when there are two or more lanes in your direction.
note: You may not use the shoulder or leave the paved portion of the road to pass another vehicle.

question: How can stress affect your driving?
options: a:It lowers your ability to concentrate on driving.,b:It decreases the likelihood of an accident.,c:It causes you to fall asleep at the wheel.
note: Strong emotions and stress reduce concentration and decision-making ability, increasing the risk of a driving mistake or crash.

question: When following another vehicle at night, which headlight setting should you use?
options: a:Keep your headlights on the low beam setting.,b:Use your high beams until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.,c:Use your high beam headlights.
note: Use low beams when following another vehicle to avoid dazzling the driver ahead; high beams should be used only when no other vehicles are nearby.

question: Why should drivers be extra alert for motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?
options: a:They are harder to see and are less protected than motorists.,b:They follow different traffic laws.,c:They always have the right-of-way.
note: Smaller road users can be difficult to spot and are more vulnerable, so drivers should pay extra attention to avoid collisions.

question: What adjustment should you make to your following distance when driving at night?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Always use high beams to improve visibility.,c:Look directly at oncoming headlights to judge distance.
note: Visibility is reduced at night, so increase following distance and use headlights properly; avoid staring at oncoming headlights.

question: What does an advisory (curve/turn) speed sign indicate?
options: a:Shows a recommended driving speed for the curve and should be reduced in adverse conditions.,b:Is blue with black lettering.,c:May be ignored in rainy, snowy, or icy conditions.
note: Advisory speed signs recommend a safe speed for curves; drivers should reduce speed in poor weather even if they feel comfortable at a higher speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you not use your horn?
options: a:Near blind pedestrians.,b:When visibility ahead is limited.,c:If you might hit another vehicle.
note: Avoid using your horn near blind pedestrians; it may startle or confuse them. Yield and proceed when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you not cross a single broken white or yellow line?
options: a:When doing so would interfere with traffic.,b:When turning left into a driveway.,c:When the car in front of you is disabled.
note: You may only cross a broken line to pass or change lanes if you can do so safely and without disrupting traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the intersection is blocked by traffic ahead while you face a green light, what should you do?
options: a:Stay out of the intersection until traffic ahead clears.,b:Turn left and find another route.,c:Follow the vehicles ahead and enter the intersection.
note: Never enter an intersection you cannot clear. Blocking an intersection when the light turns red can impede cross traffic and result in a citation.

question: What should be your first response when visibility is reduced?
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Turn on your headlights.,c:Turn on windshield wipers only.
note: Lowering speed is the first precaution when visibility decreases; also use lights and wipers as appropriate.

question: If your vehicle does not have ABS and you must stop quickly, what should you do?
options: a:Firmly pump the brake pedal.,b:Hold down the brake pedal without releasing.,c:Tap the brakes lightly and repeatedly.
note: For vehicles without ABS, pumping the brakes can help bring the vehicle to a quick stop while allowing steering control.

question: If you are emotionally upset when you get to your car after a work incident, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Take a few minutes to calm down before you begin driving.,b:Drive fast on the interstate to let off steam.,c:Play loud music to drown out thoughts.
note: Do not drive while emotionally agitated. Take time to cool off before driving to avoid risky behavior caused by anger or distraction.

question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings you should always do what to check for hazards?
options: a:Stop, listen, and proceed cautiously.,b:Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.,c:Slowly pass vehicles that seem to be stopped for no reason.
note: Whenever people or other traffic may enter your path, look left and right along the sides of your vehicle to check for hazards.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:When passing another car.,b:If another car is in danger of hitting you.,c:When you have to stop quickly.
note: Use your horn to warn others of imminent danger, such as if you believe another vehicle is about to hit you.

question: If you hear a siren but can't see the emergency vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Pull to the curb and stop so you can check if it is on your street.,b:Keep driving until you see the vehicle.,c:Slow down but do not stop until you see it.
note: If you hear a nearby emergency siren and can't locate the vehicle, safely pull to the right and stop until you are sure it is not headed toward you.

question: If you experience a tire blowout while driving, which is correct?
options: a:Tap or pump the brakes.,b:Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.,c:Apply the brakes firmly and quickly.
note: If a tire blows out, ease off the accelerator, slow down gradually, avoid heavy braking until you have control, then pull off the road safely.

question: How does smoking or preparing to smoke while driving affect your driving?
options: a:It has no effect.,b:It helps keep you alert.,c:It is a distracting activity that can take your hands or eyes off the road.
note: Smoking while driving can distract you, requiring you to remove hands from the wheel or take your eyes off the road, increasing crash risk.

question: Which of these statements about passing a motorcycle is true?
options: a:The driver of a passenger vehicle must change lanes completely when passing a motorcycle.,b:A motorcycle with two people is always more stable than one with a single rider.,c:It is acceptable for other drivers to follow motorcycles very closely.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane. When passing, change lanes completely to give them full lane width and never crowd them.

question: Which statement is true about alcohol's effect on mental and driving skills?
options: a:Even the smallest amount of alcohol can limit concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.,b:Only a BAC above the legal limit will impair these skills.,c:Alcohol does not affect driving skills.
note: Any amount of alcohol can reduce cognitive and driving skills; no amount is guaranteed safe for driving.

question: What is the most common color for warning signs?
options: a:Yellow,b:Green,c:Red
note: Most warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black symbols or words.

question: What does a steady red traffic signal require you to do?
options: a:Stop at the stop line.,b:Stop before entering any crosswalk.,c:Stop before entering the intersection.
note: A red signal means stop; you must stop before the intersection, at the stop line, or before the crosswalk, and remain stopped until the light permits you to proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering traffic from a curb, what should you do?
options: a:Should drive more slowly than other traffic for 200 feet.,b:Should wait for a large enough gap to get up to the speed of traffic.,c:Should wait for the first two vehicles to pass, then drive into the lane.
note: When merging into city or highway traffic wait for a gap large enough for your vehicle to accelerate to the speed of traffic before entering.

question: Which factor does NOT affect stopping distance?
options: a:The time of day.,b:Your reaction time.,c:The condition of your vehicle's brakes.
note: Stopping distance depends on reaction time, brakes, tires, vehicle weight, speed, and road conditions — not the time of day itself.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a steady red traffic light, a driver should:
options: a:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped until it turns green or a permitted turn is completed.,b:Proceed through the intersection if there is no traffic.,c:Continue because they have the right-of-way.
note: A steady red means stop. Drivers may turn right on red after yielding, unless prohibited by sign.

question: If your vehicle begins to hydroplane, what should you do?
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly to prevent sliding.,b:Slow down gradually and avoid braking.,c:Drive at a constant speed to regain traction.
note: If hydroplaning, ease off the gas and allow the car to slow; do not brake sharply until tires regain traction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:Into the first available lane of the one-way street.,b:Into any lane you prefer.,c:Into the second lane if it is unobstructed.
note: When turning, move from the lane closest to your direction of travel into the first legal lane on the street you enter.

question: If the road ahead is flooded, what is the safest action?
options: a:Turn around and find another route.,b:Drive in the center of the roadway.,c:Slam on the brakes immediately.
note: Never try to drive through flooded areas. Even shallow water can hide hazards. Turn around and seek a different route.

question: What should you expect from children playing near the road?
options: a:They may run into the street without looking.,b:They will always stop at the curb before crossing.,c:They will know when it is safe to cross.,d:They will follow crossing signals.
note: Children may not understand traffic danger and can dart into the roadway unpredictably; slow down and be prepared to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which is correct when changing lanes or passing on an interstate?
options: a:Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.,b:Stop on the shoulder of the road if you are tired.,c:You should always use cruise control.
note: On an interstate, signal, check mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots before changing lanes or passing. Use the shoulder only in emergencies.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the traffic light turns from green to solid yellow as you approach an intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection unless you are too close to stop safely.,b:Consider it the same as a caution sign and continue without slowing.,c:Stop immediately in the intersection.
note: A steady yellow warns the light will turn red; stop if you can do so safely, otherwise proceed through carefully.

question: Like alcohol and drugs, what effect can drowsiness have on driving?
options: a:It can impair judgment and slow reaction time.,b:It improves alertness.,c:It makes you a better driver.
note: Drowsiness reduces reaction time, awareness, and judgment, making driving unsafe.

question: Which types of drugs can impair driving?
options: a:Illegal drugs, prescription medications, and over-the-counter drugs.,b:Only marijuana.,c:Only cold remedies.
note: Many substances—including illegal drugs, and legal prescription or over-the-counter medicines—can impair driving and may make it illegal to drive.

question: Where are stop lines typically painted?
options: a:At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.,b:Next to churches and schools.,c:In curves and on hills.
note: Stop lines are solid white lines across traffic lanes at intersections and crosswalks indicating where vehicles must stop.

question: What can help drivers conserve gasoline while driving?
options: a:Accelerating quickly at every green light.,b:Sitting in the driveway with the engine running.,c:Slowing down gradually instead of braking hard and accelerating again.
note: Smooth driving—anticipating traffic flow, slowing gradually, and avoiding unnecessary rapid acceleration and braking—helps conserve fuel.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a one-way street, when may you turn left onto another one-way street?
options: a:Only when traffic on the street you are turning into moves to the left.,b:When traffic on that street moves to the right.,c:Only if you increase your speed before the turn.
note: You may turn left from a one-way street onto another one-way street only when traffic on the destination street flows to the left (the direction you will enter).

question: What happens to your field of vision as you increase your vehicle's speed?
options: a:Increases your field of vision.,b:Decreases your field of vision.,c:Makes it easier to see cross traffic.
note: As speed increases your effective field of vision narrows; you must be extra alert for hazards and reduce speed when necessary.

question: When facing an aggressive driver, what is the safest response?
options: a:Avoid eye contact, slow down, let them pass, and increase distance.,b:Cut them off to slow them down.,c:Retaliate by tailgating.
note: Remain calm, avoid engaging, create space, and let aggressive drivers pass to reduce risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a turn, how should you change your speed?
options: a:Increase your speed.,b:Vary your speed unpredictably.,c:Reduce your speed to maintain control.
note: Slow to a speed that allows you to keep control and remain within your lane while turning.

question: What is the safest way to cross railroad tracks?
options: a:Listen and look both ways, then cross only if it is safe.,b:Cross quickly when a train is approaching.,c:Proceed if the red lights are not flashing.,d:Rely only on gates to tell you when to cross.
note: Always look and listen for trains in both directions, observe signals, and do not cross until you are sure there is no danger.

question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway you should do which of the following?
options: a:Check mirrors and blind spot; signal your intention.,b:Turn on your headlights.,c:Sound your horn.
note: Before a lane change, check rearview and side mirrors, glance over your shoulder to check blind spots, and signal your intended move.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic signals are not functioning due to a power outage, how should drivers proceed at the intersection?
options: a:Turn on your hazard lights and proceed through the intersection without stopping.,b:Treat the intersection as a four-way stop and proceed when it is your turn.,c:Park your vehicle as far off the road as possible and wait for power to be restored.
note: If traffic signals are out, approach as you would a four-way stop: stop, yield as required, and proceed cautiously when it is safe.

question: What is a common effect of eating or drinking while driving?
options: a:Make no driving errors.,b:Have trouble staying in their lanes and controlling their vehicle.,c:Are better drivers because they are not hungry.
note: Eating or drinking while driving distracts your hands, eyes, and attention, making it harder to stay in your lane and safely control the vehicle.

question: Which statement is true about seat belts and child restraints?
options: a:You should never place a rear-facing infant restraint in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.,b:An airbag can be dangerous to an infant or small child, even in a low-speed collision.,c:You should always make sure all your passengers are using a seat belt or child restraint.,d:All of the above
note: Always buckle up all passengers, use child restraints appropriate to age/size, and never place a rear-facing infant in a front seat equipped with an active airbag.

question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.,d:Interior dome light.
note: Use low beams (and fog lights if equipped); high beams reflect off fog and reduce visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you are turning or changing lanes, when must you signal?
options: a:Always signal your intentions in advance, even if no visible traffic is present.,b:Only signal when other vehicles are present.,c:Only signal when driving at night.
note: You must signal prior to turning or changing lanes to inform other road users of your intentions regardless of visible traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering the interstate from a ramp, what should you do after checking for a gap?
options: a:Expect traffic to allow you to enter since you have the right-of-way.,b:Merge carefully into the gap after accelerating to match traffic speed.,c:Wait for the lane to clear completely before merging.
note: Use the acceleration lane to reach highway speed and merge carefully into an appropriate gap; don’t assume others will yield.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you use your turn signals?
options: a:When changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or entering traffic from an alley or parking area.,b:Only when other traffic is present.,c:Only during the maneuver itself, not before.
note: Use signals to communicate intentions in advance of lane changes, turns, and when entering traffic from parking or alleys.

question: When changing lanes, which of the following should you NOT forget to do?
options: a:Check for other drivers who may also be moving into the same lane.,b:Fail to signal at all.,c:Neglect side and rearview mirrors.
note: Before changing lanes, check mirrors, signal, and verify that others are not moving into the same space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where should your vehicle be positioned when making a right turn?
options: a:As close as possible to the right side of the road.,b:Near the center of the roadway.,c:Close to the left side of the street.
note: When preparing a right turn, get as far to the right side of the road as possible and do not cut across lanes of traffic.

question: If you experience a tire blowout, what sequence of actions should you take?
options: a:Do not immediately use your brakes and gradually slow down before pulling off the road.,b:Take your foot off the gas and immediately apply the brakes.,c:Gradually slow down and then speed up.
note: On a blowout, release the accelerator, avoid sudden braking, gradually slow, and then carefully pull off the road.

question: If you are driving in another vehicle's blind spot, what should you do?
options: a:Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.,b:Maintain your speed and position.,c:Stay in the blind spot to avoid being seen by others.
note: Do not linger in another driver's blind spot; adjust your position so you are visible in their mirrors.

question: Which of the following is a telltale sign of a drunk driver?
options: a:They are weaving between lanes.,b:They are driving more slowly than the normal traffic flow.,c:They are making quick and sudden stops.
note: Signs of impaired driving include weaving, erratic lane changes, sudden braking, and inconsistent speeds; such behaviors warrant caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How long before turning should you signal?
options: a:About three to four seconds before turning.,b:Immediately as you begin the turn.,c:Only when other vehicles are nearby.
note: Activate turn signals roughly three to four seconds before making the turn to alert others of your intent.

question: When parking on any hill, what steps should you take?
options: a:Set the parking brake and leave the transmission in 'park' (or in gear), and position wheels so vehicle will roll away from traffic if brakes fail.,b:Let one rear wheel touch the curb.,c:Leave front wheels parallel to the road if there is no curb.
note: Always put the vehicle in park or a gear, use the parking brake, and turn wheels so the car will roll away from traffic if brakes fail; if a curb exists, position wheels against it as appropriate.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In which situations should you not attempt to pass another vehicle?
options: a:On a hill or curve.,b:Only when the speed limit is low.,c:When on a divided highway.
note: Never pass on a hill or curve where your view of oncoming traffic is blocked, nor at intersections, railroad crossings, or other no-passing zones.

question: How can you avoid being in a truck or bus driver's blind spot?
options: a:Avoid driving alongside them and avoid tailgating.,b:Never pass them.,c:Flash your headlights at them.
note: Large vehicles have significant blind spots at their sides and rear; avoid lingering beside or too close behind them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection, if another vehicle arrives at the same time and is on your right, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up and get through the intersection.,b:Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.,c:Drive into the intersection and make the other vehicle stop.
note: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection simultaneously, yield to the vehicle on your right and proceed when it is safe.

question: What is a safe method to drive through a curve?
options: a:Slow down before entering the curve and gently speed up as you exit.,b:Maintain a constant speed through the whole curve.,c:Speed up entering and slow down exiting.
note: Reduce speed before entering a curve and accelerate gradually as you exit to maintain control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, what should you do to ensure it is safe?
options: a:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move and check mirrors.,b:Rely only on the rearview mirror.,c:Rely only on the left side mirror and then move.,d:Make the move quickly without signaling.
note: Check mirrors and glance over your shoulder to confirm no vehicles are in your blind spot before changing lanes.

question: Which statement about sudden changes in weather is true?
options: a:A sudden change in weather calls for a change in driving.,b:You should slow down when driving in rain and fog.,c:Be particularly aware of vehicles coming up behind you in inclement weather.
note: When weather changes suddenly, you must adapt your driving (slow down, increase following distance, and use appropriate lights).

question: If you become tired while driving, what is the best action?
options: a:Stop to rest or switch drivers.,b:Open a window and keep driving.,c:Drink coffee and continue driving.
note: If you feel drowsy, the safest choice is to stop and rest or change drivers. Short-term fixes like coffee are not reliable.

question: Should you always drive more slowly than other traffic?
options: a:No — driving too slowly can block traffic and be unsafe.,b:Yes — it's always the safest practice.,c:Yes, it is always safer than driving faster than other traffic.
note: Drive at a speed appropriate for conditions; driving unnecessarily slowly can be dangerous and may be illegal if it blocks traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After stopping at a stop sign, in what order should you scan the intersection?
options: a:Look left first, then right, then left again.,b:Look right first, then left, then right again.,c:Check your rearview mirror for tailgaters.
note: At a stop, look left first since vehicles from the left may be closest; then look right, then left again to be sure it's safe to go.

question: Before driving, what should you remove from your vehicle?
options: a:All snow, frost, and ice from all windows and mirrors.,b:Only the windshield.,c:Only the windshield and passenger window.
note: Clear all windows and mirrors of snow, ice, and frost so you have full visibility before moving the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you drive slower than the flow of traffic, what may happen?
options: a:You may interfere with traffic and receive a ticket.,b:You will improve traffic flow.,c:You will demonstrate defensive driving.
note: Driving so slowly that you obstruct the normal movement of traffic can earn you a citation; match the flow when safe and lawful.

question: How many behind-the-wheel driving hours must an applicant under 18 complete before applying for a probationary license?
options: a:30 hours total, including 10 at night.,b:40 hours total, including 10 at night.,c:50 hours total, including 10 at night.
note: Applicants under 18 must have 30 hours of behind-the-wheel driving experience, including at least 10 hours at night, before applying for a probationary license.

question: If another driver cuts you off, what should you do?
options: a:Let it go and continue driving safely.,b:Pull alongside and yell at them.,c:Flash your high beams repeatedly.,d:Speed up and tailgate them.
note: Avoid road rage: do not take it personally; return to safe driving and maintain distance from aggressive drivers.

question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Yes.,b:No.,c:Only if there is no oncoming traffic.
note: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing from either direction except to turn into or out of a driveway or make a permitted left turn.

question: When driving near heavy trucks you must allow for:
options: a:The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,b:The decreased stopping distance of trucks.,c:The reduced size of truck blind spots.,d:The truck's ability to swerve quickly.
note: Large vehicles require longer distances to stop. Avoid lingering in their no-zones and stay where the truck driver can see you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver who arrived before you.,b:The driver on your left.,c:The driver across from you.,d:The driver who signals first.
note: Vehicles proceed in order of arrival; if multiple arrive simultaneously, yield to the vehicle on your right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which technique helps avoid crashes on snow- or ice-covered roads?
options: a:Reduce your speed and increase following distance.,b:Get off highways as quickly as possible.,c:Add extra weight to the vehicle to improve traction.
note: Lower speed and increase following distance are key to maintaining control on snow or ice.

question: At an intersection with a flashing red light, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a full stop and proceed only when it is safe.,b:Slow down and pass through the intersection carefully.,c:Turn left or right because the road ahead is blocked.
note: A flashing red signal requires a full stop; proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe to continue.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline mean about passing?
options: a:Passing is allowed from both directions.,b:Passing is allowed only from your direction.,c:Passing is not allowed from either direction.
note: A double solid yellow line in the center of a two-way roadway means no lane may cross the line to pass.

question: Which behavior describes an inattentive driver?
options: a:Stares at objects off the roadway or daydreams while driving.,b:Maintains eye contact during a conversation with a passenger while driving.,c:Only watches the vehicle ahead of their vehicle.
note: Distractions such as daydreaming, looking away from the roadway, or reading while driving reduce awareness and increase crash risk.

question: If you are driving and a tire suddenly goes flat, what should you do?
options: a:Rapidly pump the brake pedal several times.,b:Slow down gradually and not brake.,c:Press down on the brake pedal as hard as you can.
note: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly, lift off the accelerator, let the vehicle slow, and brake gently only if needed; pull off the road when safe.

question: What is true about double solid yellow lane markings?
options: a:Neither lane may pass.,b:Both lanes may pass.,c:The lane to the right may pass.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate opposing traffic and prohibit passing from both directions.

question: What is a good habit to relieve fatigue on a long trip?
options: a:Stop and rest every two hours.,b:Do arm exercises every hour.,c:Drive with one eye open at a time.
note: To reduce fatigue on long trips, stop every two hours for a break; if drowsy, find a safe place to nap or stay overnight.

question: What single practice most reduces your risk of injury or death in a crash?
options: a:Wearing your seat belt.,b:Limiting driving to weekdays.,c:Staying in the right lane on multilane highways.
note: Wearing a seat belt is the single most effective action to reduce the risk of injury or death in a motor vehicle crash.

question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog; high beams reflect off the fog and reduce visibility further.

question: In rainy weather, when are turning and stopping most hazardous?
options: a:After it has been raining all day.,b:One half hour after it stops raining.,c:During the first half hour of rain.
note: Roads are most slippery during the first half hour of rain because oil and residue on the pavement mix with the water.

question: If you begin to feel tired while driving, the best action is to:
options: a:Stop driving and rest.,b:Open your window to get fresh air.,c:Drink caffeine and continue driving.,d:Turn up the radio volume.
note: Fatigue impairs driving similar to alcohol; stop and rest rather than trying to push through.

question: What does Wisconsin's Implied Consent Law require of drivers?
options: a:Drivers under age 21 cannot drive after drinking any alcohol.,b:Penalties become more severe after a first OWI conviction.,c:Drivers must submit to alcohol testing when requested by a police officer.
note: By driving in Wisconsin you consent to submit to chemical testing for alcohol or drugs when an officer requests it; refusal carries license penalties and arrest.

question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop before crossing the intersection.,c:Wait for a green light before proceeding.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down, check for cross traffic, and proceed with caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it acceptable to stop in a travel lane on the roadway?
options: a:You may stop to drop off passengers.,b:You may stop to look up an address.,c:You may make a U-turn or back up if you get on the wrong entrance ramp of the freeway.,d:None of the above
note: You should not stop in a travel lane. If you miss a turn or exit, continue to the next safe location rather than backing up or stopping in a travel lane.

question: Blue traffic signs provide information about:
options: a:Motorist services (rest areas, hospitals, food).,b:Construction and maintenance.,c:Regulatory requirements.,d:Distance to cities.
note: Blue signs are service signs used to inform drivers about available services and facilities.

question: How should you check blind spots when changing lanes?
options: a:Turn your head to look over your shoulder to check the blind spot.,b:Rely only on the inside rearview mirror.,c:Only use the outside mirrors.
note: Mirrors do not show all areas; always glance over your shoulder to check blind spots before lane changes.

question: A badly worn or defective suspension can cause:
options: a:Squealing brakes.,b:Slack in the steering.,c:Vehicle control problems.
note: A worn suspension affects your ability to control the vehicle and can make it difficult to keep the vehicle stable over bumps.

question: Which of these does NOT affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:How much time passes between drinks.,b:Your body weight.,c:The type of alcoholic beverage you drink.
note: BAC is influenced by amount consumed, time between drinks, and body weight — not by the brand or type of alcoholic beverage.

question: Any amount of alcohol in your blood can affect what?
options: a:Your judgment and physical coordination.,b:Your right-of-way privileges.,c:Only your knowledge.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol impair judgment, coordination, and reaction time; impairment can occur below legal limits.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic is blocking the intersection when your light turns green, what should you do?
options: a:Partially enter the intersection to establish your right-of-way.,b:Don't enter the intersection until you can get completely across.,c:Continue into the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can get completely through it; blocking the intersection is illegal and dangerous.

question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol or drugs?
options: a:All of the above (alertness, concentration, reaction time, coordination).,b:Only alertness and concentration.,c:Only reaction time and coordination.
note: Alcohol and many drugs reduce alertness and concentration and slow reaction times and coordination, affecting all driving skills.

question: For drivers 21 or older, driving with what minimum BAC is illegal?
options: a:0.05 percent.,b:0.08 percent.,c:0.02 percent.
note: For drivers 21+, it is illegal to operate a vehicle with a BAC of 0.08% or higher.

question: When must you always stop before crossing railroad tracks?
options: a:If there isn't room on the other side for your vehicle to completely clear the tracks.,b:If the crossing is in a city or town with frequent trains.,c:Only if you are carrying two or more children.
note: Never enter tracks if you cannot completely clear them; if you would have to stop on the tracks, wait until the way is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a freeway from an on-ramp you should:
options: a:Signal, yield to existing traffic, and merge at a speed comparable to traffic.,b:Enter slowly and traffic must yield to you.,c:Stop before merging and wait for a large gap.,d:Speed up beyond traffic to force your way in.
note: Use your signal, match the speed of freeway traffic when merging, and yield to vehicles already on the freeway.

question: Orange-colored traffic signs are used to indicate:
options: a:Work zones and construction.,b:Regulatory requirements.,c:School zones.,d:Hospital services.
note: Orange signs and devices in work areas warn drivers about construction and maintenance activity.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In a roundabout who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Drivers already circulating in the roundabout.,b:Drivers entering the roundabout.,c:Drivers intending to go straight across.,d:Pedestrians only.
note: Vehicles entering a roundabout must yield to traffic already in the circle.

question: To help avoid skidding on slippery surfaces, what should you do before entering a curve?
options: a:Slow down before entering curves and intersections.,b:Speed up to enter curves and slow to exit.,c:Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.
note: Reduce speed before a curve so you won't need to brake while turning, which can cause a skid.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When backing up, what should you do to see clearly?
options: a:Look directly through the rear window over your right shoulder.,b:Rely only on your rearview mirror.,c:Press hard on the gas pedal to move quickly.
note: When reversing, turn and look through the rear window and use mirrors as a supplement. Back up slowly and carefully.

question: Which factor affects how alcohol is absorbed by the body?
options: a:Weight,b:Intelligence,c:Height
note: Factors like body weight, biological sex, food intake, and amount consumed affect alcohol absorption; intelligence and height are not relevant.

question: If your accelerator becomes stuck while driving, what is the correct sequence of actions?
options: a:Turn off the ignition using care, apply the brakes, and move off the road when safe.,b:Slam on your brakes.,c:Turn on your four-way flashers and continue driving.
note: If the accelerator sticks, keep steering straight, take your foot off the gas, turn off the ignition (without locking the steering), apply brakes, and steer to a safe location.

question: While passing a row of parked vehicles, you should:
options: a:Be prepared for a person or vehicle to unexpectedly enter your lane.,b:Drive closely to the parked vehicles to make room for moving traffic.,c:Assume pedestrians will wait for you to pass.
note: Keep extra space between you and parked vehicles; a person may exit a vehicle or step out between parked cars unexpectedly.

question: A good driver should monitor which areas around the vehicle?
options: a:Beside, ahead, and to the rear of the vehicle.,b:Only directly in front of the car.,c:Only the middle of the road.
note: A safe driver continually checks side, front, and rear areas to be aware of surrounding hazards.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you, what is the proper action?
options: a:Stop immediately and prevent them from passing.,b:Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path of travel.,c:Speed up to avoid the emergency vehicle.
note: Yield the right-of-way and, if safe, pull to the side to allow emergency vehicles a clear path.

question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:Use your parking lights.,b:Use your low beam headlights.,c:Use your high beam headlights.
note: Use low beams in fog because high beams will reflect back and reduce visibility.

question: Why might a large truck need to swing wide when turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction?
options: a:May complete its turn in either of the two lanes.,b:May have to swing wide to complete the right turn.,c:Must stay in the right lane at all times while turning.
note: Long vehicles have different wheel paths and often need extra space, so trucks may swing wide to avoid clipping the curb or other vehicles.

question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?
options: a:A loss of hearing.,b:Pollution.,c:Carbon monoxide poisoning.
note: A leaking exhaust can allow carbon monoxide into the passenger compartment; repair defects promptly to avoid poisoning.

question: If you experience a sudden tire blowout while driving, how should you react?
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly.,b:Pump the brakes.,c:Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow gradually, and use brakes lightly.
note: Keep control by holding the wheel steady, ease off the gas, and brake gently to slow down before pulling over.

question: If a child is about to run into the street, what emergency action should you take?
options: a:Sound a sharp blast of your horn.,b:Flash your headlights.,c:Start to prepare to slow down slowly.
note: If a child or pedestrian is about to enter the roadway, a sharp blast of the horn may warn them and prevent an accident. Use the horn judiciously to alert them.

question: How is a driver distraction defined?
options: a:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,b:Anything that causes you to focus more on driving.,c:Anything that makes you drive slower.,d:Anything that improves safety.
note: A distraction diverts attention from driving tasks and increases risk of collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you respond to a flashing yellow traffic signal?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop.,c:Speed up to clear the intersection.,d:Turn on hazard lights.
note: A flashing yellow light warns of a hazard — slow down and cross or turn only when it is safe to do so.

question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, what is the best action?
options: a:Stay in your car and wait for help.,b:Get out and walk for help immediately.,c:Lay down and sleep in the car.
note: Remain with your vehicle in a snowstorm; you are more likely to be found and it is safer than walking in severe conditions.

question: What do temporary construction signs look like?
options: a:Orange background with black writing.,b:Red background with white writing.,c:Yellow background with blue writing.,d:Green background with white writing.
note: Work zone signs and devices use orange backgrounds with black letters or symbols to warn drivers.

question: If you drink socially, what helps ensure a safe trip home?
options: a:Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.,b:Drink coffee before driving.,c:Take a cold shower before driving.
note: Riding with someone who has not been drinking or arranging alternative transportation prevents impaired driving. Coffee or showers do not reduce blood alcohol content.

question: If there are two adjacent railroad tracks and one train passes, what should you do?
options: a:It is always safe to proceed after one train passes.,b:You must always stop before crossing the tracks.,c:Look for another train on the other track before proceeding.
note: After one train clears, check carefully for trains on the other track(s) before you cross; never assume it is safe after a single train passes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross a dashed white line?
options: a:When it is safe to change lanes.,b:Only during daylight hours.,c:At any time even if unsafe.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed when it is safe to change lanes.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic signal tell drivers to do?
options: a:Proceed with caution.,b:Stop as if it were a stop sign.,c:Yield to all pedestrians.
note: A flashing yellow signal means slow down, proceed with caution, and be prepared to stop if necessary.

question: Why should you increase your following distance behind a large vehicle?
options: a:To better see around the sides of the vehicle and avoid its blind spots.,b:Because other drivers tend to pull behind large vehicles before passing them.,c:Because following closely will get you caught in the vehicle's slipstream.
note: Large trucks and buses can hide traffic ahead. Increasing following distance helps you see around them and avoid being in their blind spots.

question: Why should you avoid sudden stops in front of large trucks and buses?
options: a:Because they require much longer distances to stop due to their size and weight.,b:Because small vehicle drivers cannot see trucks in their mirrors.,c:Because large trucks always travel at higher speeds.
note: Large vehicles need more time and distance to stop; sudden stops in front of them risk rear-end collisions.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or hear a siren, what must you do?
options: a:Pull to the right curb or edge of the road and stop.,b:Slow down and keep moving in your lane.,c:Keep driving in your lane without stopping.
note: You must immediately yield to emergency vehicles by pulling over to the right and stopping until they pass.

question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, you must:
options: a:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.,b:Slow down and continue driving in lane.,c:Turn on your hazard lights and keep going.,d:Speed up to get out of the way.
note: You must pull over to the curb or side of the road and stop to let emergency vehicles pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a divided multilane highway, if you see or hear an approaching emergency vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down, move to provide a clear path for the emergency vehicle, and stop if necessary.,b:Stop as quickly as you can in your lane.,c:Disregard the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.
note: Move over or slow down to give emergency vehicles a clear path; do not attempt to outdrive them.

question: What is the proper top-to-bottom order for traffic signal lights?
options: a:Red, yellow, green.,b:Red, green, yellow.,c:Green, red, yellow.
note: Traffic signals are vertically arranged with red on top, yellow in the middle, and green at the bottom.

question: What is defensive driving?
options: a:Identifying dangerous situations and taking action to avoid crashes.,b:Advancing ahead of slow drivers to protect yourself.,c:Following the vehicle ahead closely to block others.
note: Defensive driving means anticipating hazards and taking steps to avoid conflicts and collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Exiting the freeway onto a downhill, curving ramp, what should you do?
options: a:Slow to a safe speed before entering the curve.,b:Begin braking once you are in the curve.,c:Maintain freeway speed while on the ramp.
note: Slow down before entering a curved exit ramp; braking in a curve can cause skidding and loss of control.

question: What color are signs that indicate areas of public recreation or cultural interest?
options: a:Brown.,b:Green.,c:Red.
note: Brown signs identify cultural, historical, and recreation areas; they help direct travelers to parks and recreation sites.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:Whenever anything makes driving conditions less than perfect.,b:Only when you see a police car.,c:Only when entering a highway with other cars.
note: Drive slower than the posted limit when conditions (weather, visibility, road surface) make the posted speed unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a 'Merging traffic' sign on the freeway, what is the appropriate action?
options: a:Make room for entering vehicles by changing lanes or adjusting speed when safe.,b:Always remain at your current speed.,c:Honk at incoming traffic to warn them away.
note: Create space for merging vehicles by moving over a lane or adjusting speed when safe to do so to maintain traffic flow and safety.

question: What does BAC stand for?
options: a:Blood alcohol concentration.,b:Basic alcohol content.,c:Blood alcohol capacity.,d:Body alcohol count.
note: Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in a person's bloodstream and indicates impairment level.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to emergency vehicles?
options: a:When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.,b:Only when other vehicles yield first.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: You must yield the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle that is using its siren or flashing lights.

question: As alcohol accumulates in your blood, it:
options: a:Slows your reactions and increases confidence, leading to more errors.,b:Speeds up your reactions.,c:Improves eyesight.,d:Reduces risk-taking behavior.
note: Alcohol slows reaction times and can make drivers overconfident, increasing the likelihood of mistakes.

question: What does a single broken white centerline allow you to do?
options: a:You must stay within your lane.,b:You may cross the centerline to change lanes.,c:You may change lanes only from the left lane.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to change lanes or pass when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which factors affect braking distance?
options: a:The speed your vehicle is traveling.,b:The condition of your brakes and tires.,c:The condition of the pavement.,d:All of the above
note: Braking distance depends on speed, brake and tire condition, pavement condition, and other factors like weather and vehicle weight.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your freeway exit, what should you do?
options: a:Continue to the next exit and leave there.,b:Make a U-turn through the median.,c:Back up or stop on the highway to return to the exit.
note: If you miss an exit, take the next one. Do not stop, back up, or attempt unsafe maneuvers on the freeway.

question: Why does driving at night require increased caution?
options: a:Because drivers cannot see as well at night.,b:Because traffic volume is higher at night.,c:Because roadways are always more slippery at night.
note: Reduced visibility at night makes it harder to see hazards; use headlights and reduce speed appropriately.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To enter a gap in highway traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.,b:Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.,c:Speed up and let the other vehicles make way.
note: When entering traffic, check to the side and behind, then watch the vehicle ahead to ensure the gap is large enough for you to merge safely.

question: Before entering a roundabout, you must yield to which road users?
options: a:Vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians already in the roundabout.,b:Only pedestrians.,c:Only bicyclists.
note: Yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already circulating in the roundabout before entering.

question: The blind spot behind a large truck can extend about how far behind the truck's cab?
options: a:200 feet.,b:100 feet.,c:80 feet.
note: Large trucks have significant blind spots, including a large zone directly behind the vehicle that can extend up to around 200 feet.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, when should you move back into the right (driving) lane?
options: a:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your inside rearview mirror.,b:When you are one vehicle length ahead of the passed vehicle.,c:After signaling for three seconds.
note: Return to the driving lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, indicating a safe gap.

question: Why must you use extra caution when driving near a pedestrian with a white cane?
options: a:He or she is deaf.,b:He or she is a police officer.,c:He or she is blind.
note: A white cane or guide dog indicates a blind or visually impaired pedestrian; yield and be prepared to stop to allow them to cross safely.

question: Which of these correctly describes the slow-moving vehicle emblem?
options: a:A reflective orange triangle.,b:A rectangular red sign.,c:A circular green sign.
note: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a highly reflective orange triangle; it warns that the vehicle usually travels 25 mph or less.

question: What is commonly used on some highways to direct drivers into proper turning lanes?
options: a:Arrows painted on the roadway or signs showing lane use.,b:Flashing red lights.,c:White lines on the side of the road only.
note: Arrows (painted or on signs) indicate which lane you must use for turning or continuing straight.

question: Which behavior blocks the smooth flow of traffic?
options: a:Slowing down to look at a collision or unusual event (rubbernecking).,b:Using public transportation instead of driving.,c:Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.
note: Rubbernecking—slowing to look at collisions or other distractions—causes congestion and should be avoided.

question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light require you to do?
options: a:Stop and then proceed when the signal changes to green or a green arrow.,b:Stop and then proceed when it is clear.,c:Proceed slowly through the intersection.
note: A red arrow means stop and remain stopped until a green light or green arrow appears (unless signs indicate otherwise).

question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, what should you do?
options: a:Get out of their way and avoid confrontation.,b:Challenge them.,c:Speed up to match their behavior.
note: The safest response to aggressive driving is to get out of the way; avoid competition or retaliation.

question: If you're involved in a serious motor vehicle crash, what is your first action?
options: a:Call the police.,b:Determine whether anyone is injured.,c:Stop your vehicle.
note: Stop your vehicle if possible and move it off the roadway. If anyone is injured call 911 and provide assistance. You must report crashes to law enforcement when there is an injury, death, or more than $1,000 in property damage (or over $200 in damage to government property).

question: When preparing to enter a freeway, how should you check traffic on the freeway?
options: a:Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder in addition to mirrors.,b:Use only your rearview mirror.,c:Use only your side mirrors.
note: Use mirrors and a shoulder check to confirm lane position and blind spots before merging onto freeway traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before making a left turn, the driver should:
options: a:Yield to oncoming vehicles.,b:Swing to the right side of your lane.,c:Sound your horn.
note: Yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic when making a left turn; only turn when it is safe to do so.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:Another vehicle is in your way.,b:It may help prevent a collision.,c:Another driver makes a mistake.
note: Use your horn only to warn others of danger or to help prevent a collision; avoid using it to express frustration.

question: Drivers who have consumed alcohol before driving:
options: a:Do not have sufficient control over their bodies or vehicles.,b:Are always aware of the risks they are taking.,c:Become better drivers because they are more careful.
note: Alcohol impairs judgement, vision, concentration, and reaction time; drivers under the influence cannot control their vehicles as well.

question: Regarding small children riding in vehicles, which statement is correct?
options: a:Children must be secured in appropriate child seats or restraints; holding them by an adult is not safe.,b:Children are safe if standing in the back of a vehicle.,c:Small size prevents children from being hurt in a crash.
note: Children who are too small for regular safety belts must use approved child seats. No adult can safely hold a child during a crash or sudden stop.

question: If visibility is very poor due to fog, you should slow down and:
options: a:Switch your headlights to the low beam setting.,b:Turn on your emergency flashers.,c:Use your high beam headlights to improve vision.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow; high beams reflect off precipitation and worsen visibility. Use fog lights if the vehicle has them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, which action should you never do?
options: a:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.,b:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.,c:Move into another lane while within an intersection.
note: Never change lanes while inside an intersection. Always check mirrors, signal, and glance over your shoulder for blind spots before moving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should drivers treat a flashing red traffic light?
options: a:Treat it the same as a stop sign: stop, then proceed when safe.,b:Drive through if there is no crossing traffic.,c:Continue driving because you have the right-of-way.
note: A flashing red light requires a complete stop, then proceed only when it is safe, just like a stop sign.

question: Why should you not use high-beam headlights in fog or mist?
options: a:The light will reflect back into your eyes.,b:Vehicles behind you will not see you.,c:It improves visibility too much and blinds other drivers.
note: High beams reflect off fog and mist back toward the driver, reducing visibility. Use low beams in foggy conditions.

question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line indicate about passing?
options: a:Permitted from the side next to the solid yellow line.,b:Not permitted from either direction.,c:Permitted from the side next to the broken yellow line.
note: If the centerline is a broken yellow next to a solid yellow, passing is allowed from the side with the broken line and prohibited from the side with the solid line.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a green arrow changes to a steady green light, what must you do when turning?
options: a:You may turn but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:You may no longer turn and must go straight.,c:You retain the exclusive right-of-way to turn.
note: When a green arrow ends and a steady green remains, you may still turn but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

question: In fog, rain, or snow, which headlights setting should you use?
options: a:Low beams.,b:High beams.,c:Fog lights only.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, and snow; high beams reflect back and impair your vision in these conditions.

question: If it begins to sleet or snow while you're driving, what should you do?
options: a:Allow extra following distance between you and the vehicle ahead.,b:Approach other vehicles with the same caution as in clear weather.,c:Keep your windshield and mirrors cleared only when stopped.
note: Increase your following distance and keep your windshield and mirrors clear. Reduced traction increases stopping distances in snow or sleet.

question: Which method checks the blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Using your side mirror.,b:Using the inside rearview mirror.,c:Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.
note: Even with properly adjusted mirrors there are blind spots you cannot see; look over your shoulder before changing lanes to check them.

question: If there are oncoming cars to your left and parked vehicles to your right, how should you steer?
options: a:Keep a middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.,b:Steer closer to the oncoming vehicles than to the parked vehicles.,c:Steer closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.
note: When faced with moving traffic on one side and parked cars on the other, steer centrally between them to maximize clearance.

question: When the center of the road has a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line and the broken line is next to your lane, you may:
options: a:Only in an emergency.,b:If you are on an expressway.,c:Pass if traffic is clear.
note: If the broken yellow line is on your side, you may pass when it is safe and no oncoming traffic is present.

question: What does a flashing yellow light at an intersection indicate?
options: a:Caution—slow down and proceed with care.,b:Continue normally without slowing.,c:Stop and wait for a green light.
note: A flashing yellow light advises drivers to slow down and proceed carefully; it does not require a stop unless necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you must slow or stop where others may not expect it, how should you warn drivers behind you?
options: a:Tap your brake pedal quickly several times.,b:Wave your left arm out the window.,c:Sound your horn continuously.
note: If you will slow or stop unexpectedly, tap the brake pedal 3–4 times so your brake lights warn drivers behind you.

question: After a minor, no-injury intersection collision with little damage, what should you do if possible?
options: a:Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until law enforcement arrives.,b:Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane to a safe location.,c:Never move your vehicle for any reason.
note: If no one is injured and it is safe to do so, move vehicles out of traffic lanes to avoid blocking traffic and reducing risk.

question: How can you help keep the driver behind you a safe distance away?
options: a:Maintain a steady speed and signal intentions in advance.,b:Suddenly slow to create space.,c:Drive 10 mph faster than the car behind you.
note: A steady speed and timely signaling help the driver behind maintain a safe following distance.

question: Seat belts are most effective when worn by whom?
options: a:All occupants in the vehicle.,b:The driver only.,c:Passengers only on long trips.
note: Every occupant should wear a seat belt; unbelted passengers can become projectiles in a crash and harm others.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When do you have the right-of-way to turn left?
options: a:When a green arrow is pointing left.,b:When the light is a steady green circle.,c:When a flashing yellow arrow is displayed.,d:Always when turning from the left lane.
note: A steady green arrow for left turns gives you protected turning movement; oncoming traffic must stop for you.

question: If you must slow down on a slippery road, what should you do first?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas pedal.,b:Apply the parking brake.,c:Firmly apply your brakes.
note: To reduce speed on slippery pavement, first remove your foot from the accelerator. If more slowing is needed, apply the brake gently and steadily. Do not use abrupt braking or steering.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left, to whom must drivers yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Oncoming traffic (and any pedestrians in the intersection).,b:Other drivers who are already in the intersection.,c:Pedestrians only.
note: When making a left turn you must yield to oncoming vehicles and to pedestrians or bicyclists in the intersection.

question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line indicate?
options: a:Passing is allowed from the lane next to the broken line.,b:Passing is allowed from the lane next to the solid line.,c:Passing is permitted from either lane.
note: A broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line means drivers on the side with the broken line may pass when safe; the solid-line side may not pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When leaving an alley, driveway, or parking lot and crossing a sidewalk, what must you do?
options: a:Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.,b:Stop before driving onto the sidewalk or sidewalk area.,c:Expect pedestrians on the sidewalk to yield the right-of-way.
note: You must stop before entering a sidewalk area to yield to pedestrians before driving onto the road.

question: At dusk or on overcast days, what should you do about your vehicle lights?
options: a:Turn on your headlights.,b:Use only your parking lights.,c:Use your four-way flashers while driving.
note: You must turn on headlights at dusk or during overcast conditions; dim to low beams when within 1,000 feet of an approaching vehicle or 500 feet of a vehicle you are following.

question: If you notice a vehicle defect affecting safe operation, you should:
options: a:Have the defect corrected as soon as possible before driving.,b:Only fix the problem when you can afford it.,c:Drive more slowly and ignore it.
note: Repair any defects that could impair safe operation promptly; do not drive a vehicle with a safety-related defect.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking next to a curb, when should you use your turn signal?
options: a:When pulling next to or away from the curb.,b:Only when pulling away from the curb.,c:Only when pulling next to the curb.,d:Never during curb maneuvers.
note: Signal both when approaching a curb to park and when leaving the curb to alert other road users to your intent.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these is a correct passing practice?
options: a:Use mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check the blind spot when passing to the left.,b:Only signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes.,c:Return to your lane immediately after passing without checking.
note: When passing to the left, signal in advance, check mirrors, and glance over your left shoulder to check the blind spot; return when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your mirror.

question: When roads are snowy or icy, you should:
options: a:Use your cruise control.,b:Make speed and directional changes more gradually than you would otherwise.,c:Drive as you would under normal conditions.
note: On snow or ice, make gradual speed and steering changes and never use cruise control to reduce the risk of losing control.

question: When driving on the highway, consistently looking far ahead helps you:
options: a:Reduce the need for last-minute braking or turning.,b:Spot police officers to avoid a ticket.,c:Keep up with the speed of traffic.
note: Scanning well ahead gives time to react to changing traffic, smooth maneuvers, and helps maintain steady traffic flow.

question: Lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions are divided by what color lines?
options: a:Yellow.,b:Red.,c:Black.
note: Yellow lines are used to separate traffic moving in opposite directions; white lines separate same-direction lanes.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:Both at night and when it is raining.,b:Only at night.,c:Only when it is raining.
note: Increase your following distance in conditions that reduce visibility or traction, such as darkness or rain; a four-second rule is a good baseline for ideal conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to pass another vehicle, when should you signal?
options: a:Signal early enough for other drivers to know your intentions.,b:Signal only if there is visible traffic behind you.,c:Signal just after you begin changing lanes.
note: Signal in advance before passing so other drivers have time to respond to your maneuver.

question: As daylight fades, which lights should you use to help others see your vehicle?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:Parking lights.,c:Emergency flashers.
note: Turn on low beam headlights as visibility decreases; reserve high beams for open roads without other traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How does vehicle speed affect stopping distance and crash severity?
options: a:Stopping distance and crash severity increase as speed increases.,b:Stopping distance and crash severity decrease as speed increases.,c:Speed has no effect on stopping distance or crash severity.
note: Higher speeds increase stopping distances and the force of impact in collisions, raising the risk of serious injury or death.

question: At a school crossing sign, how should you proceed?
options: a:Always stop, whether there’s a stop sign or not.,b:Watch for children and be ready to stop.,c:Always sound your horn when you see children.
note: At school crossings be alert for children and be prepared to stop; always yield to pedestrians in crosswalks.

question: If your car stalls or breaks down on the highway, you should:
options: a:Use your four-way flashers and move off the road as far as possible.,b:Sound your horn at passing motorists.,c:Sit in your car and wait for help without signaling.
