note: Signal, get the vehicle off the road when possible, turn on hazard flashers, and make your vehicle visible to others.

question: On slippery roads, what should you do?
options: a:Use alternate routes.,b:Drive as you would on dry roads.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: Increase your following distance on slippery roads because it takes longer to stop and traction is reduced.

question: If you're angry after an argument, what is the safest action before driving?
options: a:Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.,b:Loudly play the radio to distract yourself.,c:Drive on the interstate to 'let off steam.'
note: Strong emotions impair driving ability; give yourself time to calm so you can focus on driving safely.

question: When approaching an accident scene, what is the appropriate action?
options: a:Keep moving.,b:Stop if you are involved or if emergency help has not yet arrived.,c:Keep your attention on your driving.
note: Do not stop at an accident scene unless you are involved or emergency help has not yet arrived. If you must stop, do so safely and offer assistance if appropriate.

question: What is a crosswalk?
options: a:The area designated for pedestrians to cross the roadway.,b:Another name for a four-way intersection.,c:An area only used by road construction workers.
note: A crosswalk marks where pedestrians have the right to cross; it may be marked or unmarked at intersections.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before passing another vehicle?
options: a:Check your mirrors and blind spots.,b:Re-enter your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.,c:Honk your horn at least three times.
note: Before passing, check mirrors and blind spots, signal, and only move back into the lane when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?
options: a:Motorcycles can stop more quickly than cars, so close following leaves insufficient time to react.,b:Motorcycles brake more slowly than cars.,c:Motorcyclists do not follow the same rules as cars.
note: Motorcycles can stop quickly; following too closely reduces your ability to avoid a crash if they brake suddenly.

question: After stopping for a passing train, what should you do before proceeding?
options: a:Look for a second train and wait until signals and gates are clear.,b:Proceed as soon as the first train passes.,c:Wait only for the gates to begin to lift before you go.
note: Even after a train passes, check for a second train on other tracks and do not go until gates are up and warning signals have stopped.

question: What helps someone sober up after drinking alcohol?
options: a:Nothing but time will remove alcohol's effects.,b:Drinking tomato juice and lime.,c:Drinking hot coffee.
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize alcohol; foods, coffee, or fresh air do not speed sobriety.

question: Which statement best describes backing your vehicle?
options: a:Always dangerous.,b:Dangerous if you have a helper.,c:Only dangerous in large vehicles.
note: Backing is inherently risky because visibility is limited; use caution and helpers if necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you're waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection and oncoming traffic blocks your view, what is the safe action?
options: a:Accelerate rapidly when the first lane you need to cross is clear.,b:Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across the intersection.,c:Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross before making the turn.
note: Never begin a left turn until you can see that all lanes you must cross are clear and you can safely complete the turn.

question: Why is driving at night more hazardous than daytime driving?
options: a:You cannot see as far ahead at night.,b:Roads are always more slippery at night.,c:Your reaction time is slower at night.,d:Headlights make objects appear closer.
note: Reduced visibility and glare from oncoming headlights limit how far ahead you can see; use caution and proper lighting at night.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A posted speed limit indicates:
options: a:The maximum or minimum legal speed under ideal conditions.,b:The suggested speed under ideal conditions.,c:The maximum safe speed under all conditions.
note: Speed limits indicate the maximum (or minimum) legal speeds under ideal conditions. You must reduce speed when conditions are unsafe.

question: When you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, what must you do?
options: a:Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead and reduce speed.,b:Change lanes and maintain your current speed.,c:Increase speed to pass the work zone quickly.
note: Work zones warn of workers and changing traffic patterns. Slow down, be alert, and be prepared to stop or change lanes safely.

question: When passing a large vehicle, what should drivers of small vehicles be prepared for?
options: a:Loud noises.,b:Wind gusts that can affect vehicle direction.,c:Excess air pollution.
note: Large vehicles can create strong air turbulence that may push smaller vehicles; be ready to correct steering.

question: If you are already inside an intersection when a green light changes to yellow, what should you do?
options: a:Continue moving and clear the intersection safely.,b:Stop immediately in the intersection.,c:Increase your speed to get out quickly.
note: If already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through and clear it as quickly and safely as possible.

question: If you must make an emergency stop, what should you do?
options: a:Turn on emergency flashers and stay in your vehicle if it is safe to do so.,b:Get out immediately and walk to seek help.,c:Blow your horn at passing cars to alert them.
note: When stopping for vehicle trouble, move off the road if possible, use hazard flashers, and remain inside the vehicle to stay safe from traffic.

question: If the centerline has one solid yellow and one broken yellow line and the broken line is next to your lane, what does this mean?
options: a:You are allowed to pass from your lane if it is safe.,b:You are not allowed to pass in this area.,c:You are only allowed to make right turns in this area.
note: When the broken line is next to your lane, you may pass other vehicles if it can be done safely and without interfering with oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection, what is the proper action?
options: a:Yield to vehicles approaching from your right and be prepared to stop.,b:Maintain your speed and proceed.,c:Always come to a full stop before proceeding.
note: At intersections without signs or signals, yield to vehicles coming from the right and be prepared to stop to avoid a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct action at a yield sign before entering another roadway?
options: a:Only yield to traffic on your right.,b:Slow down and yield to traffic in the road you are entering.,c:Always come to a complete stop before entering the intersection.
note: A yield sign means you must slow down and yield the right-of-way to vehicles and pedestrians in the roadway you are entering; stop only if necessary for safety.

question: What is the only thing that can reduce blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Drinking caffeine,b:Eating foods high in fat,c:Time
note: Only the passage of time allows the body to metabolize and remove alcohol; coffee, food, or exercise will not lower BAC.

question: At night, which road user is hardest to see?
options: a:Pedestrians.,b:Road signs.,c:Other motorists.
note: Pedestrians are especially difficult to see at night compared to signs or other vehicles; reduce speed and be vigilant.

question: When another vehicle is passing you, you should:
options: a:Maintain a constant speed and allow the pass.,b:Brake hard.,c:Speed up to block the pass.
note: Yield to the passing vehicle and avoid increasing your speed until it has safely re-entered your lane.

question: On a two-lane road without bicycle lanes, what is the safest way to pass a bicyclist traveling in your direction?
options: a:Continue driving straight; the bicyclist should get out of your way.,b:Slow down and wait until there is no traffic approaching, then pass leaving sufficient space.,c:Do not pass until you come to a traffic signal or stop sign.
note: Pass bicyclists as you would other vehicles but allow extra space (at least 3 feet) and only pass when it is safe and clear of oncoming traffic.

question: What is the safest way to pass a bicyclist?
options: a:Slow down and give the bicyclist as much space as possible.,b:Drive partially into the bicycle lane until you can pass.,c:Honk to alert the bicyclist you are about to pass.
note: When passing a bicyclist, reduce speed and allow as much lateral space as possible; bicyclists are vulnerable and can be shifted by sudden airflow.

question: Who must you give the right-of-way to?
options: a:Any pedestrian crossing in a marked crosswalk or in any crosswalk at an intersection.,b:Only pedestrians at marked crosswalks.,c:No one crossing the street.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in marked or unmarked crosswalks and should yield when anyone is crossing a street for safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To avoid traffic merging from on-ramps on your right while on an interstate, what is the best action when safe?
options: a:Move to the left lane.,b:Reduce your speed.,c:Maintain your lane and speed.
note: When traffic allows, move out of the right lane to let vehicles merge from on-ramps to your right.

question: If a tire blows out while driving, what steering and speed control technique should you use?
options: a:Brake hard immediately.,b:Try to steer straight while gradually slowing by removing your foot from the gas pedal.,c:Maintain your current speed and steer straight.
note: Hold the wheel steady, ease off the gas to slow gradually, and avoid braking until you have control; then brake gently and pull over.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a flashing red light, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield, then proceed when safe.,b:Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.,c:Stop and remain stopped until the light turns green.
note: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign: stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic is merging into your freeway lane, what should you do?
options: a:Make room for merging vehicles when safe.,b:Assert your right-of-way by speeding up.,c:Maintain your exact position at all costs.,d:Brake suddenly to discourage merging.
note: When traffic allows, adjust your speed or change lanes safely to allow others to merge.

question: When you approach a stopped school bus with lights flashing and arm extended, you must:
options: a:Stop and remain stopped until the arm is withdrawn and the bus moves.,b:Proceed at 15 mph if you don't see children.,c:Slow down and proceed carefully.
note: If a school bus displays flashing red lights and its stop arm is extended, all drivers must stop until the bus resumes motion and the arm is retracted.

question: At a school crossing sign, what should you do?
options: a:Watch for children and be prepared to stop.,b:Always come to a complete stop whether posted or not.,c:Sound your horn to alert children.,d:Keep your speed constant.
note: Pentagonal school signs warn you to be alert for children and prepared to stop for school crossings.

question: Why is extra space in front of a large truck needed?
options: a:Other drivers to merge onto the freeway.,b:The truck driver to stop the vehicle.,c:Other drivers when they want to slow down.
note: Large trucks require more stopping distance than cars; avoid pulling too closely in front of trucks because they need extra room to stop.

question: When sharing the roadway with a truck, what is important to remember?
options: a:Trucks require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.,b:Trucks need less time to pass on downgrades.,c:Trucks have a smaller turning radius than cars.
note: Because of their size and weight, trucks need much more distance to stop than passenger vehicles.

question: How is distracted driving best described?
options: a:Extremely risky behavior that endangers drivers, passengers, pedestrians, and bicyclists.,b:Very uncommon among drivers.,c:Not a serious concern.
note: Distracted driving diverts attention from driving tasks and greatly increases the risk of crashes; it is a serious hazard.

question: If you see animals standing near the roadway, you should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Speed up to pass before they move.,c:Swerve suddenly into the next lane.
note: Animals may bolt into the road; slow down and be prepared to stop safely rather than swerving suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit sign indicate?
options: a:Only a recommended driving speed.,b:The exact speed at which you must travel to avoid a ticket.,c:The maximum safe driving speed under ideal road and weather conditions.
note: A speed limit sign shows the maximum legal speed under ideal conditions; you may need to drive slower when conditions are hazardous.

question: A flashing red traffic signal at an intersection has the same requirement as what sign?
options: a:A stop sign.,b:A yield sign.,c:A slow sign.
note: A flashing red signal requires a full stop and the same yielding rules as a stop sign.

question: What is the purpose of a yellow and black diamond-shaped sign?
options: a:To warn about conditions on or near the road ahead.,b:To direct you to towns and cities.,c:To state traffic laws and regulations.
note: Diamond-shaped yellow/black signs are warning signs that alert drivers to hazards or changes in the road ahead.

question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?
options: a:It lets other road users know your intentions.,b:It is always unsafe to turn off a signal before completing a turn.,c:It is illegal to turn off your signal before finishing the turn.
note: Keeping the signal on during the turn communicates your intentions to drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When an emergency vehicle using lights and/or siren approaches, you must immediately:
options: a:Pull to the right and stop.,b:Pull to the right and slow down but remain moving.,c:Turn on your four-way flashers and continue driving.
note: When approached by an emergency vehicle, move to the right edge of the roadway and stop to allow it to pass.

question: If you leave your vehicle unattended you must:
options: a:Turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.,b:Only set the parking brake.,c:Leave the engine running for a short time.,d:Leave the door unlocked for emergency access.
note: When leaving your vehicle unattended, always stop the engine, remove keys, lock the ignition, and set the parking brake.

question: Parking downhill on a two-way street, how should you position the wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels toward the curb (right).,b:Keep the wheels straight ahead.,c:Turn the wheels to the left away from the curb.
note: On a downhill slope, turn the front wheels toward the curb so the vehicle will roll into the curb rather than into traffic if it moves.

question: If someone is injured in a crash, what should you do regarding moving them?
options: a:Do not move the injured unless necessary; keep them warm and give first aid.,b:Move the injured immediately away from the scene.,c:Always leave the injured where they are without aid.,d:Drive them to a hospital yourself even if moving them might harm them.
note: Unnecessary movement can worsen injuries. Keep injured people warm and provide first aid; move only if there is immediate danger.

question: In poor weather conditions, what should drivers do regarding following distance?
options: a:Increase their speed to reach their destination more quickly.,b:Decrease their following distance.,c:Increase their following distance.
note: When roads are wet or visibility is reduced, increase your following distance so you have more time to react and stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it acceptable to drive on the shoulder to pass another vehicle?
options: a:If the vehicle ahead of you is turning left.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:If the shoulder is wide enough.
note: Never pass another vehicle by driving on the shoulder; it is unsafe and typically illegal.

question: When backing up, you should drive at no faster than:
options: a:A slow crawl.,b:A slow jog.,c:A normal driving speed.
note: Back up slowly, at roughly the speed of a slow walk, because vehicles are harder to control in reverse.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you enter a roundabout, you must slow down and:
options: a:Yield to any car already within the roundabout.,b:Yield to any crossing pedestrians and bicyclists.,c:Both of the above.
note: When entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and any traffic already circulating in the roundabout.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you on a two-lane, two-way road, what should you do?
options: a:Not let other cars pass your vehicle.,b:Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.,c:Decrease your speed further.
note: If you are impeding traffic on a two-way road, pull off when safe and allow other vehicles to pass.

question: When stopped by police for a violation or equipment check, what must the driver produce?
options: a:Driver license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance.,b:Only proof of registration.,c:Only proof of insurance.
note: Drivers must present their license, vehicle registration, and proof of insurance when stopped for a traffic violation or inspection.

question: What is the best way to avoid a dangerous driving situation?
options: a:Be aware of what is happening around your vehicle.,b:Turn off the radio and focus only ahead.,c:Keep your eyes fixed straight ahead at all times.
note: Constantly scan your surroundings—front, sides, and rear—to detect hazards early and adjust speed or position accordingly.

question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:Human error.,b:New drivers.,c:Bad weather.
note: Most crashes result from human error, such as failing to see other vehicles or misjudging situations.

question: What does a flashing red traffic light at an intersection mean?
options: a:The same as a yield sign.,b:The same as a stop sign.,c:The light is about to turn green.
note: A flashing red light requires you to stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when safe — same as a stop sign.

question: Why are roads especially slippery when it first starts to rain?
options: a:Because oil and residue make the surface slick; avoid fast turns and stops.,b:Because tire traction improves temporarily.,c:Because it is safer to test tires' traction uphill.
note: When rain first begins, oil and residue on the pavement reduce traction — slow down and avoid abrupt maneuvers.

question: On the freeway, why should you look farther ahead than on city streets?
options: a:To see potential hazards early and prepare for changes in traffic.,b:Because it takes a quarter mile to stop completely.,c:Because it helps you keep up with traffic speed.
note: On high-speed roads, scanning farther ahead lets you spot hazards and react early, reducing sudden braking or lane changes.

question: At what speed should you travel?
options: a:At a speed appropriate for road and weather conditions and within posted limits.,b:Always at the posted speed limit regardless of conditions.,c:At the speed of vehicles surrounding you even if over the limit.
note: Drive at a safe speed for current conditions and never exceed the posted maximum limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles reach an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle approaching from the right.,b:The vehicle approaching from the left.,c:The vehicle whose driver honks first.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection of similar roads, yield to a vehicle approaching from your right; that vehicle has the right-of-way.

question: What are "no zones" around large trucks?
options: a:Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or limit the truck's ability to stop and maneuver.,b:Areas where cars have extra space to pass safely.,c:Places where a truck must always stop.,d:Designated parking zones for trucks.
note: No-zones are truck blind spots or areas so close that they limit a truck driver's ability to react; avoid lingering in these spaces.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching a steady green traffic light, what should you do?
options: a:Proceed if the intersection is clear, yielding to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.,b:Treat it like a four-way stop.,c:Stop if a police officer is nearby.
note: A steady green allows you to go if the intersection is clear; yield to pedestrians and any vehicles already in the intersection.

question: When must vehicles remain stopped behind a school bus with red lights flashing?
options: a:Until the stop arm is withdrawn and the bus starts moving again.,b:Until all students are off the bus.,c:Until the stop arm is retracted.
note: When a school bus has red lights flashing and its stop arm extended, drivers must stop until the lights turn off, the stop arm is withdrawn, and the bus resumes motion.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are stopped in a line at a stop sign and the intersection clears after the vehicles ahead go, what must you do?
options: a:May proceed through the intersection without stopping again.,b:Must stop again at the stop sign or stop line before proceeding.,c:May slowly roll past the stop sign.
note: Always come to a complete stop at a stop sign at the stop line or before the crosswalk, even if the vehicles ahead have moved through the intersection.

question: How should you treat all railroad crossings?
options: a:Dangerous; always look and listen for trains.,b:Safe to cross most of the time.,c:Only dangerous when signals are flashing.,d:A good place to stop and wait.
note: Railroad crossings can be hazardous; always look and listen for approaching trains and obey signals and gates.

question: If another car is in danger of hitting you, what should you do immediately?
options: a:Wave your arms.,b:Sound your horn.,c:Use your emergency lights.
note: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians if you think a collision is imminent.

question: What are construction zone signs normally shaped and colored?
options: a:Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black.,b:Round or octagonal with black and yellow.,c:Square or rectangular with white and red coloring.
note: Temporary work zone signs have an orange background with black letters or symbols and are often diamond-shaped or rectangular.

question: If an oncoming vehicle's headlights are blinding you, you should:
options: a:Look toward the right edge of the road and slow down.,b:Flash your lights at the other driver.,c:Use your high beams until they dim theirs.,d:Stare straight ahead to avoid missing signs.
note: Look away from bright high beams toward the right side of the road until the vehicle passes to avoid being blinded.

question: If weather or light conditions require lights, which should you use in fog, snow, or heavy rain?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:Parking lights.,c:High beams.
note: Use low beam headlights in foggy, snowy, or rainy conditions because high beams can reflect back and worsen visibility.

question: What do work zone signs indicate?
options: a:It is summer.,b:You must immediately stop and back up.,c:Less than ideal conditions are present for driving.
note: Work zone signs (orange) warn that road work is taking place and that conditions may be hazardous; slow down and be alert.

question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn where you also need to turn right, what should you do?
options: a:Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn before you turn.,b:Quickly turn before the larger vehicle.,c:Squeeze between the vehicle and the curb to complete your turn.
note: Large vehicles may need extra room to turn; wait until they finish the turn rather than trying to cut between them and the curb.

question: If your car begins skidding out of control, what should you avoid?
options: a:Using the brakes heavily; stay off the brakes.,b:Applying car brakes lightly.,c:Pump the brakes rapidly.
note: During a skid, avoid heavy braking; concentrate on steering to regain control and avoid further destabilizing the vehicle.

question: Why is maintaining a space cushion around your vehicle important?
options: a:It allows you time to react to unexpected situations.,b:It prevents distractions from other vehicles.,c:It keeps traffic flowing faster.
note: Leaving space around your vehicle gives you time to see hazards and react safely when others make mistakes.

question: If you see pedestrians near the roadway, you should:
options: a:Slow down and pass with caution.,b:Sound your horn and maintain speed.,c:Speed up to clear the area quickly.,d:Drive in the shoulder to avoid them.
note: Slow down, be prepared to stop, and pass carefully when pedestrians are near the road.

question: What does a yellow left-turn arrow mean?
options: a:The protected left turn is ending and drivers must prepare to yield.,b:Drivers must accelerate to complete the turn.,c:Drivers should prepare to yield to oncoming traffic only if turning right.
note: A yellow left arrow warns that the protected left-turn phase is ending and drivers must prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.

question: What happens when you take drugs together with alcohol?
options: a:The risk of causing a crash increases.,b:It is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.,c:It reduces alcohol's effect.,d:It prevents impairment.
note: Combining alcohol with prescription, over-the-counter, or illegal drugs typically increases impairment and crash risk.

question: What do orange-colored road signs typically indicate?
options: a:Construction, maintenance, or emergency operations ahead.,b:A school zone is ahead.,c:A railroad crossing is ahead.
note: Orange signs warn drivers of construction, maintenance, and emergency operations; they are usually orange with black symbols.

question: Which skill is affected first by alcohol?
options: a:Balance.,b:Vision.,c:Judgment.
note: Alcohol is absorbed into the bloodstream and affects brain areas that control judgment and skill, often impairing judgment before other abilities.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to exceed the posted speed limit?
options: a:Never.,b:When passing another vehicle.,c:When there is no traffic in your lane.
note: It is illegal to drive above the posted speed limit under any normal circumstance, including passing.

question: What helps reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Allowing extra travel time.,b:Driving faster than other traffic.,c:Refusing to use turn signals.,d:Tailgating slower vehicles.
note: Planning and allowing extra travel time reduces stress and the chance of aggressive encounters on the road.

question: At night when an oncoming vehicle approaches, which headlight setting should you use?
options: a:Should be on their high beam setting.,b:Should be on their low beam setting.,c:Should be off. Use your parking lights.
note: Do not use high beams when approaching or following other vehicles; switch to low beam to avoid blinding other drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a road with two lanes going the same direction, which lane should you use?
options: a:The right lane except to pass.,b:The left lane to avoid vehicles entering from the right.,c:The left lane at all times.
note: On two-lane roads with traffic moving the same way, stay in the right lane unless passing or preparing for a left turn.

question: When backing up, what is the safest method?
options: a:Turn and look through the rear window while backing.,b:Rely only on your mirrors.,c:Open your door to see if it is safe to proceed.
note: When reversing, look over your shoulder through the rear window and do not depend solely on mirrors or sensors.

question: When must you yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Only when the guide dog is leading them across the street.,b:At all times.,c:Only if a crossing guard is present.
note: Pedestrians who use white canes or guide dogs must be given the right-of-way at all times; yield and allow them to cross safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct procedure for making a right turn?
options: a:Signal, slow down, and get into the lane closest to the centerline before turning.,b:Signal, slow down, and get into the lane closest to the right curb before turning.,c:Approach the corner in the lane nearest the right curb, but move over toward the middle of the street before turning.
note: Signal and slow, then move into and turn from the lane nearest the right curb or edge of the roadway, staying as close to the curb as practical.

question: When driving in fog, what lighting should you use?
options: a:Turn on your low beam headlights.,b:Turn on your hazard lights.,c:It is okay to drive at the maximum speed limit.
note: Use low-beam headlights in fog; high beams reflect and reduce visibility, and hazards require reduced speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When considering a pass on a two-lane road, what should you judge first?
options: a:The distance and speed of any oncoming vehicles.,b:Sounding your horn as you pass.,c:Flashing your headlights as you pass.
note: Before passing, ensure there is adequate space and time by judging the distance and speed of oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, which way should you turn the wheels?
options: a:Turn your front wheels slightly to the right.,b:Turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb.,c:Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
note: When parked uphill with a curb, turn the wheels sharply away from the curb so a roll would move the vehicle off the roadway.

question: Regulatory traffic signs are usually what color?
options: a:White,b:Blue,c:Green
note: Regulatory signs (which control traffic movement) are typically white with black markings and must be obeyed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to make a left turn from a two-way street, where should you position your vehicle?
options: a:Near the centerline before making the turn.,b:Near the right-hand side of the road.,c:On the left side of the centerline.
note: When turning left from a two-way street, start from the lane nearest the centerline and turn into the first legal lane of the road you are entering.

question: If a driver sees an animal on the roadway, what is the safest response?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution to avoid startling the animal.,b:Speed up to pass the animal quickly.,c:Try to swerve sharply around the animal at high speed.
note: Approach animals cautiously and slow down to avoid startling them or losing control; they may suddenly change direction or be followed by others.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is an important step to perform when preparing to turn?
options: a:Check traffic in all directions.,b:Always move to the left lane.,c:Increase your speed to clear the intersection.,d:Close your windows.
note: Check rear and side traffic, signal, and adjust speed before turning to ensure the maneuver is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left at an intersection, whom must you yield to?
options: a:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:You have the automatic right-of-way.,c:No one, if you begin the turn quickly.
note: When making a left turn, always yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians before completing the turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you and vehicles on your right and left arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who do you yield to?
options: a:Yield to the vehicle on your left.,b:Yield to the vehicle on your right.,c:Wait until there are no vehicles before proceeding.
note: When multiple vehicles arrive simultaneously at an uncontrolled intersection, yield to the vehicle on your right and proceed in order of arrival.

question: Which recommendation does NOT improve safe night driving?
options: a:Carrying a flashlight in your vehicle.,b:Keeping your windshield clean.,c:Tinting windows to reduce interior glare extensively.
note: Carrying a flashlight can be helpful, but it does not directly improve driving visibility at night; maintaining clean windshields and avoiding excessive tinting improve night driving safety.

question: What color are regulatory traffic signs most commonly?
options: a:White.,b:Green.,c:Yellow.
note: Regulatory signs (speed limits, parking, lane use, etc.) are usually white rectangles or squares with black, red, or green symbols or wording.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you turn onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow line down the center, what does that tell you about the road?
options: a:Traffic moves in both directions (a two-way road).,b:It is a one-way road.,c:The road is under repair.
note: Broken yellow centerlines separate opposing traffic, indicating a two-way road where passing is allowed when safe.

question: When must you use low beam headlights?
options: a:On a freeway.,b:On a lighted street.,c:When driving in fog.
note: Use low beams in fog, rain, snow, or mist because high beams create glare and reduce visibility.

question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what should you do first?
options: a:Ease off the gas and steer in the direction of the skid to regain control.,b:Brake as hard as possible.,c:Turn off the ignition immediately.
note: Do not slam the brakes; ease off the accelerator and steer into the skid until you regain control.

question: Which statement about work zones is true?
options: a:You should slow down for the Cone Zone and expect higher fines for violations.,b:Fines are always identical to normal traffic fines.,c:Slow down only if you think workers are present.
note: Drive carefully in work zones, slow for cone zones, and expect increased fines and risks to workers and road users.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is driving below the posted speed limit illegal?
options: a:When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic.,b:Only when driving in rural areas.,c:When in heavy traffic in a construction zone.
note: It is illegal to drive so slowly that you impede the normal and reasonable movement of traffic; you may be cited for driving too slowly.

question: What is the best action to take on slippery roads?
options: a:Slow down.,b:Drive more quickly.,c:Drive at the posted speed limit but with caution.
note: Reduce speed at the first sign of rain, snow, or sleet, because slippery conditions may require driving more slowly than the posted limit.

question: If you take a non-prescription drug, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Read the drug label for warnings about driving.,b:Drink alcohol to counteract drowsiness.,c:Drive as usual regardless of warnings.
note: Over-the-counter medications can impair driving. Read labels for warnings and consult a doctor or pharmacist if unsure about driving while on the medication.

question: What do double solid yellow centerlines mean?
options: a:No passing from either direction except to turn left or to pass certain slow users when safe.,b:Pedestrian crossing ahead.,c:Railroad crossing ahead.
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate passing is prohibited from both directions except in limited circumstances such as left turns when safe.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Avoid speeding on wet roads and keep tires properly inflated with good tread.,b:Drive faster to cut through water.,c:Use underinflated tires to increase surface contact.
note: Hydroplaning risk rises with speed and poor tire condition; maintain proper tire pressure and tread and slow down in wet conditions.

question: How should you prepare for hazards ahead on the road?
options: a:Continuously scan the road and roadsides for potential problems.,b:Stare straight ahead at all times.,c:Drive with your left foot on the brake.
note: Searching ahead, to the sides, and behind helps you detect and respond to hazards early.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How close is it illegal to park to a fire hydrant?
options: a:20 feet,b:15 feet,c:10 feet
note: It is illegal to park within 10 feet of a fire hydrant.

question: At a red light with a green arrow, when may you proceed in the arrow's direction?
options: a:You first come to a complete stop.,b:You wait until the light changes.,c:You are in the proper lane and the roadway is clear.
note: If you are in the lane corresponding to a green arrow and the way is clear, you may proceed in the arrow's direction even if other signals are red.

question: How should you drive through a construction zone?
options: a:Expect the unexpected and use extra caution.,b:Slightly increase your speed to clear it quickly.,c:Expect workers to yield to motorists.,d:Drive normally as if nothing changed.
note: Construction zones present unusual hazards; slow down, watch for workers, and follow signs and flaggers.

question: What is the only effective way to remove alcohol from your body?
options: a:Wait for time to pass.,b:Drink strong coffee.,c:Take a cold shower.
note: Only time removes alcohol from the bloodstream; coffee, exercise, or showers do not speed this process.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you plan to pass another vehicle, what assumption should you avoid?
options: a:Assuming the other driver will make space for you to return to your lane.,b:Assuming the other driver will maintain their speed.,c:Assuming the other driver will signal for you to pass.
note: Do not assume other drivers will yield room for you; ensure the lane is clear before passing and re-enter only when safe.

question: On rainy, snowy, or foggy days you should use headlights primarily to:
options: a:To keep your engine warm.,b:So others can see your vehicle.,c:To warn others of bad weather conditions.
note: Turn on your low-beam headlights when visibility is reduced so other drivers can see your vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road, what must you do to complete the pass legally and safely?
options: a:Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.,b:Move into the lane used by oncoming traffic to pass when it is safe and legal.,c:Use the road shoulder to pass.
note: To pass safely on a two-lane, two-way road you must move into the lane normally used by oncoming traffic and complete the pass only if it is legal and safe to do so.

question: Signs that warn drivers about hazardous conditions are called:
options: a:Warning signs.,b:Regulatory signs.,c:Information signs.
note: Warning signs alert drivers to potentially hazardous conditions ahead; ignoring them increases the risk of accidents.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which has priority if you must choose between obedience: a steady red light, a police officer's directions, or a stop sign?
options: a:Directions from a police officer.,b:A steady red light.,c:A stop sign.
note: Instructions from authorized traffic officers take precedence over signs, signals, and pavement markings.

question: When driving in work zones, what should you do?
options: a:Follow the driver in front of you closely.,b:Pass the driver in front of you as soon as you can.,c:Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance.
note: In work zones increase following distance, avoid tailgating, and watch for workers, equipment, and changed traffic patterns.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about speed is true?
options: a:Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.,b:Speeding is safe if you are an experienced driver.,c:Speeding is never dangerous.
note: Driving significantly slower than traffic can be hazardous; both excessive speed and driving too slowly increase crash risk.

question: A school bus stopped ahead of you in your lane has red lights flashing. What must you do?
options: a:Stop and remain stopped for as long as the red lights are flashing.,b:Slow to 25 mph and pass cautiously.,c:Proceed if you believe no children are nearby.
note: Approaching drivers must stop for a stopped school bus with flashing red lights until the lights stop and the stop arm is withdrawn.

question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means you should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop immediately.,c:Wait for a green light before proceeding.
note: A flashing yellow light signals caution; you should slow and proceed carefully without stopping unless required.

question: What does a flashing red traffic signal mean?
options: a:It means the same as a stop sign — come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.,b:The signal is broken and can be ignored.,c:You may slow but do not need to stop.
note: A flashing red light requires a full stop, yielding to traffic and pedestrians, then proceeding when safe.

question: At a railroad crossing with flashing signals, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and look for a train.,b:Stop no closer than 15 feet from the rail if signals warn of an approaching train.,c:Look for a train and then speed up if none is visible.
note: If warning devices are activated, stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail and wait until signals stop and gates are up.

question: What should you do before entering a curve?
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Activate your turn signal.,c:Brake hard as you enter the curve.
note: Slow down before you enter a curve. Adjust your speed for conditions and do not exceed the posted limit if it is unsafe for the curve or road conditions.

question: On slick roads, how should you make turns?
options: a:Take turns more slowly than usual.,b:Change lanes quickly before the turn.,c:Accelerate through the turn.,d:Brake sharply while turning.
note: Reduce speed before turns on slippery surfaces and execute turns slowly to avoid skidding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a yield sign, what must you do?
options: a:Must yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is close enough to cause conflict.,b:Should slow down but never stop.,c:Must yield to vehicles only on your right.
note: At a yield sign you must slow or stop if necessary and give right-of-way to traffic close enough to create conflict.

question: Which of the following is true concerning railroad crossings?
options: a:It is against the law to go around lowered gates at a crossing.,b:Not all railroad crossings are equipped with flashing red signals and gates.,c:You must stop at every railroad crossing regardless of signals.
note: You must never drive around or under lowered crossing gates; do stop when directed by flaggers or warning devices. (Note: not all crossings have active warnings.)

question: What does a yellow and black diamond-shaped sign generally indicate?
options: a:Warning of special conditions or hazards ahead.,b:Directions to cities and towns.,c:Regulatory traffic laws and regulations.
note: Diamond-shaped yellow/black signs warn drivers about upcoming road conditions or hazards.

question: How many alcoholic drinks does it take to affect your driving ability?
options: a:Three,b:Two,c:One
note: Even a single alcoholic drink can impair your ability to drive safely; do not drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

question: If you feel drowsy while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Pull over at the next rest area or service area to take a break.,b:Try to fight drowsiness while driving.,c:Take caffeine pills and continue driving.
note: If you become tired, stop at a safe place to rest or switch drivers; caffeine or pills are not substitutes for sleep.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer directs you to go through a red light intersection without stopping, what should you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop before proceeding.,b:Go through the intersection as directed by the officer.,c:Stop until the light turns green.
note: Traffic officers' instructions override traffic signals; follow the officer's directions even if the light is red.

question: When must you stop at an intersection?
options: a:When facing a flashing red light.,b:When facing a steady yellow light.,c:When seeing a yellow arrow.
note: A flashing red signal has the same meaning as a stop sign—come to a complete stop, look both ways, and proceed when clear.

question: What is the purpose of work zone barriers, drums, cones and signs?
options: a:To keep traffic out of hazardous work areas.,b:To inconvenience drivers.,c:To make drivers go faster.,d:To mark parking for workers.
note: Barriers and signs direct traffic away from hazards in work zones to protect workers and road users.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street onto a one-way street, you should begin the turn from:
options: a:The lane closest to the left curb.,b:Any lane as long as it's clear.,c:The lane in the center of the road.,d:The rightmost lane.
note: Begin left turns from the far left lane when turning from a one-way onto another one-way street.

question: If a pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Flash your lights.,b:Slow down.,c:Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
note: Slow down and be prepared to stop; always yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk and be especially careful where children are present.

question: A circular road sign typically warns drivers about what?
options: a:An upcoming railroad crossing.,b:A school zone.,c:A no-passing area.
note: Round signs indicate an approaching railroad crossing; approach with caution.

question: Which traffic signal instructs drivers to slow down and proceed with caution?
options: a:A flashing yellow light.,b:A flashing red light.,c:A solid yellow light.
note: A flashing yellow signal means slow down, proceed with caution, and be prepared to stop if necessary.

question: Which of these affect the impact of alcohol on a person?
options: a:The amount of food in the stomach,b:How much time passes between drinks,c:All of the above
note: Blood alcohol concentration depends on factors such as stomach contents, body weight, and how much time passes between drinks; all influence intoxication.

question: If the vehicle ahead is driven distractedly with one hand and talking, you should:
options: a:Give that vehicle extra space and be prepared for unexpected moves.,b:Follow their example and talk to your passenger.,c:Try to pass immediately.
note: Distracted drivers increase risk of collisions; allow extra distance and be alert for sudden actions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is unsafe or illegal on an interstate?
options: a:Changing lanes without signaling.,b:If you miss your exit, proceed to the next exit.,c:Slower traffic keeping to the right.
note: Always signal before changing lanes. If you miss an exit, continue to the next one; slower traffic should remain in the right lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver's left arm and hand extended upward signals what?
options: a:Intends to turn right.,b:Plans to turn left.,c:Intends to stop.
note: A left arm raised with hand up is the hand signal for a right turn.

question: If you park facing uphill on a street with a curb, how should you position the front wheels?
options: a:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,b:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,c:Leave the front wheels straight.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if the brakes fail.

question: Which statement about drugs and driving is true?
options: a:Even over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.,b:Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.,c:Any prescription drug is safe to use if you do not feel drowsy.
note: Prescription and over-the-counter medications can all impair driving ability; driving while impaired by any drug is illegal and dangerous.

question: How should a lap belt fit when correctly adjusted?
options: a:Is loose.,b:Is buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.,c:Is hidden beneath the seat.
note: A lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and the lower part of your abdomen; shoulder belts should lie across your chest.

question: At a railroad crossing, what should you be especially aware of?
options: a:That vehicles like school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials may be required to stop.,b:That crossings are always clear at night.,c:That you may drive faster than posted limits to clear the tracks.,d:That you need only look in one direction.
note: Approach railroad crossings with caution; be aware that some vehicles must always stop and that multiple trains can approach from either direction.

question: How far must you stay behind an active snowplow with its red or amber lights on (on roads posted 35 mph or more)?
options: a:At least 200 feet.,b:At least 300 feet.,c:At least 400 feet.
note: On roads with posted speeds of 35 mph or higher, drivers must remain at least 200 feet behind a working snowplow displaying red or amber lights.

question: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, what is the recommended action?
options: a:Try to get out of their way and avoid confrontation.,b:Stare at the driver as they pass.,c:Speed up to prevent them from passing.,d:Brake-check them to teach a lesson.
note: Move over when safe and avoid eye contact or gestures; remove yourself from the situation to reduce danger.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a crowded freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic and check mirrors and blind spots before merging.,b:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap.,c:Enter traffic without adjusting your speed because you have the right-of-way.
note: Use the entrance ramp to accelerate to freeway speed, check mirrors and blind spots, and yield to traffic already on the freeway before merging.

question: When parking facing uphill on a road without a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn them toward the edge of the road (to the right).,b:Turn them away from the edge of the road (to the left).,c:Keep the wheels straight ahead.
note: On an uphill without a curb, turn your wheels to the right so the vehicle would roll off the road rather than into traffic if brakes fail.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To avoid collisions with vehicles in your blind spots you should:
options: a:Turn your head and glance quickly over the shoulder in the direction of the move before changing lanes.,b:Adjust your mirrors every few minutes.,c:Honk your horn before changing lanes.
note: Before changing lanes, quickly look over your shoulder to ensure the blind spot is clear; do not rely solely on mirrors.

question: If the roadway ahead is filled with heavy smoke, what should you do?
options: a:Reduce speed, move as far right as possible, and stop off the roadway.,b:Turn on your high beams and continue carefully.,c:Turn on your four-way flashers and keep driving.
note: When smoke severely limits visibility, pull well off the road, stop, and wait until it is safe to continue; smoke can be hazardous to breathe.

question: If oncoming headlights blind you at night, what is the recommended action?
options: a:Glance toward the right edge of the road.,b:Switch your lights to high beams.,c:Turn your lights on and off rapidly.
note: If blinded by oncoming headlights, look toward the right edge of the road and use peripheral vision to maintain lane position until the vehicle passes.

question: Is it ever acceptable to drive around or under a lowering or raising railroad crossing gate?
options: a:If your vehicle can do so without damaging the gate.,b:Only if an approaching train is not too close.,c:No — never drive around or under a moving gate.
note: Do not drive around or under crossing gates while they are moving; flashing lights, bells, or lowered gates require you to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a double solid yellow centerline mean on a two-lane road?
options: a:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is not permitted for either direction.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is permitted when safe.,c:Lanes move in the same direction and passing is prohibited.
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate opposing traffic and that passing across the lines is prohibited.

question: If you encounter a deep puddle ahead, you should:
options: a:Avoid it if possible.,b:Maintain posted speed to get through.,c:Shift into neutral and continue.,d:Speed up to reduce splash.
note: To prevent loss of control and hydroplaning, avoid deep puddles or drive slowly and cautiously if you must cross.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How must you treat traffic signs and pavement markings?
options: a:They must always be obeyed.,b:They are only suggestions.,c:You may ignore them when traffic is light.,d:You must follow them only at night.
note: Signs, signals, and pavement markings legally control traffic and must be obeyed at all times.

question: When does your stopping distance increase?
options: a:On wet or icy roads.,b:On paved highways.,c:When driving at night only.
note: Stopping distances increase on slippery surfaces such as wet, icy, or loose gravel roads, and in other poor traction conditions.

question: When a traffic light turns yellow, what should drivers do?
options: a:Accelerate to avoid a red light.,b:Continue driving, as they have the right-of-way.,c:Slow to a stop, unless they are already within the intersection.
note: A steady yellow light warns the signal will soon be red; slow and prepare to stop unless you are already within the intersection.

question: When must you obey instructions from school crossing guards?
options: a:At all times.,b:Only during school hours.,c:Only if you see children present.
note: Drivers must always obey the directions of school crossing guards when they are performing their duties.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill on a street that has a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Keep the front wheel straight and set the parking brake.,b:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,c:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
note: On an uphill block with a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb so if the vehicle rolls it will roll away from traffic.

question: As you near the top of a hill, what should you do?
options: a:Prepare to stop if necessary and reduce speed.,b:Speed up slightly to crest the hill.,c:Maintain the exact same speed without scanning ahead.
note: Approach hilltops with caution and be ready to stop because you cannot see what is immediately beyond the crest.

question: An orange and red triangular emblem on the back of a vehicle indicates:
options: a:A slow-moving vehicle.,b:The vehicle has the right-of-way.,c:Shoulder work ahead.,d:A wide load.
note: Slow-moving vehicles (farm equipment, certain maintenance vehicles, animal-drawn carts) display an orange-and-red triangle on the rear.

question: If a traffic signal shows a green arrow and a red light, you may:
options: a:Only proceed in the direction indicated by the green arrow.,b:Drive straight ahead only.,c:Proceed in any direction you choose.,d:Wait for a steady green light before moving.
note: A green arrow with a red light allows movement only in the arrow's direction, and only if the intersection is clear.

question: Why should you avoid following other cars too closely?
options: a:You may not see the road between the cars.,b:You may not have time to stop if the vehicle in front of you slows or stops suddenly.,c:You may not see the vehicle's turn signals.
note: Following too closely reduces your reaction time and increases the likelihood of a rear-end collision if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly.

question: What does a broken yellow line alongside a solid yellow line mean?
options: a:Traffic next to the broken line may pass; traffic next to the solid line may not.,b:Both directions may pass.,c:Passing is prohibited from both directions.
note: A broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line means vehicles next to the broken line may cross to pass when safe; vehicles next to the solid line may not.

question: If an oncoming vehicle enters your lane toward you, what emergency actions should you take?
options: a:Blow your horn, steer right, and brake.,b:Blow your horn, steer left, and brake.,c:Blow your horn, steer right, and accelerate.
note: Honk to alert the other driver, steer right to avoid a head-on collision, and brake — slowing reduces impact if a crash occurs.

question: After stopping for a school bus unloading children, what should you do before moving on?
options: a:Watch for children walking along the side of the road and proceed cautiously.,b:Do not proceed until the children wave to you.,c:Accelerate quickly to get past the bus.
note: After a bus stops with its stop arm extended, watch carefully for children near the roadway and proceed only after it's safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a narrow road when meeting oncoming traffic, what should you provide?
options: a:Demand the other vehicle pull over.,b:Pull completely off the road and stop.,c:Allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road.
note: Both drivers must allow at least one-half of the main travel portion so vehicles can safely pass each other.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If stopped by a police officer, how should you behave?
options: a:Stay in your vehicle with hands visible on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach.,b:Unbuckle and roll down the window immediately.,c:Get out of the vehicle and meet the officer on the road.
note: Remain in your vehicle with hands visible and wait until the officer asks for documents or further action.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to turn left on red?
options: a:Only when you are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street after stopping.,b:When you are on a two-way street turning onto another two-way street.,c:Whenever no other traffic is present.,d:Only when a sign permits it without stopping.
note: After a full stop, left turns on red are allowed only from a one-way street onto another one-way street, unless signs prohibit it.

question: What does a solid yellow traffic arrow indicate when displayed steadily?
options: a:It has the same meaning as a circular yellow light — prepare to stop.,b:Drivers may turn in the direction indicated by the arrow.,c:It is never used as a traffic signal.
note: A solid yellow arrow warns that the protected turn is ending; treat it like a yellow light and prepare to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-lane, two-way street, what must be true before you attempt to pass another vehicle?
options: a:You must be able to clearly see the road ahead and complete the pass before meeting oncoming traffic.,b:You must be able to return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic only.,c:Your vehicle must be capable of the speed necessary to pass.
note: You can only pass when you can clearly see far enough ahead to complete the maneuver safely and return to your lane before encountering oncoming traffic.

question: When is highway pavement especially treacherous and slippery?
options: a:If it has been raining several hours.,b:If it has just begun to rain.,c:If it has been raining for one to two hours.
note: Road surfaces are most slippery when rain first begins because oil and dirt on the pavement mix with the water and form a greasy film.

question: What effect does alcohol have on driving ability?
options: a:It slows reflexes and reaction time.,b:It wakes you up.,c:It improves coordination.,d:It increases alertness.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that reduces brain activity, slowing reaction time and impairing judgment and coordination.

question: In what ways can alcohol affect you?
options: a:It slows reaction time, impairs thinking, and may create false confidence.,b:It improves judgment and reaction time.,c:It only affects balance.
note: Alcohol dulls judgment, slows reactions, impairs coordination and vision, and can produce a false sense of confidence.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is unlawful when passing another vehicle?
options: a:Passing in marked no-passing zones or over railroad crossings.,b:Passing only on the right when safe.,c:Passing when the vehicle ahead is turning left if a passing lane exists.
note: It is illegal to pass in marked no-passing zones and at railroad crossings; these areas are unsafe for passing maneuvers.

question: Which substances can impair your ability to drive?
options: a:Tranquilizers, marijuana, sedatives, cough syrups, and some cold medications.,b:Only illegal drugs.,c:Only alcohol.,d:Caffeine in coffee.
note: Many prescription, over-the-counter, and illegal drugs can impair driving ability; always know a medicine's effects before driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you pass another vehicle?
options: a:You are on a hill or curve.,b:You are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.,c:You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.
note: You may pass when the centerline next to your lane is a broken line and the maneuver can be completed safely; never pass on hills or curves with restricted visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a green light, what is required of you?
options: a:You must yield to pedestrians and other traffic in the intersection before turning.,b:Maintain your normal speed and complete the turn quickly.,c:Stop and wait for a flashing pedestrian signal before turning.
note: You may turn right on green unless prohibited, but you must yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic as required.

question: If stopped and an officer suspects you have been drinking, are you allowed to refuse a chemical BAC test in Wisconsin?
options: a:No — under Wisconsin's implied consent law you must comply.,b:Yes — you may refuse if you haven't been drinking.,c:Yes — you may refuse if you think you'll fail the test.
note: Wisconsin's implied consent law requires drivers to submit to chemical testing when requested by an officer; refusal can carry penalties.

question: How is a driver's license classified under the law?
options: a:Privilege, not a right.,b:Requirement.,c:Right, not a privilege.
note: A driver’s license is a privilege that must be earned and maintained; it is not an absolute right.

question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Four-way flashers only.
note: Use low beams in fog; high beams can reflect off fog and reduce visibility.

question: Which driving skills are impaired by alcohol or drugs?
options: a:Both alertness and coordination.,b:Only coordination.,c:Only alertness.,d:Only vision.
note: Alcohol and many drugs slow reaction time and impair coordination, alertness, and concentration needed for safe driving.

question: Before backing out of a driveway near children playing, what should you do?
options: a:Walk to the rear of the vehicle to be sure the way is clear.,b:Sound your horn to warn the children.,c:Rev the engine to alert them.
note: When children are nearby, get out and check behind the vehicle before backing to avoid striking a child or obstacle.

question: Why is it important to be especially alert for motorcycles?
options: a:They are more difficult to see than cars.,b:They rarely use headlights.,c:Motorcyclists are less skilled than other drivers.
note: Motorcycles are smaller and harder to see, easily hidden in blind spots, and their speed and distance can be harder to judge.

question: When passing a motorcycle, you must:
options: a:Have your vehicle entirely in the left lane before and during the pass.,b:Stay in the same lane and pass quickly.,c:Blow your horn to make the motorcycle move over.
note: Allow a full lane of space for a motorcycle when passing; never share the lane with a motorcycle.

question: Which of the following can impair a person's ability to drive?
options: a:Alcohol.,b:Any medication.,c:A lack of sleep.,d:All of the above
note: Driving ability can be impaired by alcohol, legal and illegal drugs, certain medications, and fatigue. Know how substances and lack of sleep affect you.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do regarding the brakes?
options: a:Brake lightly.,b:Brake abruptly.,c:Stay off the brakes.
note: If you start to skid, avoid braking — braking can worsen the skid; steer to regain control.

question: Which of the following does NOT occur after drinking alcohol?
options: a:Your reflexes and reaction time speed up.,b:Your judgment of speed and distance is distorted.,c:You become less alert.,d:You have reduced ability to recover from glare.
note: Alcohol slows reflexes and reaction time; it does not speed them up. Drinking impairs judgment, alertness, and vision.

question: What is the best steering and braking approach when driving in bad weather?
options: a:Brake and steer smoothly to maintain control.,b:Steer off the road immediately.,c:Drive in a low gear at all times.
note: In unfavorable weather, avoid sudden braking or steering inputs; smooth actions help preserve traction and control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who proceeds first?
options: a:The driver who arrives first.,b:The driver who arrives last.,c:The driver who sounds their horn first.
note: At a four-way stop, the first vehicle to stop should be the first to go. If two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

question: Which of the following describes a work zone?
options: a:Is marked with black and white signs.,b:May be moving or stationary.,c:Does not require a driver to slow down and pay extra attention.
note: Work zones are often stationary but can also be moving (for example, when striping lines or mowing). They are marked with orange signs and you should slow down and pay extra attention when driving through them.

question: If the rear of your vehicle begins to skid to the left, which steering action corrects it?
options: a:Turn the steering wheel to the left (steer into the skid).,b:Do not turn the steering wheel at all.,c:Turn the steering wheel to the right to correct the skid.
note: If the rear of the vehicle skids left, steer left (into the skid) while easing off the accelerator. Do not oversteer or brake suddenly unless you have ABS.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing and you do not see or hear a train, in which of these situations must you stop?
options: a:If a stop sign is posted.,b:If a crossing gate is lowered.,c:If the crossing lights are flashing.,d:Any of the above
note: You must stop when a crossing gate is lowered, lights are flashing, a stop sign is posted, a flagger signals stop, or a train is close enough to be a hazard.

question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?
options: a:When directed by a flagger or stop sign, or when flashing red signals and gates are operating.,b:Only when you see a train.,c:Only at crossings with no signs.,d:Only if you are in a large vehicle.
note: Stop when a flagger or stop sign directs you, and when flashing signals or gates indicate an approaching train.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive faster than:
options: a:A speed that is reasonable and prudent for existing conditions.,b:The maximum speed limit only.,c:A speed that feels comfortable to you.
note: You must drive at a speed that is reasonable and prudent given traffic, weather, road conditions, and visibility — not faster than is safe.

question: If a vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you, what should be your first reaction?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas to create space.,b:Honk and brake hard.,c:Swerve into the next lane immediately.
note: If another vehicle merges too closely, lift your foot off the accelerator to increase the distance between you and the other vehicle without making sudden maneuvers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering an interstate on a short ramp with no acceleration lane, what should you do?
options: a:Immediately enter the far-right traffic lane and speed up to match traffic.,b:Use the shoulder of the main road to get up to the speed of traffic.,c:Speed up and enter the interstate only after you have identified a gap in traffic.
note: On a short ramp without an acceleration lane, wait and accelerate only when a sufficient gap allows you to merge safely into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a multilane highway, what should you do first?
options: a:Be sure the passing lane is clear.,b:Always pass only on the right.,c:Ignore turn signals from other vehicles.
note: Before passing, confirm the lane you intend to use is clear and signal your lane change.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your vehicle's turn signals stop working, what should you use to show a turn?
options: a:Hand signals.,b:Your horn.,c:Your headlights.
note: If turn signals fail, use standard hand signals to indicate turns or lane changes so other road users understand your intentions.

question: How should you respond to a flashing red traffic signal at an intersection?
options: a:Slow down and yield the right-of-way.,b:Come to a complete stop, yield, and go when safe.,c:Slow down and proceed without stopping.
note: A flashing red light has the same meaning as a stop sign: stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go when safe.

question: If a fire engine is following you but not using its emergency signals, what should you do?
options: a:Continue driving in a normal manner.,b:Stop as quickly as you can.,c:Speed up to clear the way.
note: If an emergency vehicle behind you is not using lights or siren, you do not need to immediately clear the lane; continue normally.

question: When a bicyclist is making a left turn, what should you expect?
options: a:They may use the left lane.,b:They may cut through all lanes.,c:They may wait on the side of the road.
note: Bicyclists may use the left lane to make a left turn just like motor vehicles; be prepared for that movement.

question: If you feel fatigued while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.,b:Open all windows and drive faster.,c:Increase radio volume and keep driving.,d:Keep driving but reduce speed.
note: Signs of fatigue include drifting lanes and struggling to keep eyes open; stop in a safe area and rest rather than continuing to drive.

question: How should you drive through a construction zone to avoid causing congestion by slowing to look?
options: a:Pass the construction area carefully and avoid “rubbernecking.”,b:Stop to watch the workers.,c:Decrease your following distance to get through faster.
note: Do not slow down to stare at incidents or workers. Maintain attention to the road and pass the work zone carefully to avoid creating additional congestion or hazards.

question: If you are involved in an accident, what should you do at or near the scene?
options: a:Stop your vehicle at or near the scene and avoid standing in traffic lanes.,b:Leave the scene if damage seems minor.,c:Keep the ignition on for wrecked vehicles.
note: Stop at or near the collision scene, move vehicles out of traffic if possible, avoid standing in traffic lanes, and turn off ignitions of wrecked vehicles.

question: When parking uphill next to a curb, what should you do after setting the parking brake?
options: a:Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.,b:Keep the front tires straight ahead.,c:Keep the rear tires against the curb.
note: On an uphill with a curb, turn wheels away from the curb so if the vehicle rolls it will roll into the curb and stop.

question: If dust or smoke reduces your ability to see other vehicles, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and turn on your headlights.,b:Turn on your parking lights only.,c:Turn on your emergency flashers but keep driving at the same speed.
note: When visibility is reduced, slow down and turn on headlights so other drivers can see you; do not rely on parking lights alone.

question: Why is night driving generally more difficult than daytime driving?
options: a:Visibility is reduced in the dark.,b:Cars are more likely to overheat.,c:It is always raining at night.,d:Headlights improve peripheral vision at night.
note: At night your field of vision is reduced; use appropriate headlights and drive at a speed that lets you stop within the visible distance ahead.

question: On a multilane road, what does a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line indicate?
options: a:Passing is permitted only from the direction next to the dashed line.,b:Passing is permitted from both directions.,c:Passing is prohibited from both directions.
note: Where a dashed yellow line is next to a solid one, only traffic next to the dashed line may pass; the side next to the solid line may not.

question: At an intersection with a flashing red light, how should you proceed?
options: a:Come to a full stop and go when it is safe.,b:Stop only if other cars are approaching.,c:Stop only if vehicles are already in the intersection.
note: Treat a flashing red light like a stop sign: stop, yield, and proceed when safe.

question: A solid white line between lanes moving in the same direction means:
options: a:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.
note: Solid white lines discourage or prohibit lane changes; they indicate lane discipline for traffic moving in the same direction.

question: When may you legally cross double solid yellow lines?
options: a:To pass another car.,b:To turn into a driveway or make a permitted left turn.,c:To pass a slow-moving truck.
note: You may not cross double solid lines except to make a left turn into or out of a driveway, to make a permitted U-turn, or to enter/exit the roadway.
